knowledge_statements.title: Homogeneous Quadratic Liftings
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Degree-two homogeneous lifting into the symmetric positive-semidefinite cone.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(n\geq1\), \(m\geq0\), and \(Q_0,\ldots,Q_m\in\mathbb S^n\), and define \(q_i(x)=x^{\mathsf T}Q_i x\) for \(x\in\mathbb R^n\). The quadratic lifting maps \(x\) to \(X=xx^{\mathsf T}\in\mathbb S_+^n\), for which \(q_i(x)=\langle Q_i,X\rangle\). Its exact lifted image is \(\{X\in\mathbb S_+^n:\operatorname{rank}X\leq1\}\); its nonzero elements have rank one, while \(X=0\) corresponds to \(x=0\). Thus every objective or constraint expressed through the \(q_i\) becomes linear in \(X\), while exactness is retained by the rank-at-most-one condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A homogeneous quadratic becomes linear after lifting x x-transpose to a positive-semidefinite matrix. Exact nonzero lifts have rank one, and the zero lift has rank zero.
assumptions_latex: \(n\geq1\), \(m\geq0\), and \(Q_i\in\mathbb S^n\) for \(i=0,\ldots,m\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(q_i(x)=\langle Q_i,xx^{\mathsf T}\rangle\) and \(\{xx^{\mathsf T}:x\in\mathbb R^n\}=\{X\succeq0:\operatorname{rank}X\leq1\}\).

children.title: Affine Quadratic Liftings
children.top_down_role: Lifted representations retaining affine terms and constant coordinates.

knowledge_statements.title: Affine Quadratic Liftings
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Lift of an inhomogeneous quadratic using first- and second-order variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(q(x)=x^{\mathsf T}Qx+2c^{\mathsf T}x+d\) on \(\mathbb R^n\), introduce \(X=xx^{\mathsf T}\) and the augmented matrix \(Y=\begin{pmatrix}1&x^{\mathsf T}\\x&X\end{pmatrix}\). With \(M(q)=\begin{pmatrix}d&c^{\mathsf T}\\c&Q\end{pmatrix}\), one has \(q(x)=\langle M(q),Y\rangle\). The exact affine lifting consists of matrices \(Y\succeq0\) satisfying \(Y_{00}=1\) and \(\operatorname{rank}Y=1\); equivalently, \(X=xx^{\mathsf T}\). Affine quadratic objectives and constraints therefore become linear functionals of \(Y\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An affine quadratic is linearized by an augmented moment matrix whose top-left entry is one and whose exact image has rank one.
assumptions_latex: \(Q\in\mathbb S^n\), \(c\in\mathbb R^n\), and \(d\in\mathbb R\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(q(x)=\langle M(q),Y\rangle\), with exactness characterized by \(Y\succeq0\), \(Y_{00}=1\), and \(\operatorname{rank}Y=1\).

children.title: Homogenized Quadratic Liftings
children.top_down_role: Homogeneous lifted representations obtained through an auxiliary scaling coordinate.

knowledge_statements.title: Homogenized Quadratic Liftings
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Homogenization of affine quadratics by one additional scalar coordinate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(q(x)=x^{\mathsf T}Qx+2c^{\mathsf T}x+d\) on \(\mathbb R^n\), define \(M(q)=\begin{pmatrix}d&c^{\mathsf T}\\c&Q\end{pmatrix}\), introduce \(z=(t,x)\in\mathbb R^{n+1}\), and set \(q^h(t,x)=x^{\mathsf T}Qx+2t c^{\mathsf T}x+d t^2=z^{\mathsf T}M(q)z\). Its matrix lifting is \(Z=zz^{\mathsf T}\succeq0\), so \(q^h(t,x)=\langle M(q),Z\rangle\). The affine chart is imposed by \(t=1\), equivalently by \(Z_{00}=1\) for rank-one \(Z\). On this chart, \(q^h(1,x)=q(x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Adding a homogenizing coordinate converts an affine quadratic into a homogeneous quadratic and recovers the original expression on the chart t=1.
assumptions_latex: \(Q\in\mathbb S^n\), \(c\in\mathbb R^n\), and \(d\in\mathbb R\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(q^h(t,x)=\langle M(q),zz^{\mathsf T}\rangle\) and \(q^h(1,x)=q(x)\).

notation.meaning: augmented symmetric coefficient matrix of q

children.title: Affine-to-Homogeneous Correspondence
children.top_down_role: Structural correspondence between affine models and their homogenized counterparts.

knowledge_statements.title: Affine-to-Homogeneous Correspondence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact correspondence between affine lifts and normalized homogeneous rank-one lifts.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Map \(x\in\mathbb R^n\) to \(z=(1,x)\) and \(Y=zz^{\mathsf T}\). This gives a bijection between pairs \((x,X)\) satisfying \(X=xx^{\mathsf T}\) and matrices \(Y\in\mathbb S_+^{n+1}\) satisfying \(Y_{00}=1\) and \(\operatorname{rank}Y=1\), through \(Y=\begin{pmatrix}1&x^{\mathsf T}\\x&X\end{pmatrix}\). Conversely, the first column of any such \(Y\) uniquely recovers \((1,x)\). For \(q(x)=x^{\mathsf T}Qx+2c^{\mathsf T}x+d\) and \(M(q)=\begin{pmatrix}d&c^{\mathsf T}\\c&Q\end{pmatrix}\), this correspondence gives \(q(x)=\langle M(q),Y\rangle\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Normalization of the homogenizing coordinate establishes a bijection between affine quadratic lifts and normalized homogeneous rank-one positive-semidefinite matrices.
assumptions_latex: \(Y\in\mathbb S^{n+1}\) is indexed by the homogenizing coordinate followed by the coordinates of \(x\).
\(Q\in\mathbb S^n\), \(c\in\mathbb R^n\), and \(d\in\mathbb R\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((x,xx^{\mathsf T})\longleftrightarrow \begin{pmatrix}1&x^{\mathsf T}\\x&xx^{\mathsf T}\end{pmatrix}\) is bijective, and \(q(x)=\langle M(q),Y\rangle\).

notation.meaning: entry associated with the squared homogenizing coordinate
augmented symmetric coefficient matrix of q

knowledge_statements.title: Quadratically Constrained Quadratic Liftings
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Rank-constrained semidefinite representation of an affine QCQP.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(i=0,\ldots,m\), let \(q_i(x)=x^{\mathsf T}Q_i x+2c_i^{\mathsf T}x+d_i\) on \(\mathbb R^n\), and define \(M_i=\begin{pmatrix}d_i&c_i^{\mathsf T}\\c_i&Q_i\end{pmatrix}\). The QCQP value \(p^*=\inf\{q_0(x):x\in\mathbb R^n,\ q_i(x)\leq0,\ i=1,\ldots,m\}\) is equivalently represented by \(p^*=\inf_Y\langle M_0,Y\rangle\) subject to \(\langle M_i,Y\rangle\leq0\) for \(i=1,\ldots,m\), \(Y\succeq0\), \(Y_{00}=1\), and \(\operatorname{rank}Y=1\). Omitting only the rank constraint yields the standard Shor semidefinite relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An affine QCQP is exactly representable as a normalized rank-one semidefinite program; deleting the rank constraint produces its standard Shor relaxation.
assumptions_latex: \(Q_i\in\mathbb S^n\), \(c_i\in\mathbb R^n\), and \(d_i\in\mathbb R\) for \(i=0,\ldots,m\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(p^*=\inf\{\langle M_0,Y\rangle:\langle M_i,Y\rangle\leq0,\ Y\succeq0,\ Y_{00}=1,\operatorname{rank}Y=1\}\).

notation.meaning: augmented coefficient matrix of the i-th quadratic

knowledge_statements.title: Rank-Relaxation Interface
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Value and recovery consequences of deleting the rank-one constraint.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(p^*\) be the minimum of a lifted minimization QCQP with the constraint \(\operatorname{rank}Y=1\), and let \(p_{\mathrm{sdp}}\) be the value after deleting that constraint while retaining all linear constraints, \(Y\succeq0\), and \(Y_{00}=1\). Then every exact lifted feasible point is SDP-feasible, hence \(p_{\mathrm{sdp}}\leq p^*\). If the SDP has an optimal solution \(Y^*\) of rank one, then \(Y^*=(1,x^*)(1,x^*)^{\mathsf T}\) for a feasible \(x^*\), and \(p_{\mathrm{sdp}}=p^*\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dropping rank one gives a lower bound for minimization; a rank-one SDP optimizer certifies exactness and recovers a QCQP optimizer.
assumptions_latex: The lifted QCQP and its SDP relaxation are feasible and attain the values being compared.
The normalization constraint is \(Y_{00}=1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(p_{\mathrm{sdp}}\leq p^*\); if \(\operatorname{rank}Y^*=1\), then \(p_{\mathrm{sdp}}=p^*\) and \(x^*=Y^*_{1:n,0}\) is optimal.

children.title: Shor Relaxation Core
children.top_down_role: Canonical Shor lifting, its modeling role, and its relation to rank relaxation.

knowledge_statements.title: Shor Relaxation Core
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical SDP obtained from the augmented quadratic lifting.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(i=0,\ldots,m\), let \(q_i(x)=x^{\mathsf T}Q_i x+2c_i^{\mathsf T}x+d_i\) on \(\mathbb R^n\), define \(M_i=\begin{pmatrix}d_i&c_i^{\mathsf T}\\c_i&Q_i\end{pmatrix}\), and let \(p^*=\inf\{q_0(x):x\in\mathbb R^n,\ q_i(x)\leq0,\ i=1,\ldots,m\}\). The Shor relaxation is \(p_{\mathrm{Shor}}=\inf_Y\langle M_0,Y\rangle\) subject to \(\langle M_i,Y\rangle\leq0\) for \(i=1,\ldots,m\), \(Y_{00}=1\), and \(Y\succeq0\). Equivalently, writing \(Y=\begin{pmatrix}1&x^{\mathsf T}\\x&X\end{pmatrix}\), its conic constraint is \(X-xx^{\mathsf T}\succeq0\). The relaxation retains the lifted linear inequalities but does not impose \(X=xx^{\mathsf T}\), and its value satisfies \(p_{\mathrm{Shor}}\leq p^*\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The Shor relaxation keeps the lifted linear constraints and positive semidefiniteness while discarding the nonconvex rank-one identity, thereby giving a lower bound for minimization.
assumptions_latex: \(Q_i\in\mathbb S^n\), \(c_i\in\mathbb R^n\), and \(d_i\in\mathbb R\) for \(i=0,\ldots,m\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(p_{\mathrm{Shor}}=\inf\{\langle M_0,Y\rangle:\langle M_i,Y\rangle\leq0,\ Y_{00}=1,\ Y\succeq0\}\leq p^*\).

notation.meaning: augmented coefficient matrix of the i-th quadratic

children.title: General Quadratic Lifting Extensions
children.top_down_role: Quadratic lifting constructions extending beyond the canonical Shor setting.

knowledge_statements.title: General Quadratic Lifting Extensions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Systematic strengthening by additional valid lifted quadratic relations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be described by quadratic constraints, and let \(Y(x)=(1,x)(1,x)^{\mathsf T}\). Any affine functional \(L(Y)\) satisfying \(L(Y(x))\leq0\) for every \(x\in F\) is a valid lifted inequality. Adding any family of such inequalities to the Shor relaxation preserves every exactly lifted feasible point and therefore preserves validity of its minimization lower bound. Products or combinations of original constraints may generate these relations when their signs make the resulting quadratic or higher-order moment inequality valid; higher-degree relations require correspondingly larger moment matrices.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Valid relations satisfied by every exact lift may strengthen Shor’s relaxation without excluding original feasible points; higher-degree relations require larger moment lifts.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is the original feasible set and \(Y(x)=(1,x)(1,x)^{\mathsf T}\).
Every added relation is valid for all \(x\in F\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\{Y(x):x\in F\}\subseteq\{Y\in\mathcal S_{\mathrm{Shor}}:L(Y)\leq0\}\subseteq\mathcal S_{\mathrm{Shor}}\).

notation.meaning: feasible region of the Shor relaxation
affine functional defining a valid lifted inequality

knowledge_statements.title: Lagrangian-Dual Quadratic Bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Weak Lagrangian dual bound for a quadratically constrained minimization problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(p^*=\inf\{q_0(x):x\in\mathbb R^n,\ q_i(x)\leq0,\ i=1,\ldots,m\}\), define \(L(x,\lambda)=q_0(x)+\sum_{i=1}^m\lambda_iq_i(x)\) for \(\lambda\in\mathbb R_+^m\), and \(g(\lambda)=\inf_{x\in\mathbb R^n}L(x,\lambda)\). The Lagrangian-dual value is \(d^*=\sup_{\lambda\geq0}g(\lambda)\). For every \(\lambda\geq0\), \(g(\lambda)\leq p^*\), hence \(d^*\leq p^*\). For any \(\gamma\in\mathbb R\), the inequality \(g(\lambda)\geq\gamma\) holds exactly when \(L(x,\lambda)-\gamma\geq0\) for all \(x\in\mathbb R^n\), equivalently when the augmented coefficient matrix of the quadratic \(L(\cdot,\lambda)-\gamma\) is positive semidefinite.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nonnegative multipliers combine quadratic constraints into globally valid lower bounds. A proposed bound gamma is certified by positive semidefiniteness of the augmented matrix of the shifted Lagrangian, and maximizing such bounds gives the Lagrangian dual value.
assumptions_latex: \(q_0,\ldots,q_m\) are real-valued quadratic functions on \(\mathbb R^n\).
The primal problem is a minimization problem with constraints \(q_i(x)\leq0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(d^*=\sup_{\lambda\geq0}\inf_{x\in\mathbb R^n}\bigl(q_0(x)+\sum_{i=1}^m\lambda_iq_i(x)\bigr)\leq p^*\).

knowledge_statements.title: Single-Quadratic-Constraint Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Strong Lagrangian duality derived from the inequality S-lemma.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f,g:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) be quadratic functions, and suppose there exists \(\bar x\) with \(g(\bar x)<0\). If \(p^*=\inf\{f(x):g(x)\leq0\}\) is finite, then \[p^*=\sup_{\lambda\geq0}\inf_{x\in\mathbb R^n}\bigl(f(x)+\lambda g(x)\bigr).\] Equivalently, for every \(\gamma<p^*\) there exists \(\lambda\geq0\) such that \(f(x)-\gamma+\lambda g(x)\geq0\) for all \(x\in\mathbb R^n\). Thus the one-constraint quadratic Lagrangian bound has no duality gap under strict feasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With one quadratic inequality and a strictly feasible point, the best quadratic Lagrangian lower bound equals the primal infimum.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) and \(g\) are quadratic on \(\mathbb R^n\).
There exists \(\bar x\in\mathbb R^n\) such that \(g(\bar x)<0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(p^*=\sup_{\lambda\geq0}\inf_x(f(x)+\lambda g(x))\).

notation.meaning: infimum of f over the single quadratic inequality

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The theorem is a standard single-inequality S-lemma duality consequence and its hypotheses and conclusion appear mathematically appropriate, but no source or inspectable locator is supplied for this nontrivial exactness theorem.

children.title: Inhomogeneous S-Lemma Variants
children.top_down_role: S-lemma regimes involving affine or constant quadratic terms.

knowledge_statements.title: Inhomogeneous S-Lemma Variants
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Standard inhomogeneous inequality S-lemma with a strict-feasibility hypothesis.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f(x)=x^{\mathsf T}Ax+2a^{\mathsf T}x+\alpha\) and \(g(x)=x^{\mathsf T}Bx+2b^{\mathsf T}x+\beta\) on \(\mathbb R^n\). Assume that \(g(\bar x)<0\) for some \(\bar x\). Then \(g(x)\leq0\Rightarrow f(x)\geq0\) for every \(x\in\mathbb R^n\) if and only if there exists \(\lambda\geq0\) such that \(f(x)+\lambda g(x)\geq0\) for every \(x\in\mathbb R^n\). Equivalently, the augmented coefficient matrix of \(f+\lambda g\) is positive semidefinite.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under strict feasibility, an inhomogeneous quadratic is nonnegative on one quadratic sublevel set exactly when a nonnegative S-lemma multiplier exists.
assumptions_latex: \(A,B\in\mathbb S^n\), \(a,b\in\mathbb R^n\), and \(\alpha,\beta\in\mathbb R\).
There exists \(\bar x\) with \(g(\bar x)<0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \([g\leq0\Rightarrow f\geq0]\iff\exists\lambda\geq0\ \forall x,\ f(x)+\lambda g(x)\geq0\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The stated inhomogeneous inequality S-lemma, including the strict-feasibility hypothesis and multiplier sign, is standard and internally consistent, but the theorem has no cited source or locator.

children.title: Equality-Constrained S-Lemma Variants
children.top_down_role: S-lemma regimes governed by quadratic equality constraints.

knowledge_statements.title: Equality-Constrained S-Lemma Variants
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Globally verifiable multiplier certificate for a quadratic equality implication.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f,g:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) be quadratic functions. A scalar \(\lambda\in\mathbb R\) satisfying \(f(x)+\lambda g(x)\geq0\) for every \(x\in\mathbb R^n\) is an equality S-procedure certificate for \(g(x)=0\Rightarrow f(x)\geq0\). Global nonnegativity is verifiable by positive semidefiniteness of the augmented coefficient matrix of \(f+\lambda g\). Unlike the strict-inequality S-lemma, necessity of such a free-sign multiplier is not unconditional; equality variants require additional regularity and exclude exceptional degenerate quadratic configurations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A free-sign multiplier producing a globally nonnegative quadratic certifies nonnegativity on a quadratic equality, but converse exactness needs extra hypotheses.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) and \(g\) are quadratic functions on \(\mathbb R^n\).
\(\lambda\in\mathbb R\) is unrestricted in sign.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\forall x,\ f(x)+\lambda g(x)\geq0\Longrightarrow[g(x)=0\Rightarrow f(x)\geq0]\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The displayed free-sign multiplier condition is a valid sufficient certificate and the certificate kind is appropriate. However, the claims about converse regularity and exceptional degenerate configurations are nontrivial, are not enumerated precisely, and have no authoritative source or locator.

children.title: Inhomogeneity–Equality Equivalence Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Conditions separating transferable formulations from nonequivalent variants.

assumptions_latex: \(f,g:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) are quadratic polynomials.
\(F,G:\mathbb R^{n+1}\to\mathbb R\) are their degree-two homogenizations, so \(F(x,1)=f(x)\) and \(G(x,1)=g(x)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(g(x)=0\Rightarrow f(x)\ge 0\) is equivalent to \(G(x,t)=0\Rightarrow F(x,t)\ge 0\) on the chart \(t\ne0\). It extends to all homogeneous feasible points exactly when \(F(x,0)\ge0\) for every \(x\) satisfying \(G(x,0)=0\). Thus points at infinity, \(t=0\), are precisely the boundary at which homogenizing an inhomogeneous equality implication can strengthen it and invalidate an otherwise equivalent S-lemma formulation.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Homogenization boundary for equality-form quadratic implications; multiplier exactness itself requires additional regularity assumptions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f(x)=x^{\mathsf T}Ax+2a^{\mathsf T}x+a_0\) and \(g(x)=x^{\mathsf T}Bx+2b^{\mathsf T}x+b_0\), with homogenizations \(F(x,t)=x^{\mathsf T}Ax+2t a^{\mathsf T}x+a_0t^2\) and \(G(x,t)=x^{\mathsf T}Bx+2t b^{\mathsf T}x+b_0t^2\). Then \(g(x)=0\Rightarrow f(x)\ge0\) is equivalent, by scaling, to \(G(x,t)=0\Rightarrow F(x,t)\ge0\) for \(t\ne0\). The implication over all \((x,t)\ne0\) is equivalent to the inhomogeneous implication if and only if \(G(x,0)=0\Rightarrow F(x,0)\ge0\). Hence feasible directions at \(t=0\) delimit the inhomogeneity-equality correspondence.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Homogenization preserves an equality-constrained quadratic implication on the affine chart. Full homogeneous equivalence additionally requires nonnegativity at every feasible point at infinity.
knowledge_statements.title: Inhomogeneity–Equality Equivalence Boundaries

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The affine-chart scaling claim is coherent and fits the failure-boundary container, but the exact points-at-infinity equivalence has no cited evidence.

assumptions_latex: Quadratic constraints are written as \(g_i(x)\ge0\).
A scalar S-procedure certificate uses multipliers \(\lambda_i\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The implication \(g_1(x,y)\ge0,\ g_2(x,y)\ge0\Rightarrow f(x,y)\ge0\) holds with strict feasibility, but no \(\lambda_1,\lambda_2e0f\ge0\) makes \(f-\lambda_1g_1-\lambda_2g_2\) globally nonnegative. Therefore the lossless scalar-multiplier S-lemma does not extend to two arbitrary quadratic constraints.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Concrete failure of the scalar-multiplier S-procedure with two constraints, despite strict feasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: On \(\mathbb R^2\), set \(g_1(x,y)=x\), \(g_2(x,y)=y\), and \(f(x,y)=xy\). The system has a strict feasible point, for example \((1,1)\), and \(g_1\ge0,\ g_2\ge0\) implies \(f\ge0\). Nevertheless, for every \(\lambda_1,\lambda_2\ge0\), the polynomial \(f-\lambda_1g_1-\lambda_2g_2=xy-\lambda_1x-\lambda_2y\) is not globally nonnegative: its quadratic part has the indefinite matrix \(\left(\begin{smallmatrix}0&1/2\\1/2&0\end{smallmatrix}\right)\). Thus no scalar S-procedure certificate exists, establishing a multiple-constraint failure boundary.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Two strictly feasible constraints can imply a quadratic inequality without admitting nonnegative scalar S-procedure multipliers; the quadrant implication for xy is a concrete example.
knowledge_statements.title: Multiple-Constraint Failure Boundary

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The counterexample fits the multiple-constraint failure container and is mathematically plausible, but no source is supplied and conclusion_latex contains the corruption \(\lambda_2e0f\ge0\).

knowledge_statements.title: Sign-Variable Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Homogeneous matrix lifting of unconstrained sign-variable quadratic optimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(Q\in\mathbb S^n\) and \(c\in\mathbb R^n\), the sign-variable problem \(\min\{x^{\mathsf T}Qx+2c^{\mathsf T}x:x\in\{-1,1\}^n\}\) has the exact lifted formulation \(\min\{\langle Q,X\rangle+2c^{\mathsf T}x:\operatorname{diag}(X)=\mathbf1,\ X=xx^{\mathsf T}\}\). Equivalently, one may impose \(\left(\begin{smallmatrix}X&x\\x^{\mathsf T}&1\end{smallmatrix}\right)\succeq0\) together with rank one. Removing the rank condition gives the standard semidefinite relaxation; in the homogeneous case \(c=0\), it is optimization over the elliptope \(\{X\succeq0:\operatorname{diag}(X)=\mathbf1\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Sign constraints become unit diagonal conditions after matrix lifting. Removing the rank-one identity produces the standard elliptope semidefinite relaxation.
assumptions_latex: \(Q\in\mathbb S^n\) and \(c\in\mathbb R^n\).
Sign variables satisfy \(x_i\in\{-1,1\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every feasible sign vector gives \(X=xx^{\mathsf T}\), \(X\succeq0\), and \(\operatorname{diag}(X)=\mathbf1\); dropping \(\operatorname{rank}(X)=1\) yields the elliptope SDP relaxation.

knowledge_statements.title: Zero-One Variable Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: First-order moment lifting for purely zero-one quadratic models.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(Q\in\mathbb S^n\) and \(c\in\mathbb R^n\), the zero-one quadratic model \(\min\{x^{\mathsf T}Qx+c^{\mathsf T}x:x\in\{0,1\}^n\}\) is represented exactly by \(X=xx^{\mathsf T}\) and \(X_{ii}=x_i\) for all \(i\). Its standard SDP relaxation is \(\min\{\langle Q,X\rangle+c^{\mathsf T}x:\operatorname{diag}(X)=x,\ \left(\begin{smallmatrix}1&x^{\mathsf T}\\x&X\end{smallmatrix}\right)\succeq0\}\). The affine transformation \(s=2x-\mathbf1\) gives an equivalent sign-variable formulation before relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Zero-one products are lifted into a matrix whose diagonal equals the binary vector. Dropping rank one gives the standard moment-matrix SDP relaxation.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The identities \(X=xx^{\mathsf T}\) and \(X_{ii}=x_i\) exactly encode binary products; dropping rank one while retaining the moment PSD constraint gives the standard zero-one SDP relaxation.

knowledge_statements.title: Reformulation–Linearization Strengthening
knowledge_statements.scope_note: First-level RLT inequalities generated from pairs of unit-box bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(0\le x_i,x_j\le1\), multiply the nonnegative bound factors \(x_i\), \(1-x_i\), \(x_j\), and \(1-x_j\) pairwise and replace \(x_ix_j\) by \(X_{ij}\). This yields \(X_{ij}\ge0\), \(X_{ij}\le x_i\), \(X_{ij}\le x_j\), and \(X_{ij}\ge x_i+x_j-1\). Together with \(X_{ii}=x_i\), these inequalities are valid for every zero-one lift \(X=xx^{\mathsf T}\). Intersecting an SDP relaxation with all such inequalities cannot remove an integer-feasible lift and can only improve or leave unchanged its objective bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Linearizing products of pairs of box bounds yields the four McCormick–RLT inequalities, which preserve binary lifts and can only tighten or leave unchanged the SDP relaxation.
assumptions_latex: \(0\le x_i\le1\) for every binary-relaxed variable.
\(X_{ij}\) represents the product \(x_ix_j\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Adding the displayed RLT inequalities preserves every binary feasible lift and can only tighten or leave unchanged the relaxation.

knowledge_statements.title: Valid-Inequality Strengthening
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic monotonic strengthening principle for lifted binary quadratic relaxations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S\) be the exact lifted feasible set and let \(R\supseteq S\) be a convex relaxation. If \(a_k^{\mathsf T}u\le\beta_k\) holds for every \(u\in S\), then \(R'=R\cap\bigcap_k\{u:a_k^{\mathsf T}u\le\beta_k\}\) still contains \(S\). For minimization, \(\inf_{u\in R}c^{\mathsf T}u\le\inf_{u\in R'}c^{\mathsf T}u\le\inf_{u\in S}c^{\mathsf T}u\); for maximization the inequalities reverse. Thus valid inequalities monotonically improve, or leave unchanged, the relaxation bound without excluding any discrete feasible solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Intersecting a relaxation with inequalities valid for every exact lifted point preserves feasibility and can only improve or leave unchanged the relaxation bound.
assumptions_latex: \(S\) contains every exact lifted feasible point of the discrete quadratic model.
Each inequality \(a_k^{\mathsf T}u\le\beta_k\) is valid on \(S\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Intersecting a relaxation \(R\supseteq S\) with valid halfspaces leaves all exact feasible lifts and produces a relaxation no weaker than \(R\).

knowledge_statements.title: Metric-Inequality Strengthening
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cycle-form metric inequalities in cut-distance coordinates for sign-variable SDP relaxations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a sign vector \(x\in\{-1,1\}^n\), let \(X=xx^{\mathsf T}\) and \(d_{ij}=(1-X_{ij})/2\). Then \(d_{ij}\in\{0,1\}\) indicates whether signs \(i\) and \(j\) differ. For every simple cycle \(C\) and every odd-cardinality subset \(F\subseteq E(C)\), the cut metric satisfies \(\sum_{e\in F}d_e-\sum_{e\in E(C)\setminus F}d_e\le|F|-1\). These linear inequalities are valid for all rank-one sign lifts. Adding them to \(X\succeq0\), \(\operatorname{diag}(X)=\mathbf1\) strengthens or leaves unchanged the elliptope relaxation without removing any sign-feasible point.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Cut distances derived from sign lifts satisfy every odd-cycle metric inequality. Adding these inequalities can only tighten or leave unchanged the elliptope while preserving all discrete solutions.
assumptions_latex: \(C\) is a simple cycle and \(F\subseteq E(C)\) has odd cardinality.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every sign lift satisfies \(\sum_{e\in F}d_e-\sum_{e\in E(C)\setminus F}d_e\le|F|-1\); imposing these cycle inequalities strengthens or leaves unchanged the elliptope relaxation.

knowledge_statements.title: Triangle-Inequality Strengthening
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Three-vertex metric and perimeter inequalities for cut-distance lifts.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For distinct \(i,j,k\), every cut-distance vector \(d_{uv}=(1-X_{uv})/2\) generated by \(X=xx^{\mathsf T}\), \(x\in\{-1,1\}^n\), satisfies \(d_{ij}\le d_{ik}+d_{kj}\), \(d_{ik}\le d_{ij}+d_{jk}\), \(d_{jk}\le d_{ij}+d_{ik}\), and \(d_{ij}+d_{ik}+d_{jk}\le2\). Intersecting the elliptope with these inequalities for every triple preserves all rank-one sign matrices and strengthens or leaves unchanged the SDP relaxation.

knowledge_statements.title: Hypermetric-Inequality Strengthening
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Hypermetric cuts for correlation-based binary semidefinite relaxations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X\in\mathbb S^n\) satisfy \(X\succeq0\) and \(X_{ii}=1\), and define \(d_{ij}=(1-X_{ij})/2\). For every integer vector \(b\in\mathbb Z^n\) with \(\sum_i b_i=1\), the associated hypermetric inequality is
\[\sum_{1\le i<j\le n}b_i b_j d_{ij}\le0.\]
Every cut semimetric satisfies this inequality. Consequently, adjoining any selected family of hypermetric inequalities to a binary quadratic SDP preserves all cut matrices while shrinking its feasible region; for a maximization relaxation, its optimal upper bound therefore cannot increase.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Hypermetric inequalities are valid for every cut metric and strengthen a binary quadratic SDP by removing fractional Gram matrices without removing integral cuts.
assumptions_latex: \(X\in\mathbb S^n_+\) and \(X_{ii}=1\) for every \(i\).
\(b\in\mathbb Z^n\) and \(\sum_i b_i=1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every cut-derived \(d\) satisfies \(\sum_{i<j}b_i b_jd_{ij}\le0\).

knowledge_statements.title: Integer Quadratic Matrix Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Rank-one matrix lifting of a bounded integer quadratic program.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(S\subseteq\mathbb Z^n\) be a bounded set described by linear constraints, and consider minimizing \(x^{\mathsf T}Qx+c^{\mathsf T}x\) over \(x\in S\). Introduce \(X\in\mathbb S^n\). The exact lifted model replaces the quadratic objective by \(\langle Q,X\rangle+c^{\mathsf T}x\) and imposes
\[Y=\begin{pmatrix}1&x^{\mathsf T}\\x&X\end{pmatrix}\succeq0,\qquad \operatorname{rank}(Y)=1,\qquad x\in S.\]
Because \(Y_{00}=1\), the first two matrix conditions together with rank one are equivalent to \(X=xx^{\mathsf T}\). Dropping rank one and retaining valid linearized constraints yields a semidefinite relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An integer quadratic program becomes a rank-one lifted matrix model; deleting the rank constraint produces an SDP relaxation while valid linearizations may be retained.
assumptions_latex: \(Q\in\mathbb S^n\), \(c\in\mathbb R^n\), and \(S\subseteq\mathbb Z^n\) is bounded.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The rank-one lifted formulation is exact, while replacing \(\operatorname{rank}(Y)=1\) by only \(Y\succeq0\) is a relaxation.

notation.meaning: Lift intended to equal the quadratic product matrix.

knowledge_statements.title: Mixed Binary–Integer Quadratic Relaxations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Moment-matrix relaxation separating binary diagonal identities from integer variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(x\in\{0,1\}^p\), \(z\in\mathbb Z^q\), and \(y=(x,z)\). For a quadratic objective or constraint in \(y\), introduce \(W\in\mathbb S^{p+q}\) and the homogenized matrix
\[M=\begin{pmatrix}1&y^{\mathsf T}\\y&W\end{pmatrix}.\]
The exact lift has \(W=yy^{\mathsf T}\). Its basic mixed relaxation imposes \(M\succeq0\), the binary identities \(W_{ii}=x_i\) for \(1\le i\le p\), and all available linearized original constraints. Retaining \(z\in\mathbb Z^q\) gives a mixed-integer SDP; replacing it by a valid continuous domain gives a continuous SDP relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Mixed lifts impose a positive-semidefinite moment matrix and binary diagonal identities, while integer variables may either remain integral or be continuously relaxed.
assumptions_latex: \(x\in\{0,1\}^p\) and \(z\in\mathbb Z^q\) satisfy the original mixed-integer constraints.
All quadratic expressions are linearized through \(W\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every original feasible point induces a feasible relaxation point with \(W=yy^{\mathsf T}\).

knowledge_statements.title: Completely Positive Lifting Interface
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cone substitution for nonnegative rank-one quadratic lifts.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The completely positive cone is
\[\mathcal{CP}^m=\left\{\sum_{k=1}^r v_kv_k^{\mathsf T}:r\in\mathbb N,\ v_k\in\mathbb R_+^m\right\}.\]
If a nonnegative quadratic model uses \(y\in\mathbb R_+^m\) and the rank-one lift \(Y=yy^{\mathsf T}\), then \(Y\in\mathcal{CP}^m\). Replacing the nonconvex rank-one condition by membership in \(\mathcal{CP}^m\) converts quadratic expressions to linear forms \(\langle Q,Y\rangle\). Exactness requires the remaining linear constraints to characterize the appropriate completely positive slice; absent such conditions, the substitution is only a convex relaxation interface.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Completely positive lifting replaces a nonnegative rank-one product matrix by a conic combination of such matrices, linearizing quadratic expressions but not automatically ensuring exactness.
assumptions_latex: \(y\in\mathbb R_+^m\).
Quadratic terms are represented by \(Y=yy^{\mathsf T}\) before cone substitution.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Rank-one nonnegative lifts lie in \(\mathcal{CP}^m\), so \(Y\in\mathcal{CP}^m\) is a convex cone substitution.

notation.meaning: Cone of completely positive symmetric matrices.

knowledge_statements.title: Dense Doubly Nonnegative Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Full-matrix doubly nonnegative cone relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(m\ge1\), the dense doubly nonnegative cone is
\[\mathcal{DNN}^m=\{Y\in\mathbb S^m:Y\succeq0,\ Y_{ij}\ge0\text{ for all }i,j\}.\]
A dense doubly nonnegative model represents every entry of \(Y\), imposes the full positive-semidefinite constraint and every entrywise nonnegativity inequality, and expresses lifted objectives and side constraints linearly in \(Y\). Since every completely positive matrix is both positive semidefinite and entrywise nonnegative, \(\mathcal{CP}^m\subseteq\mathcal{DNN}^m\); substituting \(\mathcal{DNN}^m\) for \(\mathcal{CP}^m\) therefore gives an outer relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A dense DNN model requires the entire lifted matrix to be positive semidefinite and entrywise nonnegative, providing an outer approximation of the completely positive cone.
assumptions_latex: \(Y\in\mathbb S^m\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal{CP}^m\subseteq\mathcal{DNN}^m\).

knowledge_statements.title: Structured Doubly Nonnegative Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Chordal partial-matrix representation of structured DNN constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(G=(V,E)\) be chordal with maximal cliques \(C_1,\ldots,C_t\), and let \(Y\) be a symmetric partial matrix whose specified entries are the diagonal and edges of \(G\). Then \(Y\) has a positive-semidefinite completion if and only if
\[Y[C_k,C_k]\succeq0\qquad(k=1,\ldots,t).\]
A structured doubly nonnegative model combines these clique constraints with \(Y_{ij}\ge0\) on every specified entry used by the lifted objective or side constraints, enforcing consistency on clique overlaps. This represents PSD-completability exactly for the chordal pattern, while nonnegativity of unspecified completion entries requires additional variables or constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a chordal sparsity pattern, clique PSD constraints exactly characterize PSD completion; entrywise nonnegativity is imposed on modeled entries, with completion-wide nonnegativity requiring extra constraints.
assumptions_latex: \(G=(V,E)\) is chordal.
The diagonal and all edge entries of the symmetric partial matrix \(Y\) are specified.

knowledge_statements.title: Doubly Nonnegative Validity Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dimension boundary for replacing complete positivity by double nonnegativity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For the cones of completely positive and doubly nonnegative matrices,
\[\mathcal{CP}^m=\mathcal{DNN}^m\quad\text{for }m\le4,\qquad \mathcal{CP}^m\subsetneq\mathcal{DNN}^m\quad\text{for }m\ge5.\]
Thus the DNN substitution is cone-exact in dimensions at most four. Beginning in dimension five, matrices exist that are positive semidefinite and entrywise nonnegative but have no decomposition into nonnegative rank-one factors. Accordingly, a DNN relaxation of a completely positive formulation can admit spurious lifted points and need not preserve the original optimal value once the lifted matrix dimension reaches five.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The CP and DNN cones coincide through dimension four but differ from dimension five onward, where DNN relaxations can admit non-completely-positive matrices.
assumptions_latex: \(m\) is the order of the symmetric lifted matrix.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Cone equality holds for \(m\le4\), whereas the inclusion is strict for \(m\ge5\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The equality through order four and strict inclusion from order five are substantive boundary results requiring authoritative theorem-level support; none is cited.

knowledge_statements.title: Copositive Cone-Approximation Interface
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dual cone interface for inner and outer copositive approximations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Define the copositive cone by
\[\mathcal{COP}^m=\{A\in\mathbb S^m:x^{\mathsf T}Ax\ge0\text{ for every }x\in\mathbb R_+^m\}.\]
Under the trace inner product, \((\mathcal{CP}^m)^*=\mathcal{COP}^m\) and \((\mathcal{COP}^m)^*=\mathcal{CP}^m\). Hence any tractable inner approximation \(K\subseteq\mathcal{COP}^m\) induces the outer completely positive approximation \(\mathcal{CP}^m\subseteq K^*\), suitable for relaxation. Conversely, an outer approximation \(O\supseteq\mathcal{COP}^m\) yields \(O^*\subseteq\mathcal{CP}^m\), which is an inner restriction rather than a relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Completely positive and copositive cones are dual. Inner copositive approximations dualize to outer CP relaxations, while outer copositive approximations yield inner CP restrictions.
assumptions_latex: Dual cones are taken in \(\mathbb S^m\) under \(\langle A,Y\rangle=\operatorname{tr}(AY)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(K\subseteq\mathcal{COP}^m\), then \(\mathcal{CP}^m\subseteq K^*\).

notation.meaning: Dual cone of a copositive inner approximation.
Dual cone of a copositive outer approximation.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: cone-inclusion reversal under duality is standard

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The duality and inclusion-reversal statements are coherent and correctly classified as duality, but no inspectable source supports them.

knowledge_statements.title: Basic Max-Cut Relaxation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Standard vector-Gram SDP relaxation of weighted Max-Cut.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For an undirected graph \(G=(V,E)\) with weights \(w_{ij}\), encode a cut by signs \(s_i\in\{-1,1\}\). Its value is \(\frac12\sum_{\{i,j\}\in E}w_{ij}(1-s_is_j)\). Replacing \(s_is_j\) by a Gram entry gives the basic relaxation
\[\max_{X\in\mathbb S^{|V|}}\ \frac12\sum_{\{i,j\}\in E}w_{ij}(1-X_{ij})\quad\text{subject to}\quad X\succeq0,\quad X_{ii}=1\ \text{for all }i.\]
Every cut produces the feasible rank-one matrix \(X=ss^{\mathsf T}\), so the SDP optimum is an upper bound on the maximum cut value.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The basic Max-Cut SDP replaces products of cut signs by entries of a positive-semidefinite correlation matrix with unit diagonal.
assumptions_latex: \(G=(V,E)\) is a finite undirected graph.
Each edge has a real weight \(w_{ij}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{OPT}_{\mathrm{cut}}\le\operatorname{OPT}_{\mathrm{SDP}}\).

notation.meaning: Sign indicating the side of the cut containing vertex i.
Gram matrix relaxing the sign-product matrix.

knowledge_statements.title: Strengthened Max-Cut Relaxations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Metric-polytope cuts added to the basic Max-Cut SDP.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X\succeq0\) satisfy \(X_{ii}=1\), and set \(d_{ij}=(1-X_{ij})/2\). A triangle-strengthened Max-Cut relaxation additionally requires, for every distinct \(i,j,k\),
\[d_{ij}\le d_{ik}+d_{jk},\qquad d_{ik}\le d_{ij}+d_{jk},\qquad d_{jk}\le d_{ij}+d_{ik},\qquad d_{ij}+d_{ik}+d_{jk}\le2.\]
These inequalities hold for every cut semimetric. Adding them, and optionally further valid metric or hypermetric inequalities, preserves every cut matrix and produces a feasible region contained in that of the basic SDP. Its maximization bound is therefore no weaker than the basic bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Strengthened Max-Cut SDPs add triangle, metric, or hypermetric inequalities that retain all cuts while excluding fractional correlation matrices.
assumptions_latex: \(X\in\mathbb S^{|V|}_+\) and \(X_{ii}=1\) for every vertex \(i\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The strengthened feasible set contains all cut matrices and is contained in the basic SDP feasible set.

notation.meaning: Relaxed separation indicator for vertices i and j.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: displayed triangle inequalities are directly valid on zero-one cut semimetrics

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The four displayed triangle/perimeter inequalities are valid for cut semimetrics and fit a strengthening-condition container, but no inspectable citation supports the formulation.

knowledge_statements.title: Weighted Max-Cut Variants
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nonnegative edge-weight extension of the basic Max-Cut formulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For edge weights \(w_{ij}\ge0\), weighted Max-Cut maximizes
\[\sum_{\{i,j\}\in E}w_{ij}\,\mathbf1\{s_i\ne s_j\}=\frac12\sum_{\{i,j\}\in E}w_{ij}(1-s_is_j).\]
Its vector-Gram relaxation replaces each sign \(s_i\) by a unit vector \(u_i\), equivalently using \(X_{ij}=u_i^{\mathsf T}u_j\), and maximizes \(\frac12\sum_{\{i,j\}\in E}w_{ij}(1-X_{ij})\) subject to \(X\succeq0\) and \(X_{ii}=1\). The feasible region is independent of the nonnegative weights; only the linear objective coefficients change.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Weighted Max-Cut uses the same unit-vector or Gram feasible region as unweighted Max-Cut, with nonnegative edge weights appearing only in the objective.
assumptions_latex: \(G=(V,E)\) is finite and undirected.
\(w_{ij}\ge0\) for every \(\{i,j\}\in E\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every weighted cut matrix is SDP-feasible, and the SDP objective agrees with its weighted cut value.

notation.meaning: Unit vector assigned to vertex i.
Gram matrix of the vertex vectors.

knowledge_statements.title: Signed Max-Cut Variants
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Signed edge objectives and the boundary of nonnegative-weight rounding guarantees.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(w_{ij}\in\mathbb R\) have arbitrary signs. The signed cut objective and its SDP relaxation retain the forms
\[\frac12\sum_{\{i,j\}\in E}w_{ij}(1-s_is_j),\qquad \max\ \frac12\sum_{\{i,j\}\in E}w_{ij}(1-X_{ij})\ \text{ subject to }X\succeq0,\ X_{ii}=1.\]
Every cut matrix remains feasible, so the SDP still supplies an upper bound. However, approximation arguments that compare each nonnegative edge contribution separately do not extend automatically: multiplying an edgewise inequality by \(w_{ij}<0\) reverses its direction. Thus the usual nonnegative-weight multiplicative guarantee requires additional sign structure or a different benchmark.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Signed weights preserve SDP validity as an upper bound, but negative coefficients invalidate the edgewise argument underlying the usual nonnegative-weight approximation guarantee.
assumptions_latex: \(G=(V,E)\) is finite and undirected.
\(w_{ij}\in\mathbb R\) may be positive, zero, or negative.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The SDP upper bound remains valid, but a nonnegative-weight rounding ratio cannot be transferred without further hypotheses.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: negative multiplication reverses the edgewise comparison used for nonnegative weights

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The SDP upper-bound validity and failure of the edgewise nonnegative-weight argument are coherent and fit a failure-boundary container, but the guarantee boundary lacks an authoritative citation.

children.title: Weight–Sign Interaction Regimes
children.top_down_role: Structural regimes determined jointly by weight magnitude and sign patterns.

assumptions_latex: \(G=(V,E)\) is an undirected graph with real edge weights \(w_{ij}\).
\(X\succeq 0\) and \(X_{ii}=1\) for every \(i\in V\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\operatorname{CUT}(s)=\frac12\sum_{ij\in E}w_{ij}(1-s_is_j)\leq \operatorname{SDP}(G,w):=\max_X\frac12\sum_{ij\in E}w_{ij}(1-X_{ij}).\] This upper-bound relation holds for arbitrary signs because every \(ss^{\mathsf T}\) is SDP-feasible. However, the edgewise Goemans--Williamson comparison \(w_{ij}\theta_{ij}/\pi\geq \alpha_{\mathrm{GW}}w_{ij}(1-\cos\theta_{ij})/2\) preserves its direction only when \(w_{ij}\geq0\). Thus mixed or negative weights require a global analysis or a reformulation; the standard nonnegative-weight approximation proof cannot be applied term by term.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separates SDP validity from the nonnegative-weight edgewise approximation argument.

children.title: Max-Cut Vector Embeddings
children.top_down_role: Vector-based geometric representations of the Max-Cut relaxation.

knowledge_statements.title: Max-Cut Vector Embeddings
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unit-vector form of the basic weighted Max-Cut semidefinite relaxation in a dimension sufficient to represent every feasible correlation matrix.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The Max-Cut vector relaxation replaces every scalar cut sign by a unit vector and every sign product by an inner product. Its objective is the weighted sum of relaxed edge-separation quantities \((1-\langle v_i,v_j\rangle)/2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Assign a unit vector to each vertex and maximize weighted pairwise separation; ordinary cut signs are one-dimensional feasible embeddings.
assumptions_latex: \(G=(V,E)\) is an undirected graph with \(V=\{1,\ldots,n\}\) and real edge weights \(w_{ij}\).
\(d\geq n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\max_{v_1,\ldots,v_n\in\mathbb R^d}\ \frac12\sum_{ij\in E}w_{ij}(1-\langle v_i,v_j\rangle)\quad\text{subject to}\quad \|v_i\|_2=1\ \text{for every }i\in V.\] Every sign assignment \(s_i\in\{-1,1\}\) embeds as \(v_i=s_i e_1\), so the vector optimum is at least the maximum cut value. Because \(d\geq n\), every feasible \(n\times n\) correlation matrix has such a Gram representation.

children.title: Biased Hyperplane Rounding
children.top_down_role: Hyperplane rounding variants using shifted or nonuniform decision boundaries.

assumptions_latex: \(v_1,\ldots,v_n\in\mathbb R^d\) are unit vectors.
\(t\in\mathbb R\) is a fixed threshold.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Sample \(g\sim N(0,I_d)\) and output \(s_i=1\) when \(\langle g,v_i\rangle\geq t\), otherwise output \(s_i=-1\). Then \(\Pr(s_i=1)=1-\Phi(t)\) for every vertex. For \(\rho_{ij}=\langle v_i,v_j\rangle\), the separation probability is \[p_t(\rho_{ij})=2\bigl(\Phi(t)-\Phi_2(t,t;\rho_{ij})\bigr),\] where \(\Phi_2(\cdot,\cdot;ho)\) is the standard bivariate normal distribution function with correlation \(\rho\). At \(t=0\), this reduces to ordinary random hyperplane rounding.

notation.meaning: bivariate standard normal distribution function with correlation \(\rho\)

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Thresholded Gaussian projection version; the taxonomy does not identify a unique biased-rounding variant.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Biased hyperplane rounding offsets the projection threshold from zero. The threshold fixes each vertex's marginal sign bias, while pairwise separation is determined by a correlated bivariate Gaussian probability.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Thresholding Gaussian projections away from zero biases vertex signs; pairwise cut probabilities are bivariate-normal probabilities determined by vector correlations.
knowledge_statements.title: Biased Hyperplane Rounding

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The thresholded-Gaussian formula is mathematically plausible, but the taxonomy does not identify this as the intended biased variant and no source supports the selected formulation.

children.title: Multi-Hyperplane Rounding
children.top_down_role: Rounding families using several hyperplanes to form discrete decisions.

assumptions_latex: \(v_1,\ldots,v_n\in\mathbb R^d\) are unit vectors.
\(k\geq1\) is an integer.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Independently sample \(g_1,\ldots,g_k\sim N(0,I_d)\), set \(b_{i\ell}=\operatorname{sign}\langle g_\ell,v_i\rangle\), and output the parity sign \(s_i=\prod_{\ell=1}^k b_{i\ell}\). If \(p_{ij}=\arccos(\langle v_i,v_j\rangle)/\pi\) is the one-hyperplane separation probability, independence gives \[\Pr(s_i\neq s_j)=\frac{1-(1-2p_{ij})^k}{2}.\] The algorithm outputs the cut encoded by \(s\); for \(k=1\) it is ordinary random hyperplane rounding.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Parity aggregation is one precise multi-hyperplane rule; other aggregations yield different algorithms.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: In parity-based multi-hyperplane rounding, independent hyperplanes produce sign bits and their product determines the final cut sign. Pair separation occurs when an odd number of hyperplanes separate the two vectors.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Sample several independent hyperplanes and use the parity of their signs; an edge is cut when an odd number of hyperplanes separate its endpoints.
knowledge_statements.title: Multi-Hyperplane Rounding

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Parity is only one possible multi-hyperplane aggregation rule. A dedicated source is required to establish that this precise algorithm is intended by the leaf.

children.title: Bias–Multiplicity Tradeoffs
children.top_down_role: Approximation and feasibility tradeoffs between biased cuts and multiple projections.

assumptions_latex: A single thresholded hyperplane separates a fixed vector pair with probability \(p_t\in[0,1]\).
\(k\geq1\) hyperplanes are sampled independently and aggregated by parity.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The final separation probability is \[q_{k,t}=\sum_{\substack{r=0\\r\text{ odd}}}^{k}\binom{k}{r}p_t^r(1-p_t)^{k-r}=\frac{1-(1-2p_t)^k}{2}.\] Hence \(q_{k,t}\to 1/2\) as \(k\to\infty\) whenever \(0<p_t<1\), and \[\frac{\partial q_{k,t}}{\partial p_t}=k(1-2p_t)^{k-1}.\] Multiplicity can amplify small separation probabilities, but it also drives nondegenerate pairwise separation toward \(1/2\), potentially erasing angular discrimination introduced by the bias parameter.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact tradeoff for independent thresholded hyperplanes combined by parity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For parity aggregation, bias affects the single-hyperplane probability \(p_t\), while multiplicity transforms it by the odd-binomial map. Increasing multiplicity amplifies rare separations but asymptotically flattens every nondegenerate separation probability to one half.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under parity aggregation, multiplicity transforms a biased separation probability by an odd-binomial formula, amplifying rare separation while eventually losing angular discrimination.
knowledge_statements.title: Bias–Multiplicity Tradeoffs

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The odd-binomial formula is correct for independent parity aggregation, but the claimed tradeoff inherits the unresolved choice of biased and multi-hyperplane variants and has no citation.

assumptions_latex: A randomized rounding algorithm has a finite sample space \(\Omega=\Omega_1\times\cdots\times\Omega_m\).
Its objective value \(Z(\omega)\) is computable, and conditional expectations are computable in polynomial time.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Initialize with no coordinates fixed. For \(r=1,\ldots,m\), choose \(a_r\in\Omega_r\) maximizing \[\mathbb E[Z\mid \omega_1=a_1,\ldots,\omega_{r-1}=a_{r-1},\omega_r=a_r].\] After fixing all coordinates, output the deterministic rounded solution corresponding to \(\omega=(a_1,\ldots,a_m)\). The conditional expectation never decreases, so the output satisfies \[Z(\omega)\geq\mathbb E[Z].\] Applying this interface to Gaussian hyperplane rounding additionally requires an exact finite-support surrogate or a controlled discretization.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditional-expectation interface, conditional on finite support or justified Gaussian discretization.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Let \(\theta_{ij}=\arccos\langle v_i,v_j\rangle\). children.title: Max-Cut Integrality Gaps
children.top_down_role: Worst-case separation between semidefinite values and integral cut values.

assumptions_latex: \(I=(G,w)\) is a nonnegative-weight Max-Cut instance with \(\operatorname{SDP}(I)>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Define the instance ratio and family gap by \[\gamma(I):=\frac{\operatorname{OPT}(I)}{\operatorname{SDP}(I)},\qquad \gamma_{\mathrm{MC}}:=\inf_I\gamma(I).\] Because the SDP is a relaxation, \(\gamma(I)\leq1\). The Goemans--Williamson rounding theorem gives \(\operatorname{OPT}(I)\geq\alpha_{\mathrm{GW}}\operatorname{SDP}(I)\), hence \[\alpha_{\mathrm{GW}}\leq\gamma_{\mathrm{MC}}\leq\gamma(I)\leq1.\] Equivalently, under the reciprocal convention \(\operatorname{SDP}(I)/\operatorname{OPT}(I)\), every instance has gap at most \(1/\alpha_{\mathrm{GW}}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Ratio convention is integral optimum divided by the basic SDP optimum.

children.title: Max-Cut Approximation Hardness
children.top_down_role: Complexity barriers governing achievable approximation quality.

assumptions_latex: Approximation ratios are measured for polynomial-time algorithms on nonnegative-weight Max-Cut instances.
For the unconditional bound, assume \(P\neq NP\); for the sharp bound, assume the Unique Games Conjecture.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For every \(\varepsilon>0\), it is NP-hard to approximate Max-Cut within a factor greater than \(16/17+\varepsilon\). Under the Unique Games Conjecture, for every \(\varepsilon>0\), no polynomial-time algorithm can guarantee a factor greater than \(\alpha_{\mathrm{GW}}+\varepsilon\), unless \(P=NP\). children.title: Gap–Hardness Correspondence
children.top_down_role: Structural comparison between relaxation gaps and approximation barriers.

knowledge_statements.title: Gap–Hardness Correspondence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unique-Games-conditional optimality of the Goemans–Williamson ratio for weighted Max-Cut.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a finite graph with nonnegative edge weights, let \(\operatorname{OPT}(G)\) be the maximum cut weight and let \(\operatorname{SDP}(G)\) be the Goemans–Williamson relaxation value. Define \[\rho_{\mathrm{GW}}:=\min_{-1\le t<1}\frac{2\arccos(t)}{\pi(1-t)}\approx0.87856.\] Random-hyperplane rounding gives expected value at least \(\rho_{\mathrm{GW}}\operatorname{SDP}(G)\), hence at least \(\rho_{\mathrm{GW}}\operatorname{OPT}(G)\). Assuming the Unique Games Conjecture, for every \(\varepsilon>0\), no polynomial-time algorithm approximates Max-Cut within factor \(\rho_{\mathrm{GW}}+\varepsilon\). Thus the relaxation-gap threshold and conditional approximation-hardness threshold coincide.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The Goemans–Williamson ratio is both the SDP rounding guarantee and, under the Unique Games Conjecture, the optimal polynomial-time Max-Cut approximation threshold.
assumptions_latex: Edge weights satisfy \(w_e\ge0\).
The hardness conclusion assumes the Unique Games Conjecture.
Algorithms are measured in the polynomial-time approximation model.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The common gap and conditional hardness threshold is \(\rho_{\mathrm{GW}}\approx0.87856\).

notation.meaning: value of the Goemans–Williamson semidefinite relaxation

knowledge_statements.title: Orthonormal-Representation View
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Handle formulation using orthonormal representations with nonedges constrained to be orthogonal.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G=(V,E)\) be a finite simple graph. An orthonormal representation of \(G\) is a family of unit vectors \((u_i)_{i\in V}\) in a real Euclidean space such that \(u_i^{\mathsf T}u_j=0\) whenever \(i\ne j\) and \(\{i,j\}\notin E\). A unit vector \(c\) is a handle. With the convention \(1/0=+\infty\), the Lovász theta number has the representation \[\vartheta(G)=\min_{(u_i),c}\max_{i\in V}\frac{1}{(c^{\mathsf T}u_i)^2},\] where the minimum ranges over all such representations and unit handles in arbitrary finite dimension.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Theta is the smallest possible worst reciprocal squared handle projection over orthonormal representations that make nonadjacent vertices orthogonal.
assumptions_latex: \(G\) is finite and simple.
All representing vectors and the handle are real unit vectors.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\vartheta(G)=\min_{(u_i),c}\max_{i\in V}(c^{\mathsf T}u_i)^{-2}\).

knowledge_statements.title: Primal Theta Formulations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Trace-normalized primal SDP for the Lovász theta number.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a finite simple graph \(G=(V,E)\), let \(J\) be the all-ones matrix indexed by \(V\). The trace-normalized primal formulation is \[\vartheta(G)=\max\left\{\langle J,X\rangle:\ \operatorname{Tr}(X)=1,\ X_{ij}=0\ \text{for every }\{i,j\}\in E,\ X\succeq0\right\}.\] Its feasible matrices are precisely Gram matrices of vectors \((v_i)_{i\in V}\) satisfying \(v_i^{\mathsf T}v_j=0\) on edges and \(\sum_i\lVert v_i\rVert^2=1\); under this factorization, the objective is \(\left\lVert\sum_i v_i\right\rVert^2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Theta maximizes the sum of all Gram-matrix entries over positive semidefinite, trace-one matrices whose edge entries vanish.
assumptions_latex: \(G=(V,E)\) is a finite simple graph.
Matrices are real symmetric and indexed by \(V\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed SDP and its Gram-vector formulation both have value \(\vartheta(G)\).

knowledge_statements.title: Theta-Plus Variant
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Szegedy theta-plus convention obtained by replacing edge equalities with nonpositive edge entries.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a finite simple graph \(G=(V,E)\), define the theta-plus number by \[\vartheta^{+}(G):=\max\left\{\langle J,X\rangle:\ \operatorname{Tr}(X)=1,\ X\succeq0,\ X_{ij}\le0\ \text{for every }\{i,j\}\in E\right\}.\] Every feasible matrix for \(\vartheta(G)\) is feasible for \(\vartheta^{+}(G)\), and the normalized incidence vector of every stable set yields a feasible rank-one matrix. Hence \[\alpha(G)\le\vartheta(G)\le\vartheta^{+}(G).\] This convention is distinct from Schrijver's entrywise-nonnegative strengthening, commonly denoted \(\vartheta'(G)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Theta-plus relaxes zero edge entries to nonpositive entries, giving an upper bound at least as large as ordinary theta.
assumptions_latex: \(G=(V,E)\) is a finite simple graph.
The Szegedy convention for \(\vartheta^{+}\) is used.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\alpha(G)\le\vartheta(G)\le\vartheta^{+}(G)\).

knowledge_statements.title: Theta-Body Strengthening
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Algebraic theta bodies as nested sums-of-squares outer approximations of a real variety's convex hull.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(I\subseteq\mathbb R[x_1,\ldots,x_n]\) be an ideal and let \(V_{\mathbb R}(I)\) be its real variety. An affine polynomial \(f\) is \(k\)-sums-of-squares modulo \(I\) if \(f-\sum_r h_r^2\in I\) for polynomials \(h_r\) of degree at most \(k\). The order-\(k\) theta body is \[\operatorname{TH}_k(I):=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:f(x)\ge0\ \text{for every affine }f\text{ that is }k\text{-sums-of-squares modulo }I\}.\] These convex relaxations satisfy \[\overline{\operatorname{conv}}\!\left(V_{\mathbb R}(I)\right)\subseteq\operatorname{TH}_{k+1}(I)\subseteq\operatorname{TH}_k(I).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A theta body enforces affine inequalities having bounded-degree sums-of-squares certificates modulo an ideal, producing nested convex outer approximations.
assumptions_latex: \(I\) is an ideal in \(\mathbb R[x_1,\ldots,x_n]\).
The degree bound applies to each polynomial squared in the certificate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\overline{\operatorname{conv}}(V_{\mathbb R}(I))\subseteq\operatorname{TH}_{k+1}(I)\subseteq\operatorname{TH}_k(I)\).

notation.meaning: real variety of the ideal I

knowledge_statements.title: Hierarchy-Based Theta Refinements
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Moment-SOS hierarchy refining the stable-set theta relaxation through increasing localizing degree.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(G=(V,E)\), let \(I_G=\langle x_i^2-x_i,\ x_ix_j:\{i,j\}\in E\rangle\). Applying increasing-order moment or sums-of-squares constraints to \(I_G\) yields semidefinite upper bounds \(u_k(G)\) for the stable-set number. With a consistent degree convention, \[\alpha(G)\le u_{k+1}(G)\le u_k(G),\] and the first nontrivial level recovers a theta-type relaxation. Because the feasible stable-set variety is finite, the hierarchy becomes exact at some finite order; in particular, an order no greater than the number of vertices suffices under the standard full moment construction.

The hierarchy includes the Boolean and edge ideals defining stable-set incidence vectors.

children.title: Perfect-Graph Exactness Regimes
children.top_down_role: Graph classes where theta-based bounds align with relevant combinatorial parameters.

knowledge_statements.title: Perfect-Graph Exactness Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exactness of the Lovász theta sandwich on finite perfect graphs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(G=(V,E)\) be a finite perfect graph, and use the convention \(\alpha(G)\leq\vartheta(G)\leq\chi(\overline G)\). Since the complement of a perfect graph is perfect, \(\chi(\overline G)=\omega(\overline G)=\alpha(G)\). Consequently,
\[
\vartheta(G)=\alpha(G)=\chi(\overline G).
\]
The same equality holds for every induced subgraph \(H\) of \(G\): \(\vartheta(H)=\alpha(H)\). Thus the theta semidefinite bound exactly computes the stability number throughout the perfect-graph regime.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a perfect graph and every induced subgraph, the theta sandwich collapses: the Lovász theta number equals the stability number and the complementary chromatic number.
assumptions_latex: \(G\) is finite and perfect.
\(\vartheta\) follows the convention \(\alpha(G)\leq\vartheta(G)\leq\chi(\overline G)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\vartheta(H)=\alpha(H)=\chi(\overline H)\) for every induced subgraph \(H\) of \(G\).

notation.meaning: Lovász theta number of G under the stated convention

children.title: Imperfect-Graph Separation Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Regimes where theta remains separated from integral graph parameters.

knowledge_statements.title: Imperfect-Graph Separation Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Odd cycles provide an explicit strict gap in the theta sandwich.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(G=C_{2k+1}\), where \(k\geq2\) is an integer. Then
\[
\alpha(G)=k,
\qquad
\vartheta(G)=\frac{(2k+1)\cos\!\left(\pi/(2k+1)\right)}{1+\cos\!\left(\pi/(2k+1)\right)},
\qquad
\chi(\overline G)=k+1.
\]
Moreover,
\[
k<\vartheta(G)<k+1,
\]
so \(\alpha(G)<\vartheta(G)<\chi(\overline G)\). Thus theta exactness can fail when the perfectness assumption is removed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every odd cycle of length at least five has stability number k and complementary chromatic number k+1, with its Lovász theta value strictly between them.
assumptions_latex: \(G=C_{2k+1}\) with integer \(k\geq2\).
The theta convention is \(\alpha(G)\leq\vartheta(G)\leq\chi(\overline G)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\alpha(G)<\vartheta(G)<\chi(\overline G)\).

children.title: Graph Equipartition Relaxations
children.top_down_role: Semidefinite relaxations for partitioning vertices into equally sized groups.

knowledge_statements.title: Graph Equipartition Relaxations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cluster-matrix SDP relaxation for equal-size multiway partitions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(G\) have Laplacian \(L\), let \(n=km\), and let \(Z\in\{0,1\}^{n\times k}\) encode an equipartition by \(Z\mathbf1_k=\mathbf1_n\) and \(Z^{\mathsf T}\mathbf1_n=m\mathbf1_k\). Its cluster matrix \(Y=ZZ^{\mathsf T}\) satisfies \(Y\succeq0\), \(Y\geq0\), \(\operatorname{diag}(Y)=\mathbf1_n\), and \(Y\mathbf1_n=m\mathbf1_n\). Dropping integrality and the rank restriction gives
\[
\min\left\{\tfrac12\langle L,Y\rangle:Y\succeq0,\ Y\geq0,\ \operatorname{diag}(Y)=\mathbf1_n,\ Y\mathbf1_n=m\mathbf1_n\right\}.
\]
Every equipartition embeds feasibly, so this optimum is a lower bound on minimum equipartition cut weight.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An equal-size partition yields a positive-semidefinite cluster matrix with fixed diagonal and row sums; dropping integrality and rank gives an SDP lower bound.
assumptions_latex: \(G\) is an undirected weighted graph with nonnegative edge weights.
\(n=km\) for positive integers \(k,m\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed SDP optimum does not exceed the minimum weight of an equipartition cut.

knowledge_statements.title: Graph Bisection Relaxations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Standard sign-vector SDP relaxation of minimum graph bisection.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(G\) be a weighted graph on even \(n\) with Laplacian \(L\). A bisection is encoded by \(x\in\{-1,1\}^n\) with \(\mathbf1^{\mathsf T}x=0\), and its cut weight is \(\tfrac14x^{\mathsf T}Lx\). Setting \(X=xx^{\mathsf T}\) and dropping the rank-one condition gives
\[
\min\left\{\tfrac14\langle L,X\rangle:X\succeq0,\ \operatorname{diag}(X)=\mathbf1_n,\ X\mathbf1_n=0\right\}.
\]
Every bisection produces a feasible rank-one matrix with the same objective value; therefore the SDP optimum is a lower bound on the minimum bisection weight.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Lifting a balanced sign vector to its Gram matrix and dropping rank one produces an SDP lower bound for minimum graph bisection.
assumptions_latex: \(G\) is an undirected weighted graph with nonnegative edge weights.
The number of vertices \(n\) is even.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{val}_{\mathrm{SDP}}\leq\operatorname{val}_{\mathrm{bisection}}\).

children.title: Balance-Constraint Regimes
children.top_down_role: Exact, relaxed, and asymmetric balance requirements across partition models.

knowledge_statements.title: Balance-Constraint Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Assignment predicates for exact, bounded, and unconstrained part sizes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(k\) labeled parts, an assignment matrix \(Z\in\{0,1\}^{n\times k}\) represents a partition precisely when \(Z\mathbf1_k=\mathbf1_n\). Writing \(s=Z^{\mathsf T}\mathbf1_n\), the principal balance regimes are: exact sizes \(s=\bar s\); interval balance \(\ell\leq s\leq u\); relative balance \(\lvert s_a-n/k\rvert\leq\delta\) for every \(a\); and unconstrained nonempty parts \(s_a\geq1\). These predicates are linear in \(Z\). Any lifted conic relaxation preserves a selected regime by retaining the corresponding linear constraints on its first-order assignment variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Balance is imposed by linear constraints on column sums of a one-hot assignment matrix, covering exact, bounded, relative, and merely nonempty regimes.
assumptions_latex: Each vertex is assigned to exactly one labeled part.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The chosen balance regime is equivalent to its stated linear predicate on \(s=Z^{\mathsf T}\mathbf1_n\).

notation.meaning: componentwise lower and upper size bounds

children.title: Multiway Graph Partition Relaxations
children.top_down_role: Semidefinite relaxations for partitioning graphs into several prescribed groups.

knowledge_statements.title: Multiway Graph Partition Relaxations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Simplex-vector SDP relaxation for weighted multiway cuts.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(G=(V,E,w)\) and \(k\geq2\). Encode each part by one of \(k\) unit simplex vectors whose distinct inner products equal \(-1/(k-1)\). For the Gram matrix \(X\), the integral cut objective is
\[
\frac{k-1}{k}\sum_{\{i,j\}\in E}w_{ij}(1-X_{ij}).
\]
The simplex SDP relaxation minimizes this expression subject to \(X\succeq0\), \(X_{ii}=1\), and \(X_{ij}\geq-1/(k-1)\). Every integral \(k\)-partition supplies a feasible Gram matrix, so the relaxation is a lower bound for minimum \(k\)-way cut; prescribed balance constraints may be added separately.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Replacing discrete simplex labels by arbitrary unit vectors with the same lower inner-product bound yields an SDP lower bound for a multiway cut.
assumptions_latex: \(G=(V,E,w)\) has nonnegative edge weights.
\(k\geq2\) is an integer.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The simplex SDP optimum is no greater than the minimum weighted \(k\)-way cut value.

notation.meaning: Gram matrix of vertex label vectors

knowledge_statements.title: Graph Clustering Relaxations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cluster-matrix SDP for weighted disagreement minimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(E^+\) and \(E^-\) be weighted similar and dissimilar vertex pairs. An integral clustering has \(Y=ZZ^{\mathsf T}\), where \(Y_{ij}=1\) exactly when vertices \(i,j\) share a cluster. Dropping integrality, transitivity, and rank yields
\[
\min\left\{\sum_{\{i,j\}\in E^+}w_{ij}(1-Y_{ij})+\sum_{\{i,j\}\in E^-}w_{ij}Y_{ij}:Y\succeq0,\ Y\geq0,\ \operatorname{diag}(Y)=\mathbf1\right\}.
\]
Every clustering matrix is feasible and its objective equals its total disagreement weight. Hence the SDP optimum lower-bounds the minimum-disagreement clustering objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Relaxing an equivalence-relation cluster matrix to a nonnegative correlation matrix gives an SDP lower bound for weighted disagreement clustering.
assumptions_latex: Pair weights satisfy \(w_{ij}\geq0\).
Each observed pair belongs to exactly one of \(E^+\) and \(E^-\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed SDP value is at most the minimum integral disagreement cost.

knowledge_statements.title: Partition–Clustering Correspondence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalence between labeled partitions and integral co-membership matrices.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Z\in\{0,1\}^{n\times k}\) satisfy \(Z\mathbf1_k=\mathbf1_n\), and define \(Y=ZZ^{\mathsf T}\). Then \(Y_{ij}=1\) if and only if \(i\) and \(j\) occupy the same part, while \(Y\succeq0\), \(Y\geq0\), \(\operatorname{diag}(Y)=\mathbf1_n\), and \(\operatorname{rank}(Y)\leq k\). Conversely, every symmetric binary matrix with unit diagonal whose relation \(i\sim j\iff Y_{ij}=1\) is transitive is the cluster matrix of a partition, unique up to relabeling. It uses at most \(k\) parts exactly when \(\operatorname{rank}(Y)\leq k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A partition determines a binary co-membership Gram matrix, and every transitive binary unit-diagonal matrix recovers a partition uniquely up to cluster labels.
assumptions_latex: \(Z\) is a one-hot assignment matrix.
Empty labeled parts are permitted when counting at most \(k\) parts.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Partitions into at most \(k\) nonempty classes correspond, up to labels, to transitive binary cluster matrices \(Y\) with \(\operatorname{rank}(Y)\leq k\).

notation.meaning: vertices i and j belong to the same class

knowledge_statements.title: Quadratic Assignment Relaxations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: First-order semidefinite lift of the quadratic assignment problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For symmetric \(A,B\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\), the quadratic assignment problem minimizes \(\langle A,PBP^{\mathsf T}\rangle\) over permutation matrices \(P\). Put \(p=\operatorname{vec}(P)\) and lift \(Y=pp^{\mathsf T}\), so the objective is \(\langle B\otimes A,Y\rangle\). A basic SDP relaxation retains \(P\geq0\), \(P\mathbf1=\mathbf1\), \(P^{\mathsf T}\mathbf1=\mathbf1\), \(\operatorname{diag}(Y)=p\), and
\[
\begin{pmatrix}1&p^{\mathsf T}\\p&Y\end{pmatrix}\succeq0,
\]
while dropping integrality and rank one. Every permutation matrix has a feasible lift, so the relaxation gives a lower bound for minimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Vectorizing a permutation and replacing its rank-one outer product by a positive-semidefinite moment matrix gives a quadratic-assignment lower bound.
assumptions_latex: \(A,B\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) are symmetric.
Vectorization and the Kronecker product use consistent column-major ordering.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The lifted SDP optimum does not exceed the quadratic assignment optimum.

knowledge_statements.title: Traveling-Salesperson Relaxations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Edge-incidence moment SDP containing every Hamiltonian tour.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(K_n=(V,E)\) have edge costs \(c_e\), and let \(x\in\{0,1\}^E\) denote a Hamiltonian cycle. Lift \(Y=xx^{\mathsf T}\). A basic TSP SDP relaxation minimizes \(c^{\mathsf T}x\) subject to the degree equations \(\sum_{e\in\delta(v)}x_e=2\), subtour inequalities \(\sum_{e\in\delta(S)}x_e\geq2\) for \(\varnothing\neq S\subsetneq V\), bounds \(0\leq x\leq1\), \(\operatorname{diag}(Y)=x\), and
\[
\begin{pmatrix}1&x^{\mathsf T}\\x&Y\end{pmatrix}\succeq0.
\]
Dropping rank one and integrality retains every tour, hence yields a lower bound on the minimum tour cost.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Degree and subtour constraints combined with a positive-semidefinite edge moment lift form a valid lower-bounding relaxation for the traveling-salesperson problem.
assumptions_latex: The instance is the symmetric TSP on \(K_n\).
Edge costs are finite real numbers.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed relaxation has value at most the minimum Hamiltonian-cycle cost.

knowledge_statements.title: Association-Scheme Reductions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Symmetry reduction of invariant SDPs through a commutative orbital association scheme.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\Gamma\) be a finite permutation group on \(v\) points whose orbitals define a symmetric commutative association scheme with adjacency matrices \(A_0,\ldots,A_d\) and primitive idempotents \(E_0,\ldots,E_d\). Write
\[
A_i=\sum_{j=0}^d P_{ji}E_j.
\]
Suppose an SDP feasible set is convex and invariant under \(X\mapsto Q_gXQ_g^{\mathsf T}\) for every \(g\in\Gamma\), and its objective is invariant under the same action. Averaging a feasible matrix over \(\Gamma\) preserves feasibility and objective value and produces a matrix
\[
X=\sum_{i=0}^d x_iA_i.
\]
Since the Bose–Mesner algebra is simultaneously diagonalizable,
\[
X\succeq0
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\sum_{i=0}^d x_iP_{ji}\geq0
\quad\text{for every }j=0,\ldots,d.
\]
Thus the invariant positive-semidefinite constraint reduces to scalar linear inequalities in the coefficients \(x_i\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When a symmetric commutative association scheme is the orbital scheme of the SDP symmetry group, group averaging yields an equally good solution in the Bose–Mesner algebra, where positive semidefiniteness is equivalent to nonnegative scheme eigenvalues.
assumptions_latex: \(\Gamma\) is a finite permutation group whose orbitals define the stated symmetric commutative association scheme.
The SDP feasible set is convex and invariant under conjugation by the permutation matrices \(Q_g\), and the objective is invariant under the same action.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: An optimal invariant solution may be chosen in the Bose–Mesner algebra, where \(X\succeq0\) is equivalent to \(\sum_{i=0}^d x_iP_{ji}\geq0\) for every \(j\).

notation.meaning: orbital adjacency matrices of the association scheme

children.title: MAX-2SAT Semidefinite Relaxations
children.top_down_role: Semidefinite relaxations specialized to weighted or unweighted MAX-2SAT.

knowledge_statements.title: MAX-2SAT Semidefinite Relaxations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unit-vector SDP obtained from the quadratic satisfaction formula for weighted two-literal clauses.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\mathcal C\) be a finite collection of weighted two-literal clauses. Represent each truth assignment by \(x_i\in\{-1,1\}\), where \(x_i=1\) means true. For each \(C\in\mathcal C\), write the clause as \((s_Cx_{i_C})\lor(t_Cx_{j_C})\), where \(s_C,t_C\in\{-1,1\}\) and \(w_C\geq0\). Its satisfaction indicator is
\[
\frac{3+s_Cx_{i_C}+t_Cx_{j_C}-s_Ct_Cx_{i_C}x_{j_C}}{4}.
\]
Replace \(x_i\) by \(\langle v_0,v_i\rangle\) and \(x_ix_j\) by \(\langle v_i,v_j\rangle\), require \(\lVert v_0\rVert=\lVert v_i\rVert=1\), and maximize
\[
\sum_{C\in\mathcal C}\frac{w_C}{4}\left(3+s_C\langle v_0,v_{i_C}\rangle+t_C\langle v_0,v_{j_C}\rangle-s_Ct_C\langle v_{i_C},v_{j_C}\rangle\right).
\]
Every integral assignment embeds through \(v_i=x_iv_0\), so the SDP optimum upper-bounds the maximum satisfiable clause weight.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The quadratic satisfaction indicator for each weighted two-literal clause yields a unit-vector SDP containing every Boolean assignment, so its optimum upper-bounds weighted MAX-2SAT.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal C\) is a finite collection of two-literal clauses.
Every clause weight satisfies \(w_C\geq0\).
Each literal sign satisfies \(s_C,t_C\in\{-1,1\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{OPT}_{\mathrm{MAX\text{-}2SAT}}\leq\operatorname{OPT}_{\mathrm{SDP}}\).

notation.meaning: finite collection of weighted two-literal clauses
unit vector representing Boolean variable i

knowledge_statements.title: Boolean CSP Semidefinite Relaxations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Moment-SDP representation for finite weighted Boolean CSPs of bounded arity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(I\) be a weighted Boolean CSP on \(x\in\{-1,1\}^n\), with constraint polynomials \(P_C\) of degree at most \(k\), and choose \(d\geq\lceil k/2\rceil\). Its order-\(d\) semidefinite relaxation maximizes \(\sum_C w_C\widetilde{\mathbb E}[P_C(x)]\) over linear functionals \(\widetilde{\mathbb E}\) on polynomials of degree at most \(2d\), subject to \(\widetilde{\mathbb E}[1]=1\), \(\widetilde{\mathbb E}[q(x)^2]\geq0\) for every \(q\) of degree at most \(d\), and \(\widetilde{\mathbb E}[(x_i^2-1)q(x)]=0\) whenever the product has degree at most \(2d\). Every Boolean assignment induces a feasible functional, so the relaxation value upper-bounds the CSP optimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Replace evaluation at a Boolean assignment by a positive normalized pseudoexpectation satisfying the Boolean equations. Every assignment remains feasible, so the resulting SDP upper-bounds the optimal CSP value.
assumptions_latex: \(w_C\geq0\) for every constraint \(C\).
Each \(P_C\) is the multilinear polynomial representing its Boolean predicate.
\(d\geq\lceil k/2\rceil\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{OPT}(I)\leq\operatorname{SDP}_d(I)\).
