children.top_down_role: Relaxation quality and rounding behavior across Boolean predicate families.

knowledge_statements.title: Predicate-Specific Approximation Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Approximation ratios induced by a fixed predicate, relaxation, and rounding rule.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix a Boolean predicate \(P\), an SDP relaxation \(S_P\), and a randomized rounding rule \(R_P\). Define its worst-case ratio by \[\alpha(P,S_P,R_P)=\inf_{I:\,\operatorname{SDP}_{S_P}(I)>0}\frac{\mathbb E[\operatorname{val}_I(R_P(Y_I))]}{\operatorname{SDP}_{S_P}(I)},\] where \(Y_I\) is an optimal SDP solution for the instance \(I\). Then every such instance satisfies \(\mathbb E[\operatorname{val}_I(R_P(Y_I))]\geq\alpha(P,S_P,R_P)\operatorname{SDP}_{S_P}(I)\). Consequently, changing the predicate, relaxation level, or rounding distribution can change the certified approximation regime.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A predicate-specific guarantee is the worst rounded-value-to-SDP ratio over its instances. It certifies that ratio uniformly, while different predicates or rounding rules may yield different constants.
assumptions_latex: All instances \(I\) use predicate \(P\) and nonnegative constraint weights.
The SDP optimum is attained and positive on instances included in the infimum.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb E[\operatorname{val}_I(R_P(Y_I))]\geq\alpha(P,S_P,R_P)\operatorname{SDP}_{S_P}(I)\).

notation.meaning: chosen SDP relaxation for predicate P

children.title: XOR Constraint Relaxations

knowledge_statements.title: XOR Constraint Relaxations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Vector SDP for weighted two-variable XOR equations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For constraints \(x_i x_j=b_{ij}\), where \(x_i,b_{ij}\in\{-1,1\}\) and weights \(w_{ij}\geq0\), the satisfied weight equals \(\sum_{ij}w_{ij}(1+b_{ij}x_ix_j)/2\). Replacing each sign \(x_i\) by a unit vector \(v_i\) gives the relaxation \[\max_{\|v_i\|=1}\sum_{ij}w_{ij}\frac{1+b_{ij}\langle v_i,v_j\rangle}{2}.\] Equivalently, optimize over \(X\succeq0\) with \(X_{ii}=1\), replacing \(\langle v_i,v_j\rangle\) by \(X_{ij}\). Rank-one matrices \(X=xx^{\mathsf T}\) recover exactly the Boolean feasible solutions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A weighted 2-XOR instance becomes an SDP by replacing each product of Boolean signs with an inner product of unit vectors. Rank-one feasible matrices are precisely Boolean assignments.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{OPT}_{\mathrm{2XOR}}\leq\operatorname{SDP}_{\mathrm{2XOR}}\).

unit-vector relaxation of Boolean variable i
Gram matrix of the relaxation vectors

knowledge_statements.title: Bilinear Sign Relaxations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Standard vector relaxation of a real bilinear sign optimization problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), define \(\operatorname{OPT}_{\pm}(A)=\max_{\varepsilon_i,\delta_j\in\{-1,1\}}\left|\sum_{i,j}A_{ij}\varepsilon_i\delta_j\right|\). Its vector relaxation is \[\operatorname{SDP}(A)=\sup_{d\geq1}\max_{u_i,v_j\in S^{d-1}}\left|\sum_{i,j}A_{ij}\langle u_i,v_j\rangle\right|.\] Taking all vectors collinear with a fixed unit vector embeds every sign solution into the vector feasible set. Hence \(\operatorname{OPT}_{\pm}(A)\leq\operatorname{SDP}(A)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Replace the two families of signs in a bilinear form by unit vectors and each sign product by an inner product. Collinear vectors recover every sign solution.
assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\).
All vectors belong to a common real Euclidean space.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{OPT}_{\pm}(A)\leq\operatorname{SDP}(A)\).

notation.meaning: unit sphere in real d-dimensional Euclidean space

children.title: XOR–Bilinear Reductions
children.top_down_role: Structural reductions connecting parity predicates with bilinear sign objectives.

knowledge_statements.title: XOR–Bilinear Reductions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Value-preserving affine correspondence between bipartite weighted 2-XOR objectives and bilinear sign objectives.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let a bipartite 2-XOR instance have left signs \(x_i\), right signs \(y_j\), constraint signs \(b_{ij}\), weights \(w_{ij}\geq0\), and total weight \(W=\sum_{i,j}w_{ij}>0\). Set \(A_{ij}=w_{ij}b_{ij}\). For every assignment, \[\frac{1}{W}\sum_{i,j}w_{ij}\frac{1+b_{ij}x_i y_j}{2}=\frac12+\frac{1}{2W}\sum_{i,j}A_{ij}x_i y_j.\] Define \(B(A)=\max_{x_i,y_j\in\{-1,1\}}\sum_{i,j}A_{ij}x_i y_j\). Global sign reversal of either variable family implies \(B(A)=\max_{x_i,y_j\in\{-1,1\}}\left|\sum_{i,j}A_{ij}x_i y_j\right|\), and hence \(\operatorname{OPT}_{\mathrm{2XOR}}=\tfrac12+B(A)/(2W)\). Likewise, with \(V(A)=\sup_{d\geq1}\max_{u_i,v_j\in S^{d-1}}\sum_{i,j}A_{ij}\langle u_i,v_j\rangle\), the vector relaxation satisfies \(\operatorname{SDP}_{\mathrm{2XOR}}=\tfrac12+V(A)/(2W)\), and \(V(A)\) is unchanged if the objective is placed inside absolute values.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A bipartite weighted 2-XOR objective equals one half plus its bilinear sign objective divided by twice the total weight. Global sign reversal makes the signed and absolute bilinear optima equal, and the same affine correspondence holds for the vector SDP.
assumptions_latex: The constraint graph is bipartite.
All vectors in the vector formulation lie in a common real Euclidean space and have unit norm.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{OPT}_{\mathrm{2XOR}}=\tfrac12+B(A)/(2W)\) and \(\operatorname{SDP}_{\mathrm{2XOR}}=\tfrac12+V(A)/(2W)\).

notation.meaning: left and right unit vectors in the SDP relaxation

knowledge_statements.title: Real Bilinear Grothendieck Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional real Grothendieck inequality for unrestricted bilinear coefficient matrices.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: There exists a universal finite constant \(K_G^{\mathbb R}\) such that, for every \(m,n\geq1\), every \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), every real Hilbert space \(H\), and all unit vectors \(u_1,\ldots,u_m,v_1,\ldots,v_n\in H\), \[\left|\sum_{i=1}^m\sum_{j=1}^n A_{ij}\langle u_i,v_j\rangle\right|\leq K_G^{\mathbb R}\max_{\varepsilon_i,\delta_j\in\{-1,1\}}\left|\sum_{i=1}^m\sum_{j=1}^n A_{ij}\varepsilon_i\delta_j\right|.\] Consequently, the real vector SDP has integrality gap at most \(K_G^{\mathbb R}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The real vector optimum of every bilinear form is at most the universal real Grothendieck constant times its sign optimum.
assumptions_latex: \(A\) is a finite real matrix.
All relaxation vectors are unit vectors in one real Hilbert space.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{SDP}(A)\leq K_G^{\mathbb R}\operatorname{OPT}_{\pm}(A)\).

notation.meaning: real Hilbert space containing the vectors

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The stated real Grothendieck inequality is standard, precise, and correctly classified as a theorem, but no authoritative theorem or section locator is supplied.

knowledge_statements.title: Positive-Semidefinite Grothendieck Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Real positive-semidefinite Grothendieck inequality with the sharp factor \(\pi/2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A\in\mathbb S_+^n\). Then \[\max_{d\geq1}\max_{u_1,\ldots,u_n\in S^{d-1}}\sum_{i,j=1}^n A_{ij}\langle u_i,u_j\rangle\leq\frac{\pi}{2}\max_{x\in\{-1,1\}^n}\sum_{i,j=1}^n A_{ij}x_i x_j.\] Thus the unit-vector SDP for a positive-semidefinite quadratic form has integrality gap at most \(\pi/2\), and an appropriate randomized rounding guarantee is at least \(2/\pi\) times the SDP value in expectation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a positive-semidefinite quadratic form, the unit-vector optimum is at most π/2 times the Boolean sign optimum, yielding a 2/π approximation regime.
assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb S_+^n\).
The vectors are real and have unit norm.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{SDP}_{\mathrm{psd}}(A)\leq(\pi/2)\operatorname{OPT}_{\pm}(A)\).

notation.meaning: cone of real n-by-n positive-semidefinite matrices
real unit sphere in dimension d

review_flags: authoritative positive-semidefinite Grothendieck theorem locator required

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The positive-semidefinite Grothendieck factor and associated rounding guarantee require an authoritative theorem locator, especially because the record asserts the sharp factor and an algorithmic expectation guarantee.

knowledge_statements.title: Rank-Constrained Grothendieck Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Monotonic hierarchy obtained by restricting the dimension of Grothendieck vectors.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) and integer \(r\geq1\), define \[\operatorname{SDP}_r(A)=\max_{u_i,v_j\in S^{r-1}}\left|\sum_{i,j}A_{ij}\langle u_i,v_j\rangle\right|.\] Then \(\operatorname{SDP}_1(A)=\operatorname{OPT}_{\pm}(A)\), \(\operatorname{SDP}_r(A)\leq\operatorname{SDP}_{r+1}(A)\), and \(\sup_{r\geq1}\operatorname{SDP}_r(A)=\operatorname{SDP}(A)\). If \(K_G^{\mathbb R}(r)\) denotes the least uniform constant satisfying \(\operatorname{SDP}_r(A)\leq K_G^{\mathbb R}(r)\operatorname{OPT}_{\pm}(A)\), then \(1=K_G^{\mathbb R}(1)\leq K_G^{\mathbb R}(r)\leq K_G^{\mathbb R}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Restricting relaxation vectors to dimension r yields nested optima: rank one is the sign problem, and increasing rank approaches the unrestricted Grothendieck SDP.
assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\).
\(r\) is a positive integer.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{OPT}_{\pm}(A)=\operatorname{SDP}_1(A)\leq\operatorname{SDP}_r(A)\leq\operatorname{SDP}(A)\).

notation.meaning: vector optimum restricted to dimension r

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The rank-restricted hierarchy and constants are internally consistent and fit the regime container, but no source with a specific locator is provided.

children.title: General Rounding Interfaces
children.top_down_role: Rounding families not confined to the Goemans–Williamson Max-Cut construction.

children.title: Gaussian Vector Rounding
children.top_down_role: Rounding based on Gaussian directions applied to semidefinite vector solutions.

knowledge_statements.title: Gaussian Vector Rounding
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Hyperplane rounding of unit SDP vectors using one standard Gaussian direction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input unit vectors \(v_1,\ldots,v_n\in\mathbb R^d\). Sample \(g\sim N(0,I_d)\) and output \(x_i=\operatorname{sgn}(\langle g,v_i\rangle)\), using any fixed convention at zero. For unit vectors \(u,v\), the rounded signs satisfy \[\mathbb E[\operatorname{sgn}(\langle g,u\rangle)\operatorname{sgn}(\langle g,v\rangle)]=\frac{2}{\pi}\arcsin(\langle u,v\rangle),\] equivalently \(\Pr[x_u\neq x_v]=\arccos(\langle u,v\rangle)/\pi\). The algorithm may stop after one sample or repeat independently and retain the best feasible rounded solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Project every SDP vector onto one Gaussian direction and take its sign. Pairwise rounded correlations follow the arcsine formula, enabling exact expected-objective calculations.
assumptions_latex: \(v_i\in\mathbb R^d\) and \(\|v_i\|_2=1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb E[x_i x_j]=(2/\pi)\arcsin(\langle v_i,v_j\rangle)\).

children.title: Random-Projection Rounding
children.top_down_role: Projection-based rounding using random lower-dimensional directions or subspaces.

knowledge_statements.title: Random-Projection Rounding
knowledge_statements.scope_note: General sign rounding from a sampled projection direction and optional thresholds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input vectors \(v_1,\ldots,v_n\in\mathbb R^d\), thresholds \(t_1,\ldots,t_n\in\mathbb R\), and a specified distribution \(D\) on \(\mathbb R^d\). Sample \(r\sim D\) and output \(x_i=1\) when \(\langle r,v_i\rangle\geq t_i\), and \(x_i=-1\) otherwise. For a randomized threshold vector, sample \((r,t)\) jointly from the prescribed law before applying the same rule. Repeat independently if requested and output either one feasible sample or the sampled solution having the greatest original objective value.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Sample a direction, project each relaxation vector, and threshold the resulting scalar. The direction and thresholds may follow any specified joint distribution.
assumptions_latex: \(D\) is a probability distribution on \(\mathbb R^d\).
The input vectors and thresholds are finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x=(x_1,\ldots,x_n)\in\{-1,1\}^n\) is a feasible rounded assignment.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The general projection-and-threshold algorithm is well-defined and correctly classified, but no inspectable source or locator is provided.

children.title: Projection-Distribution Regimes
children.top_down_role: Rounding behavior under alternative projection distributions and dimensional choices.

knowledge_statements.title: Projection-Distribution Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Kernel representation of pairwise correlations produced by sign projections.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D\) be a centrally symmetric distribution on \(\mathbb R^d\) assigning zero probability to every hyperplane through the origin. Define \(x(u)=\operatorname{sgn}(\langle r,u\rangle)\) for \(r\sim D\) and nonzero \(u\), and define the correlation kernel \(\kappa_D(u,v)=\mathbb E[x(u)x(v)]\). For any coefficients \(A_{ij}\) and vectors \(u_i,v_j\), \[\mathbb E\left[\sum_{i,j}A_{ij}x(u_i)x(v_j)\right]=\sum_{i,j}A_{ij}\kappa_D(u_i,v_j).\] Thus a projection-distribution regime is characterized, for pairwise objectives, by its induced kernel. For rotationally invariant \(D\), the kernel depends only on \(\langle u/\|u\|,v/\|v\|\rangle\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every sign-projection distribution induces a pairwise correlation kernel. Expected rounded bilinear objectives are obtained by replacing vector inner products with that kernel.
assumptions_latex: \(D\) is centrally symmetric.
\(D\) gives every origin-centered hyperplane probability zero.
All projected vectors are nonzero.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb E[\sum_{i,j}A_{ij}x(u_i)x(v_j)]=\sum_{i,j}A_{ij}\kappa_D(u_i,v_j)\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The induced-kernel representation and rotational-invariance specialization are mathematically coherent, but the record lacks a supporting citation with a specific locator.

children.title: Threshold Rounding
children.top_down_role: Rounding families based on scalar thresholds applied to relaxed coordinates.

knowledge_statements.title: Threshold Rounding
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Common-threshold rounding for scalar relaxation values in the interval \([-1,1]\).
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input scores \(s_1,\ldots,s_n\in[-1,1]\). Sample one threshold \(\tau\sim\operatorname{Unif}[-1,1]\) and output \(x_i=1\) if \(s_i\geq\tau\), and \(x_i=-1\) otherwise. Then \(\Pr[x_i=1]=(1+s_i)/2\), so \(\mathbb E[x_i]=s_i\). Moreover, because the same threshold is used for every coordinate, \(\Pr[x_i\neq x_j]=|s_i-s_j|/2\). The algorithm outputs the resulting Boolean vector, or repeats independently and retains the best feasible sample under the original objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Choose one uniform threshold and compare every scalar score with it. Each rounded sign has the prescribed mean, while pairwise disagreement equals half the score distance.
assumptions_latex: \(s_i\in[-1,1]\) for every \(i\).
A common threshold \(\tau\) is uniform on \([-1,1]\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb E[x_i]=s_i\) and \(\Pr[x_i\neq x_j]=|s_i-s_j|/2\).

notation.meaning: scalar relaxation score for variable i

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The common-threshold algorithm and its marginal and disagreement formulas are precise and consistent with the leaf, but no source or locator is supplied.

children.title: Sign Rounding
children.top_down_role: Rounding families mapping projected values to discrete signs.

knowledge_statements.title: Sign Rounding
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Gaussian hyperplane rounding of unit-vector SDP solutions to binary signs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given unit vectors \(v_1,\ldots,v_n\in\mathbb R^d\), sample \(g\sim N(0,I_d)\) and output \(X_i=\operatorname{sign}(\langle g,v_i\rangle)\in\{-1,1\}\), with \(\operatorname{sign}(0)=1\). The output satisfies \[\mathbb P(X_i\ne X_j)=\frac{\arccos(\langle v_i,v_j\rangle)}{\pi},\qquad \mathbb E[X_iX_j]=\frac{2}{\pi}\arcsin(\langle v_i,v_j\rangle).\] Thus every rounded pair is determined by the angle, or equivalently the Gram-matrix entry, of its SDP vectors.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A random Gaussian hyperplane converts SDP vectors to signs; pairwise disagreement equals their angle divided by pi.
assumptions_latex: \(g\) is a standard Gaussian vector independent of the SDP solution.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(X\in\{-1,1\}^n\) and \(\mathbb P(X_i\ne X_j)=\arccos(\langle v_i,v_j\rangle)/\pi\).

notation.meaning: unit SDP vector for variable i

children.title: Threshold–Sign Equivalence Regimes
children.top_down_role: Settings where threshold and sign views coincide or lead to different guarantees.

knowledge_statements.title: Threshold–Sign Equivalence Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact equivalence for binary rounding obtained by thresholding a common real-valued score.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Z_i\) be any real-valued score and let \(\tau_i\in\mathbb R\). With ties assigned to the upper outcome, threshold rounding and sign rounding obey \[B_i=\mathbf 1\{Z_i\ge\tau_i\}=\frac{1+X_i}{2},\qquad X_i=2B_i-1=\operatorname{sign}(Z_i-\tau_i).\] Hence the two interfaces are distributionally identical whenever they use the same joint score vector and the same tie convention. A zero-threshold sign rule is the special case \(\tau_i=0\); unequal thresholds are absorbed by translating each score.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Binary thresholding and sign rounding are identical after translating the score and mapping zero-one outputs to minus-one/plus-one outputs.
assumptions_latex: \((Z_1,\ldots,Z_n)\) is a jointly distributed real-valued score vector.
Ties \(Z_i=\tau_i\) are assigned consistently to \(B_i=1\) and \(X_i=1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(B_i=(1+X_i)/2\) and \(X_i=2B_i-1\) almost surely for every \(i\).

notation.meaning: zero-one and sign encodings of the same outcome

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: direct algebraic equivalence of binary encodings

children.title: Dependent Rounding
children.top_down_role: Rounding schemes coordinating discrete choices through controlled dependence.

knowledge_statements.title: Dependent Rounding
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pairwise dependent rounding preserving marginals and an integral cardinality sum.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input \(x\in[0,1]^n\) with \(\sum_i x_i=k\in\mathbb Z\). While two coordinates \(x_i,x_j\) are fractional, set \(\alpha=\min\{1-x_i,x_j\}\) and \(\beta=\min\{x_i,1-x_j\}\). Replace \(x\) by \(x+\alpha(e_i-e_j)\) with probability \(\beta/(\alpha+\beta)\), and by \(x-\beta(e_i-e_j)\) otherwise. When no fractional pair remains, output \(X=x\). The procedure terminates with \(X\in\{0,1\}^n\), preserves \(\sum_iX_i=k\) surely, and satisfies \(\mathbb E[X_i]=x_i^{(0)}\) for every coordinate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Random pairwise transfers make coordinates integral while preserving every marginal expectation and the exact cardinality sum.
assumptions_latex: \(\sum_i x_i^{(0)}=k\in\mathbb Z\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(X\in\{0,1\}^n\), \(\sum_iX_i=k\) almost surely, and \(\mathbb E[X_i]=x_i^{(0)}\).

children.title: Constraint-Preserving Rounding
children.top_down_role: Rounding schemes designed to retain balance, assignment, or feasibility constraints.

knowledge_statements.title: Constraint-Preserving Rounding
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Rounding kernels supported on the integral feasible set while retaining prescribed first moments.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P\subseteq[0,1]^n\) be a relaxation and let \(F=P\cap\{0,1\}^n\) be its integral feasible set. A randomized kernel \(R\) is constraint-preserving at \(x\in P\) if \[\mathbb P(R(x)\in F)=1.\] It is also marginal-preserving at \(x\) if \(\mathbb E[R(x)]=x\). If the equality \(Ay=b\) holds for every \(y\in F\), constraint preservation implies \(AR(x)=b\) almost surely. If instead only marginal preservation is known and \(Ax=b\), then \(A\mathbb E[R(x)]=b\), which does not by itself imply samplewise feasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Constraint-preserving rounding outputs only integral feasible points. Marginal preservation is an additional expectation condition and, even when the fractional point satisfies a linear equality, does not by itself ensure that every rounded outcome satisfies it.
assumptions_latex: \(P\subseteq[0,1]^n\) and \(F=P\cap\{0,1\}^n\ne\varnothing\).
\(R(x)\) is a measurable random vector for each \(x\in P\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(R\) preserves constraints at \(x\) exactly when \(\mathbb P(R(x)\in F)=1\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: support-based definition of feasibility preservation and linearity of expectation
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

children.title: Dependence–Feasibility Tradeoffs
children.top_down_role: Tradeoffs between correlation control, marginal preservation, and discrete feasibility.

knowledge_statements.title: Dependence–Feasibility Tradeoffs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact cardinality feasibility forces dependence unless the rounded solution is deterministic.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X_1,\ldots,X_n\in\{0,1\}\) satisfy \(\sum_iX_i=k\) almost surely. Then \[0=\operatorname{Var}\!\left(\sum_iX_i\right)=\sum_i\operatorname{Var}(X_i)+2\sum_{i<j}\operatorname{Cov}(X_i,X_j).\] If at least one coordinate is nonconstant, the variance sum is positive, so some pair has negative covariance. Consequently, mutually independent nondegenerate coordinates cannot preserve an exact cardinality constraint; dependence is necessary to combine nontrivial marginals with samplewise feasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Any nontrivial rounding that preserves an exact cardinality must introduce dependence, including negative covariance between at least one pair.
assumptions_latex: \(\sum_iX_i=k\) almost surely for a fixed integer \(k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If some \(\operatorname{Var}(X_i)>0\), then \(\operatorname{Cov}(X_i,X_j)<0\) for at least one pair \(i<j\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: variance identity gives the tradeoff directly

knowledge_statements.title: Local-Distribution Rounding
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Seed-conditioned rounding from a consistent hierarchy of local distributions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(V\) be a finite variable set with finite alphabet \(\Omega\), and suppose consistent distributions \(\mu_T\) are available for every \(T\subseteq V\) of size at most \(r\). Choose a seed set \(S\) with \(|S|<r\), sample \(X_S=\sigma\sim\mu_S\), and, conditional on \(\mu_S(\sigma)>0\), independently sample each \(X_i\), \(i\notin S\), according to \[\mathbb P(X_i=a\mid X_S=\sigma)=\frac{\mu_{S\cup\{i\}}(\sigma,a)}{\mu_S(\sigma)},\qquad a\in\Omega.\] Output the resulting assignment \(X\in\Omega^V\). Each one-variable conditional marginal supplied by the hierarchy is preserved.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Sample a seed assignment from the local hierarchy distributions, then round the remaining variables independently from their conditional local marginals.
assumptions_latex: The family \((\mu_T)_{|T|\le r}\) is nonnegative, normalized, and marginally consistent.
\(|S|<r\), so every distribution \(\mu_{S\cup\{i\}}\) used by the rule exists.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(X\in\Omega^V\) and \(\mathcal L(X_i\mid X_S=\sigma)=\mu_{i\mid S=\sigma}\) for every \(i\notin S\).

notation.meaning: local distribution on variables in T

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: canonical seed-and-condition hierarchy rounding interface
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

knowledge_statements.title: Correlation-Reduction Rounding
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Adaptive conditioning followed by independent rounding after residual local correlations become small.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given consistent local distributions and weights \(w_{ij}\ge0\) with \(\sum_{i<j}w_{ij}=1\), maintain a conditioned seed assignment \(X_S=\sigma\). Define \[D(S,\sigma)=\sum_{i<j}w_{ij}\left\|\mu_{ijrack\mid S=\sigma}-\mu_{i\mid S=\sigma}\otimes\mu_{j\mid S=\sigma}\right\|_{\mathrm{TV}}.\] While \(D(S,\sigma)>\varepsilon\), select an unconditioned variable according to a specified correlation-reduction rule, sample it from its conditional marginal, and add it to \(S\). Upon stopping, independently sample all remaining variables from their conditional marginals and output the combined assignment. The stopping certificate is \(D(S,\sigma)\le\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Condition adaptively on selected variables until weighted residual pairwise dependence is small, then independently round the remaining conditional marginals.
assumptions_latex: All local distributions required after each conditioning step are available and consistent.
The variable-selection rule and tolerance \(\varepsilon\ge0\) are fixed in advance.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: At normal termination, \(D(S,\sigma)\le\varepsilon\), and remaining coordinates are sampled from the corresponding conditional marginals.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The expression containing “mu_{ijrack}” is malformed, the coordinate-selection rule is unspecified, and no progress or hierarchy-depth condition ensures the claimed stopping certificate. A precise sourced variant is required before the algorithm can be repaired reliably.

knowledge_statements.title: Spectral-Conditioning Rounding
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditioning guided by the leading eigenvector of the residual covariance matrix.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For binary variables represented by consistent local distributions, maintain a seed event \(X_S=\sigma\) and its conditional covariance matrix \(C\) on unconditioned coordinates. If \(\lambda_{\max}(C)\le\varepsilon\), independently sample the remaining conditional marginals and stop. Otherwise choose a unit leading eigenvector \(u\), select an unconditioned coordinate \(q\in\arg\max_i |u_i|\sqrt{C_{ii}}\), sample \(X_q\) from its conditional marginal, add \(q\) and its value to the seed, and recompute \(C\). The output is a complete binary assignment; the spectral stopping certificate is \(\lambda_{\max}(C)\le\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repeatedly condition on a coordinate exposed by the leading residual covariance direction, then round independently once the spectral dependence is small.
assumptions_latex: Conditional first and second moments remain available at every seed size reached.
\(C\) is the conditional covariance matrix of the unconditioned binary variables.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The procedure outputs \(X\in\{0,1\}^V\); normal early termination certifies \(\lambda_{\max}(C)\le\varepsilon\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The leading-eigenvector coordinate rule is a specific spectral-conditioning variant, but no source or progress argument supports it, and the available hierarchy depth is not quantified. Source evidence is needed to determine the correct algorithmic statement.

knowledge_statements.title: Constraint Loss after Rounding
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Independent marginal rounding generally destroys exact linear equalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x\in[0,1]^n\) satisfy \(\sum_i x_i=k\in\mathbb Z\), and independently round \(X_i\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(x_i)\). Although \(\mathbb E[\sum_iX_i]=k\), \[\operatorname{Var}\!\left(\sum_iX_i\right)=\sum_i x_i(1-x_i).\] If any \(x_i\) is fractional, this variance is positive, so \(\mathbb P(\sum_iX_i\ne k)>0\). Thus preservation of the equality in expectation does not imply feasibility of individual rounded outcomes; exact preservation requires a coupled rule or a repair step.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Independent rounding preserves a cardinality equality only in expectation and violates it with positive probability whenever any marginal is fractional.
assumptions_latex: \(x\in[0,1]^n\) and \(\sum_i x_i=k\in\mathbb Z\).
The variables \(X_i\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(x_i)\) are mutually independent.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If some \(x_i\in(0,1)\), then \(\mathbb P(\sum_iX_i\ne k)>0\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: Bernoulli variance identity gives a sharp failure condition

knowledge_statements.title: Correlation Loss after Rounding
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Marginal-only independent rounding discards prescribed pairwise moments.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose a relaxation prescribes binary marginals \(x_i=\mathbb E[Y_i]\) and pair moments \(m_{ij}=\mathbb E[Y_iY_j]\). Independent marginal rounding \(X_i\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(x_i)\) forces \[\mathbb E[X_iX_j]=x_ix_j,\qquad \operatorname{Cov}(X_i,X_j)=0.\] Therefore every target correlation \(m_{ij}-x_ix_j\ne0\) is lost. For example, when \(x_i=x_j=1/2\) and the target has \(Y_i=Y_j\) almost surely, \(m_{ij}=1/2\), whereas independent rounding gives \(\mathbb E[X_iX_j]=1/4\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Independent marginal rounding sets all cross-covariances to zero and can halve the joint-one probability of perfectly correlated balanced variables.
assumptions_latex: \(Y_i,Y_j\in\{0,1\}\) have prescribed first and second moments.
The rounded coordinates \(X_i\) are sampled independently with \(\mathbb E[X_i]=x_i\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The pair-moment error is \(\mathbb E[X_iX_j]-m_{ij}=x_ix_j-m_{ij}\).

children.title: Rounding Variance Regimes
children.top_down_role: Regimes where dispersion in rounded objectives or constraints limits reliability.

knowledge_statements.title: Rounding Variance Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Variance of a rounded linear statistic is governed by pairwise covariance structure.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For square-integrable rounded coordinates and coefficients \(a_i\in\mathbb R\), the statistic \(L=\sum_i a_iX_i\) satisfies \[\operatorname{Var}(L)=\sum_i a_i^2\operatorname{Var}(X_i)+2\sum_{i<j}a_ia_j\operatorname{Cov}(X_i,X_j).\] For nonnegative \(a_i\), pairwise nonpositive covariance never exceeds the corresponding independent-marginal variance. An exact constraint \(L=b\) gives zero variance. At the opposite extreme, if \(X_i=Y\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(1/2)\) and \(a_i=1\), then \(\operatorname{Var}(L)=n^2/4\), showing quadratic variance under perfect positive dependence.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Negative dependence suppresses variance, exact constraints eliminate it, and perfect positive dependence can make a rounded sum's variance quadratic in dimension.
assumptions_latex: Each \(X_i\) is square-integrable.
The comparison with independence uses the same one-dimensional marginals and coefficients \(a_i\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{Var}(L)\) equals its marginal variance sum plus the weighted covariance contribution.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: covariance expansion and explicit extremal examples

children.title: Rounding Tail-Risk Regimes
children.top_down_role: Regimes dominated by rare but consequential rounding outcomes.

knowledge_statements.title: Rounding Tail-Risk Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pairwise independence alone does not yield Chernoff-type concentration.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(q\) be a prime power, choose \(A,B\) uniformly and independently from \(\mathbb F_q\), and for each \(t\in\mathbb F_q\) set \(X_t=\mathbf 1\{At+B=0\}\). The variables are pairwise independent with \(\mathbb P(X_t=1)=1/q\), and \(S=\sum_tX_t\) has \(\mathbb E[S]=1\). Nevertheless, \[\mathbb P(S=q)=\mathbb P(A=0,B=0)=q^{-2}.\] Thus a deviation of order \(q\) retains polynomial probability; pairwise independence or covariance control alone cannot support a Chernoff-type exponentially small tail bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A pairwise-independent Bernoulli family can have a polynomially likely all-one event, so covariance control alone does not guarantee exponential concentration.
assumptions_latex: \(q\) is a prime power.
\(A\) and \(B\) are independent and uniform on \(\mathbb F_q\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb E[S]=1\) but \(\mathbb P(S=q)=q^{-2}\), despite pairwise independence.

notation.meaning: indicator of a random affine root at t
number of roots counted over the field

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: explicit finite-field construction is directly checkable

children.title: Concentration Failure Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Structural settings where standard concentration behavior becomes insufficient.

assumptions_latex: \(Z\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(p)\), with no independence requirement imposed on the rounded coordinates.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{Var}(\bar X_n)=p(1-p)\) for every \(n\), so concentration cannot improve with dimension.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Concrete failure of dimension-dependent concentration when rounded coordinates may be perfectly dependent.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X_i=Z\) for every \(i\in\{1,\ldots,n\}\), where \(Z\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(p)\). Then \(\bar X_n=Z\), \(\mathbb E[\bar X_n]=p\), and \(\operatorname{Var}(\bar X_n)=p(1-p)\). Moreover,
\[
\mathbb P\!\left(\left|\bar X_n-p\right|\ge \min\{p,1-p\}\right)=1.
\]
Thus marginally valid rounding without a dependence or bounded-difference hypothesis admits no tail bound whose deviation scale vanishes as \(n\to\infty\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Perfect dependence can keep a rounded average equal to one Bernoulli variable, so its variance and nontrivial deviation probability do not decrease with dimension.
knowledge_statements.title: Concentration Failure Boundaries

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The Bernoulli counterexample is mathematically correct and the failure_boundary kind fits the terminal container, but no source is cited. A specific source locator supporting dependence-driven failure of concentration is required.

source_refs.locator: 3.1.2 The truncated moment problem p. 56
source_refs.source_title: Moments, Positive Polynomials and Their Applications

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A truncated moment sequence of order \(2d\) is a vector
\[
y=(y_\alpha)_{\alpha\in\mathbb N^n,\ |\alpha|\le 2d}\in\mathbb R^{\binom{n+2d}{2d}}.
\]
It induces the linear functional \(L_y:\mathbb R[x]_{2d}\to\mathbb R\) defined, for \(p(x)=\sum_{|\alpha|\le 2d}p_\alpha x^\alpha\), by
\[
L_y(p)=\sum_{|\alpha|\le 2d}p_\alpha y_\alpha.
\]
If a finite Borel measure \(\mu\) satisfies \(y_\alpha=\int x^\alpha\,d\mu\), then \(y\) is represented by \(\mu\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A truncated moment sequence records putative moments through degree 2d and defines a linear functional on all polynomials of that degree.
knowledge_statements.title: Truncated Moment Sequences

source_witnesses.locator: 3.1.2 The truncated moment problem p. 56

assumptions_latex: \(n,d\in\mathbb N\), \(\mathbb R[x]=\mathbb R[x_1,\ldots,x_n]\), and \(y=(y_\alpha)_{|\alpha|\le 2d}\) is a real truncated sequence.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(M_d(y)\succeq0\) if and only if \(L_y(q^2)\ge0\) for every \(q\in\mathbb R[x]_d\).

notation.meaning: Coefficient vector of q in the monomial basis

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Positive-semidefinite constraint for the order-\(d\) monomial basis.

source_refs.locator: 3.2.1 Moment and localizing matrix p. 58
source_refs.source_title: Moments, Positive Polynomials and Their Applications

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The order-\(d\) moment matrix associated with \(y\) is the symmetric matrix indexed by multi-indices of degree at most \(d\), with entries
\[
[M_d(y)]_{\alpha,\beta}=y_{\alpha+\beta}.
\]
For \(q(x)=\sum_{|\alpha|\le d}q_\alpha x^\alpha\), let \(\mathbf q=(q_\alpha)_{|\alpha|\le d}\) be its coefficient vector. Then
\[
\mathbf q^\mathsf{T}M_d(y)\mathbf q=L_y(q(x)^2).
\]
Consequently, the moment-matrix constraint is \(M_d(y)\succeq0\), equivalently \(L_y(q^2)\ge0\) for every \(q\in\mathbb R[x]_d\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The moment matrix is positive semidefinite exactly when the truncated moment functional is nonnegative on the square of every polynomial of degree at most d.
knowledge_statements.title: Moment-Matrix Constraints

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(M_{d-r}(gy)\succeq0\) if and only if \(L_y(gq^2)\ge0\) for every \(q\in\mathbb R[x]_{d-r}\).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The localizing matrix of \(g\) with respect to \(y\), indexed by \(|\alpha|,|\beta|\le d-r\), is defined by
\[
[M_{d-r}(gy)]_{\alpha,\beta}=L_y(gx^{\alpha+\beta})=\sum_\gamma g_\gamma y_{\alpha+\beta+\gamma}.
\]
For \(q(x)=\sum_{|\alpha|\le d-r}q_\alpha x^\alpha\), let \(\mathbf q=(q_\alpha)_{|\alpha|\le d-r}\). Then
\[
\mathbf q^\mathsf{T}M_{d-r}(gy)\mathbf q=L_y(gq^2).
\]
Hence \(M_{d-r}(gy)\succeq0\) if and only if \(L_y(gq^2)\ge0\) for every \(q\in\mathbb R[x]_{d-r}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A localizing matrix is positive semidefinite exactly when the moment functional is nonnegative on g times the square of every polynomial of degree at most d-r.
knowledge_statements.title: Localizing-Matrix Constraints

source_refs.locator: 5.3 Constrained Polynomial Optimization: Semidefinite Relaxations p. 117
source_refs.source_title: Moments, Positive Polynomials and Their Applications

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Define the degree-\(2d\) truncated ideal space by
\[
I_{2d}=\left\{\sum_{j=1}^s q_jh_j:\ q_j\in\mathbb R[x],\ \deg(q_jh_j)\le2d\right\}.
\]
The polynomial ideal constraints on \(y\) require \(L_y(p)=0\) for every \(p\in I_{2d}\). Equivalently, for each \(j\),
\[
L_y(x^\alpha h_j)=0
\]
for every multi-index \(\alpha\) satisfying \(|\alpha|+\deg(h_j)\le2d\). These are homogeneous linear equations in the entries of \(y\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At order d, ideal constraints require the moment functional to annihilate every degree-feasible polynomial multiple of each equality generator.
knowledge_statements.title: Polynomial Ideal Constraints

children.title: Polynomial Equality Constraints
children.top_down_role: Moment restrictions induced directly by polynomial equalities.

assumptions_latex: \(n,d,m,s\in\mathbb N\), \(g_1,\ldots,g_m,h_1,\ldots,h_s\in\mathbb R[x_1,\ldots,x_n]\), and \(K=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:g_i(x)\ge0\ (i=1,\ldots,m),\ h_j(x)=0\ (j=1,\ldots,s)\}\).
\(y=(y_\alpha)_{|\alpha|\le2d}\) is real and has associated functional \(L_y\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Each equality \(h_j=0\) is encoded by \(L_y(x^\alpha h_j)=0\) for every \(j\in\{1,\ldots,s\}\) and every \(\alpha\in\mathbb N^n\) satisfying \(|\alpha|+\deg(h_j)\le2d\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Moment-relaxation encoding of polynomial equalities, without asserting existence of a representing measure.

source_refs.locator: 5.3 Constrained Polynomial Optimization: Semidefinite Relaxations p. 117
source_refs.source_title: Moments, Positive Polynomials and Their Applications

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For every \(j\in\{1,\ldots,s\}\), the order-\(d\) moment relaxation encodes the equality \(h_j=0\) by imposing
\[
L_y(x^\alpha h_j)=0
\]
for every \(\alpha\in\mathbb N^n\) satisfying \(|\alpha|+\deg(h_j)\le2d\). If \(y\) has a representing measure \(\mu\) supported on \(K\), these equations are necessary because
\[
L_y(x^\alpha h_j)=\int x^\alpha h_j(x)\,d\mu(x)=0.
\]
The linear equations alone do not assert that such a representing measure exists.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each polynomial equality is encoded by linear moment equations for all degree-admissible monomial multiples; these equations are necessary for a measure supported on the equality set but do not establish that such a measure exists.
knowledge_statements.title: Polynomial Equality Constraints

children.top_down_role: Comparison of algebraic ideal encodings with explicit equality representations.

assumptions_latex: \(n,d,s\in\mathbb N\), \(h_1,\ldots,h_s\in\mathbb R[x_1,\ldots,x_n]\), and \(I=\langle h_1,\ldots,h_s\rangle\).
\(y=(y_\alpha)_{|\alpha|\le2d}\) is real and \(L_y\) is its functional on \(\mathbb R[x]_{2d}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L_y(p)=0\) for every \(p\in I_{2d}\) if and only if \(L_y(x^\alpha h_j)=0\) for every \(j\in\{1,\ldots,s\}\) and every degree-admissible \(\alpha\in\mathbb N^n\).

notation.meaning: Ideal generated by the equality polynomials

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-degree equivalence between annihilation of the termwise degree-truncated generated ideal space and generator-based equality equations.

source_refs.locator: 5.3 Constrained Polynomial Optimization: Semidefinite Relaxations p. 117
source_refs.source_title: Moments, Positive Polynomials and Their Applications

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Define
\[
I_{2d}=\left\{\sum_{j=1}^s q_jh_j:q_j\in\mathbb R[x]\ \text{and}\ \deg(q_jh_j)\le2d\ \text{for every}\ j\right\}.
\]
Then the following conditions are equivalent: \(L_y(p)=0\) for every \(p\in I_{2d}\); \(L_y(qh_j)=0\) for every \(j\in\{1,\ldots,s\}\) and every \(q\in\mathbb R[x]\) satisfying \(\deg(qh_j)\le2d\); and \(L_y(x^\alpha h_j)=0\) for every \(j\in\{1,\ldots,s\}\) and every \(\alpha\in\mathbb N^n\) satisfying \(|\alpha|+\deg(h_j)\le2d\). Thus the generator-multiple equations encode annihilation of the degree-truncated generated ideal space.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Annihilating the degree-truncated span of the equality-generator multiples is equivalent to imposing every degree-admissible generator-multiple moment equation.
knowledge_statements.title: Ideal–Equality Encoding Correspondence

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The quadratic module generated by \(g=(g_1,\ldots,g_m)\) is
\[
Q(g)=\left\{\sigma_0+\sum_{i=1}^m\sigma_i g_i:\sigma_i\in\Sigma[x]\right\}.
\]
A displayed identity
\[
f=\sigma_0+\sum_{i=1}^m\sigma_i g_i
\]
with sums of squares \(\sigma_i\) is a quadratic-module certificate. For every \(x\in K\), each \(\sigma_i(x)\ge0\) and each \(g_i(x)\ge0\); hence the identity certifies \(f(x)\ge0\) on \(K\). Degree bounds on the summands produce a finite semidefinite certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Expressing a polynomial as an SOS plus SOS-weighted defining inequalities gives a semidefinite-verifiable certificate of nonnegativity on the feasible set.
knowledge_statements.title: Quadratic-Module Certificates

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The order-\(d\) primal moment relaxation is
\[
p_d=\inf_y\left\{L_y(f):y_0=1,\ M_d(y)\succeq0,\ M_{d-r_i}(g_i y)\succeq0,\ L_y(x^\alpha h_j)=0\right\},
\]
where the equality equations range over \(|\alpha|+\deg(h_j)\le2d\). Every point \(x\in K\) generates the feasible sequence \(y_\alpha=x^\alpha\), whose objective is \(f(x)\). Consequently,
\[
p_d\le\inf_{x\in K}f(x).
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The primal relaxation minimizes the objective moment subject to moment, localizing, normalization, and equality equations, producing a lower bound on polynomial optimization.
knowledge_statements.title: Primal Moment View

The order \(d\) permits every term in the certificate to have degree at most \(2d\).
When equality of finite optimal values is asserted, at least one finite-dimensional primal or dual SDP satisfies the appropriate Slater condition.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(q_d\le p_d\le\inf_{x\in K}f(x)\), and \(q_d=p_d\) under the stated Slater and finiteness hypotheses.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The conic dual of the order-\(d\) moment relaxation is
\[
q_d=\sup_{\gamma\in\mathbb R}\left\{\gamma:f-\gamma=\sigma_0+\sum_{i=1}^m\sigma_i g_i+\sum_{j=1}^s\phi_jh_j,\ \deg(\sigma_0)\le2d,\ \deg(\sigma_i g_i)\le2d,\ \deg(\phi_jh_j)\le2d\right\},
\]
where \(\sigma_0,\ldots,\sigma_m\in\Sigma[x]\) and \(\phi_1,\ldots,\phi_s\in\mathbb R[x]\). Each feasible identity certifies \(f(x)\ge\gamma\) on \(K\), so weak duality gives
\[
q_d\le p_d\le\inf_{x\in K}f(x).
\]
If one finite-dimensional SDP side satisfies the appropriate Slater condition and the relevant optimal value is finite, standard conic strong duality gives \(q_d=p_d\), with the corresponding standard attainment conclusion for the opposite side.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The dual maximizes a lower bound certified by a degree-bounded SOS-plus-ideal identity. Weak duality places this value below the primal moment value and the polynomial minimum, while suitable Slater regularity removes the finite-order duality gap.
knowledge_statements.title: Dual Positivity-Certificate View

children.title: Moment–SOS Duality Gaps
children.top_down_role: Regimes where primal moment values and dual certificate values differ.

knowledge_statements.title: Moment–SOS Duality Gaps
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-order moment–SOS SDP duality; this does not assert infinite-dimensional measure-cone strong duality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix a relaxation order \(d\). Let \(p_d\) be the infimum of the truncated moment SDP and \(q_d\) the supremum of its SOS dual. Then \(q_d\le p_d\). The order has a positive duality gap exactly when \(q_d<p_d\). If the moment SDP is strictly feasible and \(q_d\) is finite, the SOS optimum is attained and \(q_d=p_d\). Symmetrically, strict feasibility of the SOS-side conic formulation and finiteness of \(p_d\) imply primal attainment and equality. Thus a finite positive gap requires failure of both applicable Slater conditions, although such failure alone does not imply a gap.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At a fixed order, the SOS bound cannot exceed the moment bound. A positive gap requires failure of both applicable strict-feasibility conditions, while either Slater condition yields equality and opposite-side attainment.
assumptions_latex: The order-\(d\) moment relaxation and its SOS dual are feasible finite-dimensional semidefinite programs.
Their optimal values are denoted by \(p_d\) and \(q_d\), respectively, with the SOS problem posed as a maximization.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Weak duality gives \(q_d\le p_d\). A positive order-\(d\) duality gap is precisely \(q_d<p_d\). Either applicable Slater condition, together with finiteness of the opposite value, gives \(q_d=p_d\) and opposite-side attainment.

notation.meaning: Optimal value of the order-d truncated moment minimization SDP.
Optimal value of the order-d SOS maximization SDP.

children.title: Primal Attainment Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Conditions governing existence or loss of optimal primal moment solutions.

knowledge_statements.title: Primal Attainment Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A sufficient finite-order compactness boundary for primal attainment, using an explicit redundant ball constraint.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(y=(y_\alpha)_{|\alpha|\le 2d}\) satisfy \(y_0=1\), the order-\(d\) moment constraint, and all required localizing constraints. If one localizing polynomial is \(R^2-\lVert x\rVert_2^2\), and its truncation is sufficient to bound every retained moment coordinate, then the feasible set is closed and bounded in a finite-dimensional space, hence compact. Whenever it is nonempty, the linear objective \(L_y(f)\) attains its minimum. If no constraint or derived relation controls all retained moments, the feasible set may be unbounded, and primal attainment is not guaranteed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A normalized feasible moment relaxation attains its minimum when a ball localizing constraint bounds every retained moment. Without such control, the feasible set may be unbounded and attainment can fail.
assumptions_latex: The order-\(d\) moment SDP is feasible.
Its constraints include \(y_0=1\) and the localizing condition for \(R^2-\lVert x\rVert_2^2\ge 0\), with sufficient truncation degree.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The feasible truncated-moment set is compact, so every linear moment objective \(L_y(f)\) attains its finite minimum. Closedness alone does not ensure attainment without a constraint or consequence bounding all retained moment coordinates.

notation.meaning: Truncated moment sequence indexed through degree 2d.

children.title: Dual Attainment Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Conditions governing existence or loss of optimal dual positivity certificates.

knowledge_statements.title: Dual Attainment Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Slater-type sufficient boundary for attainment of the finite-order SOS dual.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At order \(d\), write the SOS dual as \(q_d=\sup\{\gamma\in\mathbb R:f-\gamma\in Q_d(g)\}\). If the primal moment SDP has a feasible point for which every semidefinite block not forced onto a proper face is positive definite, and if \(q_d\) is finite, then there exists \(\gamma_d\) such that \(f-\gamma_d\in Q_d(g)\), \(\gamma_d=q_d\), and \(q_d=p_d\). When primal strict feasibility is lost, this condition supplies neither attainment of \(q_d\) nor absence of a gap; facial reduction or a separate closedness argument is then required.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Strict feasibility of the moment SDP and a finite SOS value guarantee that the SOS supremum is attained with no gap. At boundary-feasible orders, attainment requires additional analysis.
assumptions_latex: The finite-order moment SDP is strictly feasible relative to its unreduced semidefinite blocks or an identified minimal face.
The associated SOS dual has a finite optimal value.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The SOS dual supremum is attained and equals the moment optimum. Failure of strict moment feasibility alone determines neither dual attainment nor equality.

notation.meaning: Order-d quadratic module used by the SOS dual.

knowledge_statements.title: Gap–Attainment Interaction Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Logical interaction of finite gap and primal or dual attainment at one relaxation order.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For finite values define \(\delta_d=p_d-q_d\ge 0\), and let \(a_d^{\mathrm P},a_d^{\mathrm D}\in\{0,1\}\) record primal and dual attainment. Zero gap, \(\delta_d=0\), does not by itself imply either form of attainment. Primal Slater regularity forces \(\delta_d=0\) and \(a_d^{\mathrm D}=1\); dual Slater regularity forces \(\delta_d=0\) and \(a_d^{\mathrm P}=1\). Hence \(\delta_d>0\) implies failure of both applicable Slater conditions, but does not by itself determine \(a_d^{\mathrm P}\) or \(a_d^{\mathrm D}\). Attainment and zero gap are therefore distinct properties.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Gap status and attainment are distinct. Slater regularity forces zero gap and opposite-side attainment; without it, zero gap need not imply attainment, while a positive gap does not determine attainment.
assumptions_latex: The order-\(d\) primal and dual values \(p_d\) and \(q_d\) are finite.
Weak duality is oriented as \(q_d\le p_d\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The status is described by \(\delta_d=p_d-q_d\) and the two attainment indicators. Either applicable Slater condition forces \(\delta_d=0\) and opposite-side attainment. If \(\delta_d>0\), both applicable Slater conditions fail, but the attainment indicators are not determined by the gap alone.

notation.meaning: Indicator that the moment infimum is attained.
Indicator that the SOS supremum is attained.

knowledge_statements.title: Dense Lasserre Hierarchy
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dense Putinar-type hierarchy for global polynomial minimization on an Archimedean basic closed set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Set \(g_0=1\) and \(d_0=\max_{0\le j\le m}\lceil\deg(g_j)/2\rceil\). For each \(d\ge d_0\), form \(Q_d(g)=\{\sum_{j=0}^m\sigma_jg_j:\sigma_j\text{ is SOS},\ \deg(\sigma_jg_j)\le 2d\}\) and compute \(\rho_d=\sup\{\gamma\in\mathbb R:f-\gamma\in Q_d(g)\}\), equivalently through its moment-SDP dual. Increase \(d\) until the selected stopping criterion is met. Then \(\rho_d\le\rho_{d+1}\le f^*\); under the Archimedean assumption, \(\rho_d\to f^*\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At each order, the dense hierarchy places the objective residual in a degree-truncated quadratic module using every variable and constraint. Its lower bounds increase to the global minimum under Archimedeanity.
assumptions_latex: The polynomial problem is \(f^*=\inf\{f(x):g_j(x)\ge 0,\ j=1,\ldots,m\}\).
The quadratic module generated by \(g=(g_1,\ldots,g_m)\) is Archimedean.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The bounds satisfy \(\rho_d\le\rho_{d+1}\le f^*\) and \(\rho_d\uparrow f^*\). Each order uses all variables and constraint polynomials in one dense truncated quadratic module.

knowledge_statements.title: Equality-Constrained Lasserre Hierarchy
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Putinar hierarchy in a polynomial quotient represented by explicit truncated equality-ideal terms.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For equalities \(h_1=\cdots=h_s=0\), define \(I_{2d}(h)=\{\sum_{k=1}^s\phi_kh_k:\deg(\phi_kh_k)\le 2d\}\), and let \(Q_d(g)\) be the truncated quadratic module of the inequalities. The equality-constrained order-\(d\) bound is \(\rho_d=\sup\{\gamma\in\mathbb R:f-\gamma\in I_{2d}(h)+Q_d(g)\}\). Its moment dual imposes \(L_y(h_kx^\alpha)=0\) whenever \(\deg(h_kx^\alpha)\le 2d\), together with the moment and localizing positive-semidefinite constraints. Under Archimedeanity modulo \(I(h)\), \(\rho_d\uparrow f^*\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Equality constraints enter the Lasserre certificate through unrestricted truncated ideal multipliers and enter the moment formulation as linear equations. Under quotient Archimedeanity, the bounds converge upward to the optimum.
assumptions_latex: The feasible set is \(K=\{x:g_j(x)\ge 0,\ j=1,\ldots,m,\ h_k(x)=0,\ k=1,\ldots,s\}\).
The quadratic module modulo the equality ideal \(I(h)\) is Archimedean.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The bounds are valid, monotone, and converge to \(f^*\). Equality multipliers are unrestricted polynomials, while inequality multipliers remain sums of squares.

notation.meaning: Degree-truncated ideal generated by equality constraints.

knowledge_statements.title: Boolean Lasserre Hierarchy
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Zero–one Lasserre hierarchy in the quotient by the Boolean ideal, using quotient-reduced degree conventions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(I_B=\langle x_i^2-x_i:i=1,\ldots,n\rangle\). At order \(d\), reduce monomials modulo \(I_B\) to square-free monomials and compute \(\rho_d=\sup\{\gamma\in\mathbb R:f-\gamma\in I_B+Q_d(g)\}\), with all terms represented within the chosen quotient truncation. Equivalently, the moment formulation imposes \(y_{\alpha+2e_i}=y_{\alpha+e_i}\) whenever the required indices lie within the truncation. The bounds are monotone and valid on \(\{0,1\}^n\). Under the quotient-degree convention in which order \(d\ge n\) retains every square-free monomial, the relaxation is exact for every nonempty feasible subset described by the included inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Boolean equations reduce moments to square-free subsets. The resulting Lasserre bounds are monotone and become exact once the quotient truncation represents every function on the finite Boolean cube.
assumptions_latex: The variables satisfy \(x_i^2-x_i=0\) for \(i=1,\ldots,n\).
Any additional inequalities are represented by a truncated quadratic module, and truncation is interpreted after Boolean quotient reduction.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The hierarchy may be formed in the square-free quotient and is exact once all square-free monomials are retained. Lower orders give valid monotone bounds.

knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Set Preordering Refinements
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite convergence after adjoining equations that generate the finite feasible set's vanishing ideal.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K=\{u^1,\ldots,u^N\}\) and suppose \(I(K)=\langle h_1,\ldots,h_s\rangle\). Define \(\theta_d=\sup\{\gamma\in\mathbb R:f-\gamma\in I_{2d}(h)+T_d(g)\}\). There exists \(d_0<\infty\) such that \(f-f^*\in I_{2d_0}(h)+T_{d_0}(g)\), and therefore \(\theta_d=f^*\) for every \(d\ge d_0\). If an optimal truncated moment sequence satisfies the applicable flat-extension rank condition, it also yields a finitely supported representing measure concentrated on global minimizers.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When equations generating the vanishing ideal of a finite feasible set are included, the refined hierarchy is exact at a finite order. A flat optimal moment sequence can additionally recover a finitely supported optimizer measure.
assumptions_latex: The feasible set \(K\) is finite and nonempty.
Its vanishing ideal \(I(K)\) is included through generators \(h\), and the relaxation contains the required inequality preordering.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: There exists \(d_0<\infty\) such that \(\theta_d=f^*\) for every \(d\ge d_0\). At an exact order, an optimal moment sequence satisfying flatness permits recovery of a representing measure supported on global minimizers.

notation.meaning: Vanishing ideal of the finite feasible set.

knowledge_statements.title: Krivine–Stengle LP Hierarchies
knowledge_statements.scope_note: LP positivity hierarchy for normalized compact descriptions satisfying a Krivine-type certificate theorem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(r\in\mathbb N\), compute the largest \(\gamma\in\mathbb R\) for which coefficients \(c_{\alpha\beta}\ge 0\) satisfy \(f-\gamma=\sum_{|\alpha|+|\beta|\le r}c_{\alpha\beta}g^\alpha(1-g)^\beta\). This coefficient-matching problem is a linear program; denote its value by \(\kappa_r\). Start at the least order capable of representing \(f\), increase \(r\), and return the current lower bound when the selected stopping criterion is met. Under the stated Krivine hypotheses, \(\kappa_r\le\kappa_{r+1}\le f^*\) and \(\kappa_r\to f^*\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Krivine–Stengle hierarchies match the objective residual to normalized constraint products with nonnegative scalar coefficients, producing LP lower bounds that converge under the certificate theorem's compactness and generation hypotheses.
assumptions_latex: The compact feasible set is described by normalized generators satisfying \(0\le g_j(x)\le 1\).
The polynomials \(g_1,\ldots,g_m\) generate \(\mathbb R[x]\) as an algebra and satisfy the applicable Krivine positivity hypotheses.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The LP bounds are valid and monotone and converge to \(f^*\). Positivity is encoded by nonnegative scalar coefficients rather than positive-semidefinite Gram matrices.

knowledge_statements.title: Mixed LP–SDP Hierarchies
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic mixed certificate template; the node path does not select a unique LP–SDP hierarchy.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Choose finite families \(\mathcal P_d\) and \(\mathcal S_d\) of polynomials nonnegative on \(K\). Define \(\mu_d\) as the supremum of \(\gamma\in\mathbb R\) admitting \(f-\gamma=\sum_{p\in\mathcal P_d}c_pp+\sum_{s\in\mathcal S_d}\sigma_ss\), where \(c_p\ge 0\), every \(\sigma_s\) is a sum of squares, and all products have degree at most \(2d\). Coefficient matching, scalar nonnegativity, and Gram-matrix positivity form a mixed LP–SDP. The bound satisfies \(\mu_d\le f^*\); nested certificate families give \(\mu_d\le\mu_{d+1}\). Convergence holds if the union of the certificate cones contains every polynomial strictly positive on \(K\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A mixed hierarchy combines nonnegative scalar multipliers for selected positivity products with SOS multipliers for others. Nested families yield monotone valid bounds; convergence depends on asymptotic completeness of the combined certificate cone.
assumptions_latex: A finite collection of polynomials nonnegative on \(K\) is partitioned into an LP block and an SOS block.
Every certificate term respects the common degree bound \(2d\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The resulting bound is valid. Enlarging either block or increasing \(d\) cannot decrease the lower bound when the certificate cones are nested; convergence requires asymptotic completeness for polynomials strictly positive on \(K\).

knowledge_statements.title: Lagrange-Multiplier-Augmented Hierarchies
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Lifted moment–SOS hierarchy using polynomial KKT equations and multiplier variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(f,g_1,\ldots,g_m\in\mathbb R[x]\), introduce \(\lambda\in\mathbb R^m\) and the KKT ideal \(I_{\mathrm{KKT}}=\langle \nabla f-\sum_{j=1}^m\lambda_j\nabla g_j,\,\lambda_jg_j:j=1,\ldots,m\rangle\). Starting at the least compatible degree \(d_0\), order \(d\ge d_0\) maximizes \(\gamma\) subject to \(f-\gamma\in I_{\mathrm{KKT},2d}+Q_d(g_1,\ldots,g_m,\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_m)\). Its output is the lower bound \(\rho_d\); increase \(d\) until a prescribed gap tolerance or a flat moment certificate is obtained. If every global minimizer admits KKT multipliers and the lifted quadratic module is Archimedean, then \(\rho_d\uparrow f^*\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Apply moment–SOS relaxations to the feasible KKT system in variables and multipliers; under KKT coverage and lifted Archimedeanity, the resulting lower bounds converge to the optimum.
assumptions_latex: \(K=\{x:g_j(x)\ge0,\ j=1,\ldots,m\}\neq\varnothing\) and \(f^*=\min_K f\) is finite.
Every global minimizer satisfies the displayed KKT system with some \(\lambda\ge0\).
The lifted quadratic module is Archimedean.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\rho_d\le\rho_{d+1}\le f^*\) and \(\lim_{d\to\infty}\rho_d=f^*\).

notation.meaning: degree-2d truncation of the KKT ideal

knowledge_statements.title: Archimedean Quadratic-Module Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Standard Archimedean condition for basic closed polynomial feasible sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(g_1,\ldots,g_m\in\mathbb R[x]\), define \(Q(g)=\{\sigma_0+\sum_{j=1}^m\sigma_jg_j:\sigma_j\text{ are sums of squares}\}\). The quadratic module is Archimedean precisely when there exists \(R>0\) such that \(R-\|x\|_2^2\in Q(g)\). This condition implies that \(K=\{x:g_j(x)\ge0,\ j=1,\ldots,m\}\) is compact. Moreover, every polynomial strictly positive on \(K\) belongs to \(Q(g)\), so degree truncations of \(Q(g)\) provide asymptotically complete positivity certificates.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A quadratic module is Archimedean when it certifies a bounding ball; this makes the feasible set compact and enables Putinar positivity certificates.
assumptions_latex: \(g_1,\ldots,g_m\in\mathbb R[x]\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(R-\|x\|_2^2\in Q(g)\) for some \(R>0\), hence \(K\) is compact and \(p>0\) on \(K\Rightarrow p\in Q(g)\).

notation.meaning: quadratic module generated by the constraint polynomials

knowledge_statements.title: Compact Preordering Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Schmüdgen positivity regime based on compactness of the basic closed set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:g_j(x)\ge0,\ j=1,\ldots,m\}\) be compact, and define the preordering \(T(g)=\{\sum_{I\subseteq\{1,\ldots,m\}}\sigma_I\prod_{i\in I}g_i:\sigma_I\text{ are sums of squares}\}\). Then every \(p\in\mathbb R[x]\) satisfying \(p(x)>0\) for all \(x\in K\) belongs to \(T(g)\). Consequently, SOS lower bounds formed from degree truncations \(T_d(g)\) converge monotonically to the minimum of any polynomial attaining a finite minimum on \(K\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Compactness alone makes the generated preordering complete for strict positivity and yields asymptotic convergence of preordering-based SOS bounds.
assumptions_latex: \(K=\{x:g_j(x)\ge0\}\) is compact.
\(p\in\mathbb R[x]\) is strictly positive on \(K\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(p\in T(g)\); in particular, \(\sup\{\gamma:f-\gamma\in T_d(g)\}\uparrow\min_K f\).

knowledge_statements.title: Redundant-Ball-Constraint Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Archimedeanity obtained by explicitly adjoining a redundant bounding-ball inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K=\{x:g_j(x)\ge0,\ j=1,\ldots,m\}\) be compact. Choose \(R>\max_{x\in K}\|x\|_2^2\) and append \(g_{m+1}(x)=R-\|x\|_2^2\). The augmented description defines exactly the same set \(K\), while its quadratic module \(Q(g_1,\ldots,g_m,g_{m+1})\) is Archimedean because it contains \(R-\|x\|_2^2\) as a generator. Hence Putinar certificates and asymptotic convergence of the associated Lasserre hierarchy apply to the augmented formulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Appending a valid bounding-ball inequality does not change a compact feasible set and makes its generated quadratic module Archimedean.
assumptions_latex: \(K=\{x:g_j(x)\ge0\}\) is nonempty and compact.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(K=\{x:g_1(x),\ldots,g_m(x),R-\|x\|_2^2\ge0\}\) and the augmented quadratic module is Archimedean.

knowledge_statements.title: Putinar Certificate Mechanism
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Strict-positivity certificate in an Archimedean quadratic module.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:g_j(x)\ge0,\ j=1,\ldots,m\}\), and suppose the quadratic module \(Q(g)\) is Archimedean. For every polynomial \(p\in\mathbb R[x]\) with \(p(x)>0\) on \(K\), there exist sum-of-squares polynomials \(\sigma_0,\ldots,\sigma_m\) satisfying \[p=\sigma_0+\sum_{j=1}^m\sigma_jg_j.\] This identity is directly verifiable by polynomial coefficient comparison and Gram-matrix positive semidefiniteness; it certifies \(p(x)\ge0\) for every \(x\in K\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under Archimedeanity, every polynomial strictly positive on the feasible set has a sum-of-squares weighted constraint representation.
assumptions_latex: \(Q(g)\) is Archimedean.
\(p(x)>0\) for every \(x\in K\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(p=\sigma_0+\sum_{j=1}^m\sigma_jg_j\) for sum-of-squares polynomials \(\sigma_j\).

knowledge_statements.title: Schmüdgen Certificate Mechanism
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Strict-positivity certificate using all square-free products of defining inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:g_j(x)\ge0,\ j=1,\ldots,m\}\) be compact. For every \(p\in\mathbb R[x]\) with \(p(x)>0\) on \(K\), there exist sum-of-squares polynomials \(\sigma_I\), indexed by \(I\subseteq\{1,\ldots,m\}\), such that \[p=\sum_{I\subseteq\{1,\ldots,m\}}\sigma_I\prod_{i\in I}g_i.\] Since each product is nonnegative on \(K\), the identity is a coefficient-checkable certificate of nonnegativity there. Unlike Putinar's form, it uses the full preordering and requires compactness rather than an explicitly Archimedean quadratic module.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On a compact basic closed set, strict positivity is certified by SOS multipliers times every square-free product of defining inequalities.

\(p(x)>0\) for every \(x\in K\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(p=\sum_I\sigma_I\prod_{i\in I}g_i\) with every \(\sigma_I\) a sum of squares.

children.title: Minimizer Convergence

knowledge_statements.title: Minimizer Convergence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convergence of asymptotically optimal feasible points on a compact set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be nonempty and compact, let \(f:K\to\mathbb R\) be continuous, and set \(X^*=\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in K}f(x)\). If a sequence \((x_d)\subseteq K\) satisfies \(f(x_d)\to f^*=\min_K f\), then \(\operatorname{dist}(x_d,X^*)\to0\). Every accumulation point of \((x_d)\) therefore belongs to \(X^*\). If \(X^*=\{x^*\}\) is a singleton, the entire sequence converges to \(x^*\). This applies to feasible points extracted from moment relaxations whenever their objective values become asymptotically optimal.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On a compact feasible set, asymptotically optimal feasible points approach the minimizer set; uniqueness forces convergence to the unique minimizer.
assumptions_latex: \(K\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is nonempty and compact.
\(f\) is continuous on \(K\).
\(x_d\in K\) and \(f(x_d)\to\min_K f\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{dist}(x_d,X^*)\to0\); if \(X^*=\{x^*\}\), then \(x_d\to x^*\).

knowledge_statements.title: Moment-Sequence Convergence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Subsequential convergence of asymptotically optimal moment relaxations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Assume the quadratic module of \(K\) is Archimedean. For each relaxation order \(d\), let \(y^{(d)}\) be a normalized feasible moment sequence with \(y^{(d)}_0=1\) and \(L_{y^{(d)}}(f)\to f^*\). Then the moment bounds implied by Archimedeanity permit a diagonal subsequence converging coordinatewise to a full sequence \(y^*\). The limiting positivity and localizing conditions give a probability measure \(\mu^*\) supported on \(K\), and optimality implies \(\operatorname{supp}\mu^*\subseteq X^*\). If \(X^*=\{x^*\}\), every convergent subsequence has \(y^*_{\alpha}=(x^*)^{\alpha}\), hence the full family converges coordinatewise to the Dirac moment sequence at \(x^*\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Archimedean moment relaxations have convergent subsequences whose representing measures are supported on global minimizers; uniqueness yields convergence to the minimizer's Dirac moments.
assumptions_latex: The constraint quadratic module is Archimedean.
Each \(y^{(d)}\) is normalized and feasible at order \(d\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(y^{(d_k)}_{\alpha}\to\int_Kx^{\alpha}\,d\mu^*(x)\) for every \(\alpha\), with \(\operatorname{supp}\mu^*\subseteq X^*\).

children.title: Moment-to-Minimizer Transfer Regimes
children.top_down_role: Conditions connecting convergent moment information with minimizer recovery.

knowledge_statements.title: Moment-to-Minimizer Transfer Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditions under which relaxation moments determine actual global minimizers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(y\) be an optimal feasible truncated moment sequence with value \(L_y(f)=f^*\). Two transfer regimes are valid. First, if an applicable flat-extension condition holds, such as \(\operatorname{rank}M_t(y)=\operatorname{rank}M_{t-r}(y)\), then \(y\) has a finitely atomic representing measure \(\mu=\sum_{i=1}^q w_i\delta_{x_i}\) on \(K\); since \(f-f^*\ge0\) on \(K\) and its \(\mu\)-integral is zero, every atom \(x_i\) is a global minimizer. Second, if asymptotically optimal representing measures converge and the minimizer is unique, their first moments converge to that minimizer. Without flatness or uniqueness, first moments need not themselves be minimizers.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Flat moment matrices permit extraction of minimizing atoms; alternatively, uniqueness transfers asymptotically optimal moment measures to the unique minimizer.
assumptions_latex: \(y\) is feasible and attains the global value \(f^*\).
Either the stated flat-extension condition holds or the global minimizer is unique.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Flatness yields atoms \(x_i\in X^*\); uniqueness yields convergence of first moments to \(x^*\).

notation.meaning: degree offset required by the constraints

review_flags: A source with the precise constrained flat-extension rank offset and extraction theorem is required.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The principle kind is suitable for a leaf collecting multiple transfer regimes, and the warning about first moments is appropriate. However, the flat-extension condition is stated only as an example, the constraint-dependent offset r is not defined precisely, and no source establishes the constrained extraction theorem or the asymptotic representing-measure regime. These details materially determine the valid hypotheses.

knowledge_statements.title: Missing-Compactness-Certificate Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Loss of tightness and minimizer convergence without a compactness certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Without an Archimedean quadratic module or another tightness-producing certificate, value convergence and moment-to-minimizer convergence have no general guarantee. Concretely, minimize \(f(x,y)=(xy-1)^2+x^2\) over \(\mathbb R^2\). Its infimum is \(0\), but it is unattained: along \((x_t,y_t)=(t^{-1},t)\), one has \(f(x_t,y_t)=t^{-2}\to0\) while \(\|(x_t,y_t)\|_2\to\infty\). The associated Dirac moment sequences are asymptotically optimal but are not tight and possess no coordinatewise finite subsequence even at first order. Thus asymptotic values alone cannot transfer to a minimizer when compactness control is absent.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Without a compactness certificate, nearly optimal mass may escape to infinity, preventing attainment, moment tightness, and minimizer extraction.
assumptions_latex: The feasible set is \(K=\mathbb R^2\).
No Archimedean or equivalent coercive compactness certificate is imposed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\inf_K f=0\) is unattained, and the asymptotically optimal sequence \((t^{-1},t)\) escapes to infinity.
review_flags: Concrete example is directly checkable, but no supplied locator documents this noncompact failure boundary.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary kind exactly fits the leaf, and the displayed example is algebraically consistent: its infimum is zero, is unattained, and the given sequence escapes to infinity. Nevertheless, the record supplies no cited source or explicit standard-field rationale for either the example or the broader no-guarantee claim, so it does not satisfy the evidence requirement.

knowledge_statements.title: Optimization Nonattainment
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nonattainment for polynomial optimization over a closed noncompact feasible set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be nonempty and closed, and let \(f\in\mathbb R[x]\) have finite infimum \(f^*:=\inf_{x\in K}f(x)>-\infty\). Optimization nonattainment occurs when \(\{x\in K:f(x)=f^*\}=\varnothing\). In that case, for every sequence \((x_k)\subseteq K\) satisfying \(f(x_k)\to f^*\), one has \(\|x_k\|\to\infty\). Thus compactness-based arguments for existence of an optimizer, representing optimal measures, or finite convergence cannot be invoked without an additional coercivity, tightness, or positivity-at-infinity condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite polynomial infimum may be unattained on a closed noncompact set; then every minimizing sequence diverges to infinity.
assumptions_latex: \(K\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is nonempty and closed.
\(f\in\mathbb R[x]\) and \(f^*>-\infty\).
The infimum \(f^*\) is not attained on \(K\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every minimizing sequence \((x_k)\subseteq K\) satisfies \(\|x_k\|\to\infty\).

knowledge_statements.title: Mass Escape to Infinity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Loss of tightness for minimizing measures in a noncompact moment formulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be closed and let \((x_k)\subseteq K\) satisfy \(\|x_k\|\to\infty\). The probability measures \(\mu_k:=\delta_{x_k}\) are not tight: for every compact set \(C\subseteq K\), one has \(\mu_k(C)=0\) for all sufficiently large \(k\). Consequently, \((\mu_k)\) has no weakly convergent subsequence in the space of probability measures on \(K\). If additionally \(f(x_k)\to f^*\), these measures form a minimizing sequence for the measure formulation while no limiting probability measure captures their mass.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dirac measures supported on a diverging minimizing sequence lose tightness, so their mass has no probability-measure limit on the feasible set.
assumptions_latex: \(K\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is closed.
\((x_k)\subseteq K\) and \(\|x_k\|\to\infty\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The sequence \((\delta_{x_k})\) is not tight and has no weakly convergent subsequence in \(\mathcal P(K)\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The tightness and weak-convergence claims are correct for Dirac measures along a norm-divergent sequence, and the failure-boundary role fits. No source is supplied for the measure-theoretic assertion or its noncompact moment interpretation.

children.title: Nonattainment–Escape Coupling
children.top_down_role: Structural connections between absent optimizers and escape phenomena.

knowledge_statements.title: Nonattainment–Escape Coupling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalence between nonattainment and escape of all minimizing sequences.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be nonempty and closed, let \(f:K\to\mathbb R\) be continuous, and suppose \(f^*:=\inf_{x\in K}f(x)\) is finite. Then \(f\) fails to attain \(f^*\) on \(K\) if and only if every minimizing sequence \((x_k)\subseteq K\), defined by \(f(x_k)\to f^*\), satisfies \(\|x_k\|\to\infty\). Equivalently, nonattainment is precisely the absence of a bounded minimizing subsequence; the associated Dirac minimizing measures therefore escape every compact subset of \(K\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On a closed feasible set, a finite infimum is unattained exactly when every minimizing sequence escapes to infinity.
assumptions_latex: \(K\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is nonempty and closed.
\(f:K\to\mathbb R\) is continuous.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The infimum is unattained if and only if every minimizing sequence satisfies \(\|x_k\|\to\infty\).

notation.meaning: finite infimum of f on K

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The equivalence is mathematically correct under the stated closedness and continuity assumptions, and theorem is the appropriate content kind. No citation is supplied for either the equivalence or the associated escape-of-mass conclusion.

knowledge_statements.title: Weighted Positivity Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Polynomial positivity certified after multiplication by a positive weight.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K:=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:g_j(x)\geq 0,\ j=1,\ldots,m\}\), and let \(Q(g):=\{\sigma_0+\sum_{j=1}^m\sigma_jg_j:\sigma_j\text{ is a sum of squares}\}\). For \(f,w\in\mathbb R[x]\), a weighted positivity certificate is an identity \(wf=\sigma_0+\sum_{j=1}^m\sigma_jg_j\) with \(w(x)>0\) on \(K\). This identity is finitely checkable using semidefinite Gram matrices and certifies \(f(x)\geq 0\) for every \(x\in K\). Strict positivity of \(w\) permits division of the certified inequality by the weight.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If a positive polynomial weight times the target belongs to the quadratic module, the target is nonnegative on the feasible set.

\(w(x)>0\) for every \(x\in K\).
