knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed SOS identity certifies \(f(x)\geq 0\) for every \(x\in K\).

knowledge_statements.title: Denominator Positivity Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Rational positivity certificate with a denominator positive on the feasible set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K:=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:g_j(x)\geq 0,\ j=1,\ldots,m\}\) and \(Q(g):=\{\sigma_0+\sum_{j=1}^m\sigma_jg_j:\sigma_j\text{ is a sum of squares}\}\). For \(q,f\in\mathbb R[x]\), a denominator positivity certificate consists of \(q(x)>0\) on \(K\) and an identity \(qf=\sigma_0+\sum_{j=1}^m\sigma_jg_j\), where every \(\sigma_j\) is a sum of squares. Equivalently, on \(K\), \(f=(\sigma_0+\sum_{j=1}^m\sigma_jg_j)/q\). Since the denominator is positive and the numerator is nonnegative on \(K\), the identity certifies \(f(x)\geq 0\) for every \(x\in K\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A positive denominator and an SOS quadratic-module numerator provide a rational certificate that the target polynomial is nonnegative.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The rational representation certifies \(f(x)\geq 0\) for every \(x\in K\).

knowledge_statements.title: Weight–Denominator Selection Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Validity and tractability conditions for choosing certificate multipliers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K:=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:g_j(x)\geq 0,\ j=1,\ldots,m\}\), let \(f,q\in\mathbb R[x]\), and let \(Q_d(g)\) denote the quadratic module truncated at degree \(2d\). The polynomial \(q\) is admissible as a weight or denominator at order \(d\) when \(q(x)>0\) for every \(x\in K\) and \(qf\in Q_d(g)\). Equivalently, there are sum-of-squares polynomials \(\sigma_j\) such that \(qf=\sigma_0+\sum_{j=1}^m\sigma_jg_j\) and \(\deg(\sigma_jg_j)\leq 2d\), with \(g_0:=1\). For \(q_r:=(1+\|x\|^2)^r\), where \(r\in\mathbb N\), each \(q_r\) is globally positive, and the untruncated certificate families are nested because \(q_rf\in Q(g)\) implies \(q_{r+1}f\in Q(g)\). Increasing \(r\) increases the degree lower bound on any compatible relaxation order.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A multiplier is admissible when it is positive on the feasible set and its product with the target has a degree-compatible quadratic-module representation; standard positive-power families are nested but require increasing degree capacity.
assumptions_latex: \(K=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:g_j(x)\geq 0,\ j=1,\ldots,m\}\).
\(f,q\in\mathbb R[x]\).
\(q(x)>0\) for every \(x\in K\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The multiplier \(q\) is admissible at order \(d\) exactly when \(qf\in Q_d(g)\); for \(q_r=(1+\|x\|^2)^r\), increasing \(r\) produces a nested untruncated family and increases the required degree capacity.

knowledge_statements.title: Finite Real-Variety Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite convergence when equality constraints generate a real-radical ideal with finite real variety.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(h=(h_1,\ldots,h_s)\subseteq\mathbb R[x]\) and \(g=(g_1,\ldots,g_m)\subseteq\mathbb R[x]\), and define \(K:=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:h_i(x)=0\ \text{for }i=1,\ldots,s,\ g_j(x)\geq 0\ \text{for }j=1,\ldots,m\}\). Assume \(K\neq\varnothing\), the ideal \(I(h)\) is real radical, and its real variety \(V_{\mathbb R}(h):=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:h_i(x)=0\ \text{for all }i\}\) is finite. Then, for every \(f\in\mathbb R[x]\), there exists \(d_0\) such that \(f-f^*\in I_{2d_0}(h)+Q_{d_0}(g)\), where \(f^*:=\min_{x\in K}f(x)\). Consequently, the standard moment–SOS hierarchy has relaxation value \(f^*\) at every order \(d\geq d_0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If the equality ideal is real radical and has a finite real variety, the moment–SOS hierarchy reaches the exact minimum at a finite order and admits a finite-degree certificate.
assumptions_latex: \(K\neq\varnothing\).
\(I(h)\) is real radical.
\(V_{\mathbb R}(h)\) is finite.
\(f\in\mathbb R[x]\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: There exists \(d_0\) such that \(f-f^*\in I_{2d_0}(h)+Q_{d_0}(g)\), and the relaxation value equals \(f^*\) for every \(d\geq d_0\).

knowledge_statements.title: Generic Optimality Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite convergence under generic nonlinear-programming conditions at every global minimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f,h_i,g_j\in\mathbb R[x]\), define \(K:=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:h_i(x)=0,\ g_j(x)\geq 0\}\), and assume \(K\neq\varnothing\), \(I(h)+Q(g)\) is Archimedean, and \(I(h)\) is real radical. Suppose that the constraint qualification condition, strict complementarity condition, and second-order sufficiency condition hold at every global minimizer of \(f\) on \(K\). Then \(f-f^*\in I(h)+Q(g)\), where \(f^*:=\min_{x\in K}f(x)\), and hence the Lasserre hierarchy is exact at some finite relaxation order. For fixed degree patterns, failure of these local optimality conditions is confined to an algebraic exceptional set of coefficient data, subject to feasibility and attainment.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With an Archimedean module and a real-radical equality ideal, constraint qualification, strict complementarity, and second-order sufficiency at every minimizer imply a finite-degree certificate and finite convergence; these conditions are generic outside exceptional polynomial data.
assumptions_latex: \(K\neq\varnothing\).

knowledge_statements.title: Flat-Extension Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Full moment-matrix flatness certifying a unique finite atomic extension.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(y=(y_\alpha)_{|\alpha|\leq2t}\) be a truncated real multisequence with \(y_0=1\) and \(M_t(y)\succeq0\). If \(\operatorname{rank}M_t(y)=\operatorname{rank}M_{t-1}(y)=r\), then \(y\) has a unique infinite positive-semidefinite moment extension and a unique representing probability measure \(\mu=\sum_{i=1}^r\lambda_i\delta_{x_i}\), where \(\lambda_i>0\) and the points \(x_i\in\mathbb R^n\) are distinct. The rank identity is therefore a verifiable certificate of finite atomic representability and permits extraction of the support through multiplication matrices.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A positive moment matrix whose rank stops increasing has a unique representing measure supported on exactly that many points.

knowledge_statements.title: Flat-Truncation Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Rank-flat feasible truncation certifying exactness and optimizer extraction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(y\) be feasible for an order-\(t\) moment relaxation over \(K:=\{x:h_i(x)=0,\ g_j(x)\geq0\}\), and set \(d_K:=\max\{1,\lceil\deg h_i/2\rceil,\lceil\deg g_j/2\rceil\}\). If \(y\) is relaxation-optimal, its atoms are global minimizers and the relaxation value equals the polynomial optimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Constraint-compatible rank stabilization of an optimal moment truncation certifies exactness and yields finitely many global minimizers.

\(\operatorname{rank}M_t(y)=\operatorname{rank}M_{t-d_K}(y)=r\).

knowledge_statements.title: Nonflat-Truncation Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary of finite atomic extraction when the required moment-matrix rank stabilization fails.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(y=(y_\alpha)_{|\alpha|\le 2t}\) satisfy the moment and localizing positive-semidefiniteness conditions of a basic closed set \(K\), and let \(d\) be the maximum relaxation shift. If \(\operatorname{rank}M_t(y)>\operatorname{rank}M_{t-d}(y)\), then the flat-truncation hypothesis is absent. Consequently, this truncation alone supplies neither an \(r\)-atomic representing measure nor a finite multiplication-matrix extraction certificate. Nonflatness is only failure of this certificate: it does not imply that no representing measure exists, that the relaxation value is inexact, or that a higher-order truncation cannot become flat.

knowledge_statements.title: Finite Atomic-Measure Recovery
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Flat-truncation recovery for normalized feasible moment data on a basic closed semialgebraic set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:g_j(x)\ge0,\ j=1,\ldots,m\}\), and let \(y=(y_\alpha)_{|\alpha|\le 2t}\) be a normalized feasible truncated moment sequence with \(y_0=1\). Set \(d=\max\{1,\max_{1\le j\le m}\lceil\deg(g_j)/2\rceil\}\). Suppose the required moment and localizing matrices are positive semidefinite and \(\operatorname{rank}M_t(y)=\operatorname{rank}M_{t-d}(y)=r\). Then \(y\) admits an \(r\)-atomic representing probability measure \(\mu=\sum_{k=1}^r w_k\delta_{x^{(k)}}\), where the points \(x^{(k)}\in K\) are distinct, the weights satisfy \(w_k>0\), and \(\sum_{k=1}^r w_k=1\). If additionally \(f\in\mathbb R[x]\), \(\deg(f)\le2t\), \(y\) is optimal for the moment relaxation, and \(L_y(f)=f^*:=\min_{x\in K}f(x)\), then every recovered atom is a global minimizer of \(f\) on \(K\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A normalized feasible flat moment truncation has an r-atomic probability measure on K. If the truncation is optimal, contains the moments needed for the objective, and attains the true minimum, every recovered atom is a global minimizer.
assumptions_latex: \(y=(y_\alpha)_{|\alpha|\le2t}\) satisfies \(y_0=1\) and the required moment and localizing positive-semidefiniteness conditions for \(K\).
\(d=\max\{1,\max_{1\le j\le m}\lceil\deg(g_j)/2\rceil\}\) and \(\operatorname{rank}M_t(y)=\operatorname{rank}M_{t-d}(y)=r\).
For minimizer recovery, \(f\in\mathbb R[x]\), \(\deg(f)\le2t\), \(y\) is optimal, and \(L_y(f)=f^*:=\min_{x\in K}f(x)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(y_\alpha=\sum_{k=1}^r w_k(x^{(k)})^\alpha\) for every \(|\alpha|\le2t\), with \(x^{(k)}\in K\), \(w_k>0\), and \(\sum_{k=1}^r w_k=1\); under the objective hypotheses, \(f(x^{(k)})=f^*\) for every \(k\).

notation.meaning: maximum constraint degree shift, with a minimum value of one

knowledge_statements.title: Multiplication-Matrix Extraction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extraction of atoms from commuting coordinate-multiplication operators induced by flat moment data.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a flat truncated moment sequence \(y\) with \(r=\operatorname{rank}M_{t-d}(y)\). Choose monomials \(B=(b_1,\ldots,b_r)\) indexing a nonsingular principal Gram block \(G=(L_y(b_p b_q))_{p,q}\). For each coordinate \(x_i\), form \(H_i=(L_y(x_i b_p b_q))_{p,q}\) and solve \(G X_i=H_i\). The resulting multiplication matrices \(X_i\) commute on the quotient space. Simultaneously diagonalize them, or diagonalize a generic linear combination and evaluate the remaining matrices on its eigenvectors. Output the joint eigenvalue tuples \(x^{(k)}\); recover weights from \(y_\alpha=\sum_k w_k(x^{(k)})^\alpha\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Build commuting coordinate-multiplication matrices from moment blocks; their joint eigenvalues are the recovered atoms, and a Vandermonde system yields weights.
assumptions_latex: \(y\) satisfies a flat rank condition supporting an \(r\)-atomic measure.
The selected basis block \(G\) is nonsingular.
Moments defining every \(H_i\) are available.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The output tuples are the support points of the representing measure, and the solved weights reproduce the supplied moments.

notation.meaning: matrix representing multiplication by coordinate x_i

knowledge_statements.title: Quotient-Algebra Extraction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Algebraic recovery of a finite support through the kernel ideal of a flat moment matrix.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a flat truncated moment sequence \(y\). Form the nullspace relations \(\ker M_t(y)\) and close the degree-valid relations under multiplication to obtain the zero-dimensional support ideal \(I\). Select a monomial basis \(B\) of the quotient algebra \(A=\mathbb R[x]/I\). Reduce each product \(x_i b\), with \(b\in B\), modulo \(I\) to construct the coordinate multiplication operator \(T_i:A\to A\). Compute the common zeros of \(I\), equivalently the joint spectrum of the commuting operators \((T_1,\ldots,T_n)\), and output those real feasible points. Determine positive weights by matching the available moments.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Kernel relations define a zero-dimensional quotient algebra; coordinate multiplication on that algebra yields the finite support through its joint spectrum.
assumptions_latex: \(y\) is flat and has a feasible finite atomic representing measure.
Kernel relations are available to all degrees needed for quotient reduction.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The real feasible joint spectrum of \((T_1,\ldots,T_n)\) equals the support of the representing measure.

notation.meaning: zero-dimensional ideal generated by moment-kernel relations

knowledge_statements.title: Multiple Isolated Minimizers
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Recovery behavior when the global minimizer set is finite but contains several isolated points.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the global minimizer set be \(S=\{x^{(1)},\ldots,x^{(q)}\}\). Every probability measure \(\mu=\sum_{k=1}^q w_k\delta_{x^{(k)}}\), with \(w_k\ge0\) and \(\sum_k w_k=1\), is optimal for the measure formulation. If its truncated moments become flat, extraction returns exactly the atoms having \(w_k>0\), and the stable moment rank equals their number. Thus one optimal moment solution need not expose all \(q\) minimizers: omitted minimizers may simply have zero mass. Recovering the complete finite minimizer set requires an optimal measure whose support is all of \(S\), or additional algebraic exploration.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An optimal measure may weight only some isolated minimizers, so flat extraction recovers its positive-weight support rather than necessarily every minimizer.
assumptions_latex: \(S=\{x^{(1)},\ldots,x^{(q)}\}\) is the finite global minimizer set.
The selected optimal moment sequence admits flat extraction.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The extracted set is \(\{x^{(k)}:w_k>0\}\subseteq S\), with cardinality equal to the stabilized moment rank.

knowledge_statements.title: Positive-Dimensional Minimizer Sets
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary between finite atomic extraction and recovery of an entire positive-dimensional minimizer set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the global minimizer set \(S\subseteq K\) have positive real dimension. An optimal representing measure may still be finitely atomic, including a Dirac measure at one minimizer, so flatness can recover a finite subset of \(S\). However, if an optimal measure has infinite support not contained in any finite algebraic subset, its moment-matrix ranks cannot stabilize at a finite rank: finite rank would imply a finitely atomic representing measure. Hence finite joint-spectrum extraction cannot recover all of a positive-dimensional \(S\); complete recovery instead requires an algebraic or semialgebraic description of the minimizer set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Flat extraction may recover selected atoms from a positive-dimensional minimizer set, but it cannot enumerate the entire set when the representing measure has infinite support.
assumptions_latex: The global minimizer set \(S\) has positive real dimension.
The considered optimal measure has infinite support for the nonflatness conclusion.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Finite-rank flat extraction cannot represent or enumerate the entire infinite support; full-set recovery requires a set description rather than finitely many atoms.

knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Support Recovery Limits
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cardinality limit imposed by the stable rank of a flat truncated moment sequence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose a feasible truncated moment sequence is flat with stable rank \(r\). Its flat extension has an \(r\)-atomic representing measure, so any extraction based solely on that sequence can certify at most \(r\) distinct support points. If the desired minimizer set contains more than \(r\) points, the sequence cannot certify all of them, even when every extracted atom is globally optimal. Conversely, for a representing measure supported on \(s\) distinct points with positive weights, sufficiently high moment matrices have rank \(s\). Thus complete finite-support recovery requires eventual rank at least the number of points to be recovered.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A flat sequence of rank r certifies r support atoms; it cannot recover a larger minimizer set without additional moment data or solutions.
assumptions_latex: The truncated moment sequence satisfies a flat rank condition with stable rank \(r\).
Support points are distinct and their representing weights are positive.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The certified support has exactly \(r\) atoms, and recovery of \(s>r\) distinct minimizers is impossible from that sequence alone.

notation.meaning: stable rank of the flat moment matrices
number of distinct desired support points

knowledge_statements.title: Continuum-Recovery Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Output limitation of finite spectral extraction when the minimizer set contains a continuum.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Multiplication-matrix extraction from a flat moment truncation operates on a finite-dimensional quotient algebra and therefore returns a finite joint spectrum. If the global minimizer set \(S\) contains a continuum, no such finite spectrum can equal \(S\). A flat optimal sequence may nevertheless return finitely many valid minimizers because its representing measure may select finitely many points of \(S\). Accordingly, exactness of the relaxation value and correctness of the extracted atoms do not certify recovery of the whole continuum. Whole-set recovery must instead identify equations and inequalities defining \(S\), or otherwise provide an infinite-set representation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Finite spectral extraction cannot equal a continuum of minimizers, although it may correctly recover finitely many selected minimizers and the exact optimal value.
assumptions_latex: The global minimizer set \(S\) is infinite and contains a continuum.
Extraction uses a finite-dimensional quotient algebra or finite moment matrix.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The finite extracted spectrum is at most a subset of \(S\), not a representation of the entire continuum.

knowledge_statements.title: Unconstrained Polynomial Optimization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Moment and sum-of-squares formulations for minimizing a polynomial over Euclidean space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(f\in\mathbb R[x]\) bounded below on \(\mathbb R^n\),
\[f^*=\inf_{x\in\mathbb R^n}f(x)=\inf\left\{\int f\,d\mu:\mu\in\mathcal P(\mathbb R^n)\right\}=\sup\{\gamma\in\mathbb R:f-\gamma\ge0\text{ on }\mathbb R^n\}.\]
For every \(d\) with \(2d\ge\deg f\), the degree-bounded SOS relaxation is
\[\rho_d=\sup\{\gamma:f-\gamma\in\Sigma[x]_{2d}\}\le f^*.\]
Its moment dual minimizes \(L_y(f)\) subject to \(y_0=1\) and \(M_d(y)\succeq0\). Equality \(\rho_d=f^*\) requires an SOS certificate and is not automatic for general nonnegative polynomials.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Unconstrained polynomial minimization equals a probability-measure problem; bounded-degree SOS certificates yield semidefinite lower bounds, not universally exact bounds.
assumptions_latex: \(f\in\mathbb R[x]\) is bounded below on \(\mathbb R^n\).
\(2d\ge\deg f\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\rho_d\le f^*\), with equality whenever \(f-f^*\in\Sigma[x]_{2d}\).

notation.meaning: sums of squares of degree at most 2d

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Generic finite convergence for unconstrained polynomial optimization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extraction-grounded generic finite-exactness result for the semidefinite relaxation specified by the source, conditional on its referenced construction and on attainment of the unconstrained global minimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\mathbf K\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be as in (6.29), and let \(\rho_d\) denote the optimal value of the semidefinite relaxation defined in (6.3). Define
\[
\mathcal F_t:=\left\{f\in\mathbb R[\mathbf x]_t:\exists\mathbf x^*\in\mathbb R^n,\ f(\mathbf x^*)=f^*=\inf_{\mathbf x\in\mathbb R^n}f(\mathbf x)\right\}.
\]
Then, for almost all \(f\in\mathcal F_t\), there exists an index \(d\) such that \(\rho_d=f^*\); hence the relaxation has finite convergence generically within \(\mathcal F_t\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For almost all degree-at-most-t polynomials whose unconstrained global minimum is attained, the source-specified semidefinite relaxation is exact at some finite relaxation order, subject to the construction referenced in the theorem.
assumptions_latex: \mathbf K\subseteq\mathbb R^n\text{ is as specified in (6.29)}
\rho_d\text{ is the optimal value of the semidefinite relaxation defined in (6.3)}
f\in\mathcal F_t:=\left\{g\in\mathbb R[\mathbf x]_t:\exists\mathbf x^*\in\mathbb R^n,\ g(\mathbf x^*)=g^*=\inf_{\mathbf x\in\mathbb R^n}g(\mathbf x)\right\}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{For almost all }f\in\mathcal F_t,\ \exists d<\infty\text{ such that }\rho_d=f^*.

knowledge_statements.title: Constrained Basic Semialgebraic Optimization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Moment and quadratic-module formulations for polynomial optimization on a basic closed set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(K=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:g_j(x)\ge0,\ j=1,\ldots,m\}\) be nonempty and let \(f\in\mathbb R[x]\). Then
\[f^*=\inf_{x\in K}f(x)=\inf\left\{\int_K f\,d\mu:\mu\in\mathcal P(K)\right\}.\]
At order \(d\), the moment relaxation minimizes \(L_y(f)\) subject to \(y_0=1\), \(M_d(y)\succeq0\), and \(M_{d-d_j}(g_jy)\succeq0\), where \(d_j=\lceil\deg(g_j)/2\rceil\). Its SOS dual maximizes \(\gamma\) subject to \(f-\gamma=\sigma_0+\sum_j\sigma_jg_j\) within degree \(2d\), with every \(\sigma_j\) a sum of squares.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Polynomial optimization on a basic closed set has a measure formulation and paired moment–SOS semidefinite relaxations using localizing matrices.
assumptions_latex: \(K\) is a nonempty basic closed semialgebraic set.
The relaxation order satisfies \(d\ge\max\{\lceil\deg(f)/2\rceil,d_1,\ldots,d_m\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The order-\(d\) moment and SOS programs provide lower bounds on \(f^*\), subject to their usual conic-duality qualifications.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Lifted basic semialgebraic representation and polynomial-optimization reduction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Applies when all operations define real-valued functions on the basic semialgebraic domain; division denominators must be nonzero and fractional powers must be real-valued wherever used. No convergence guarantee for the resulting moment–SOS hierarchy is asserted here.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathbf K\subset\mathbb R^n\) be a basic semialgebraic set, and let \(\mathcal A\) consist of the real-valued functions on \(\mathbf K\) generated from polynomials using \(|\cdot|\), \((\cdot)^{1/p}\) for \(p\in\mathbb N\), and \(+,\times,\div,\vee,\wedge\). For every \(f\in\mathcal A\), there exist \(q\in\mathbb N\) and a basic semialgebraic set \(S_f\subset\mathbb R^{n+q+1}\) whose projection onto the \((\mathbf x,t)\)-coordinates equals \(\{(\mathbf x,f(\mathbf x)): \mathbf x\in\mathbf K\}\). knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every real-valued function on a basic semialgebraic set constructed from polynomials using absolute values, integer-indexed roots, arithmetic, maxima, and minima has a graph that is the projection of a higher-dimensional basic semialgebraic set. Optimization with objectives and inequality constraints of this form therefore reduces to lifted polynomial optimization and can be treated using moment–SOS relaxations.

\(f,g\in\mathcal A\), where \(\mathcal A\) is generated from polynomials by \(|\cdot|\), \((\cdot)^{1/p}\) for \(p\in\mathbb N\), and \(+,\times,\div,\vee,\wedge\).

children.title: Discrete Polynomial Optimization
children.top_down_role: Polynomial optimization over general finite or discrete feasible domains.

knowledge_statements.title: Discrete Polynomial Optimization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Polynomial minimization over a finite feasible subset represented by polynomial equations and inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A discrete polynomial optimization problem is
\[f^*=\min\{f(x):x\in D,\ g_j(x)\ge0,\ j=1,\ldots,m\},\]
where \(f,g_j\in\mathbb R[x]\) and \(D\subset\mathbb R^n\) is finite. When \(D\) is specified by a vanishing ideal \(I(D)=\{p:p(x)=0\text{ for all }x\in D\}\), moment–SOS relaxations impose the equations \(L_y(hq)=0\) for degree-admissible \(h\in I(D)\) and monomials \(q\), together with moment and inequality-localizing positivity. Because \(D\) is finite, the coordinate algebra \(\mathbb R[x]/I(D)\) is finite-dimensional.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Discrete polynomial optimization minimizes a polynomial on a finite set, encoded by its vanishing ideal plus any polynomial inequalities.
assumptions_latex: \(D\subset\mathbb R^n\) is finite.
The feasible subset \(\{x\in D:g_j(x)\ge0\}\) is nonempty.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The problem admits a finite-dimensional coordinate-algebra representation through \(\mathbb R[x]/I(D)\).

children.top_down_role: Polynomial optimization specialized to Boolean-valued variables.

knowledge_statements.title: Boolean Polynomial Optimization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The sign-valued convention for polynomial optimization over the Boolean hypercube.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A Boolean polynomial optimization problem in the sign convention is
\[f^*=\min\{f(x):x\in\{-1,1\}^n,\ g_j(x)\ge0,\ j=1,\ldots,m\},\]
with \(f,g_j\in\mathbb R[x]\). Its Boolean domain is represented algebraically by \(x_i^2-1=0\) for \(i=1,\ldots,n\), hence computations may be performed in \(\mathbb R[x]/\langle x_1^2-1,\ldots,x_n^2-1\rangle\). Every residue class has a multilinear representative, since powers reduce by \(x_i^2=1\). The alternative \(\{0,1\}^n\) convention is obtained by an affine change of variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Boolean polynomial optimization minimizes a polynomial on the sign hypercube, whose ideal relations reduce all polynomials to multilinear representatives.
assumptions_latex: Variables use the sign convention \(x_i\in\{-1,1\}\).
Any additional feasible-set restrictions are polynomial inequalities \(g_j(x)\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The Boolean equations generate \(\langle x_i^2-1:i=1,\ldots,n\rangle\), and every polynomial has a multilinear representative modulo this ideal.

notation.meaning: Boolean vanishing ideal in the sign convention

knowledge_statements.title: Discreteness-Ideal Relaxations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite Cartesian domains represented by their coordinate vanishing ideal.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \(h_i(t)=\prod_{a\in D_i}(t-a)\) for \(i=1,\ldots,n\). The equations \(h_i(x_i)=0\) for all \(i=1,\ldots,n\) hold exactly when \(x\in D\). Thus \[K=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:g_j(x)\ge0\text{ for }j=1,\ldots,m,\ h_i(x_i)=0\text{ for }i=1,\ldots,n\}.\] At relaxation order \(d\), the moment relaxation imposes the moment and localizing positive-semidefinite constraints together with \(L_y(x^\alpha h_i(x_i))=0\) for every \(i\) and every multi-index \(\alpha\in\mathbb N^n\) satisfying \(|\alpha|+\deg h_i\le2d\). These equalities reduce moments modulo \(I(D)\) without changing the discrete feasible set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite Cartesian domain is exactly described by its coordinate vanishing polynomials, and moment relaxations impose the corresponding truncated ideal consequences as linear moment equations.
assumptions_latex: Let \(D=D_1\times\cdots\times D_n\subset\mathbb R^n\), where each \(D_i\) is finite.
Let \(g_1,\ldots,g_m\in\mathbb R[x]\) and \(K=\{x\in D:g_j(x)\ge0\text{ for }j=1,\ldots,m\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Optimization over \(K\) is polynomial optimization modulo the vanishing ideal \(I(D)\).

knowledge_statements.title: Rational-Function Optimization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Single rational objective with a strictly positive denominator and finite infimum on the feasible set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(r^*=\inf_{x\in K}p(x)/q(x)\in\mathbb R\), positivity of \(q\) gives \[r^*=\max\{\lambda\in\mathbb R:p(x)-\lambda q(x)\ge0\text{ for every }x\in K\}.\] A degree-\(2d\) SOS lower bound is \(r_d=\sup\{\lambda\in\mathbb R:p-\lambda q\in Q_d(g)\}\), where \(Q_d(g)\) is the truncated quadratic module. Every feasible \(\lambda\) satisfies \(\lambda\le r^*\). If \(Q(g)\) is Archimedean, then \(r_d\) converges monotonically to \(r^*\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With a positive denominator and finite infimum, rational minimization equals finding the largest scalar for which the numerator minus that scalar times the denominator is nonnegative. Truncated quadratic-module membership gives lower bounds that converge monotonically under an Archimedean hypothesis.
assumptions_latex: Let \(K=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:g_j(x)\ge0,\ j=1,\ldots,m\}\) be nonempty.
Let \(p,q\in\mathbb R[x]\), suppose \(q(x)>0\) for every \(x\in K\), and assume \(r^*=\inf_{x\in K}p(x)/q(x)\in\mathbb R\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The rational optimum \(r^*\) is the largest \(\lambda\in\mathbb R\) for which \(p-\lambda q\) is nonnegative on \(K\).

knowledge_statements.title: Lifted-Graph Representations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact graph lifting by polynomial equalities and inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \[G=\{(x,t,z)\in\mathbb R^{n+1+s}:a_i(x,t,z)\ge0\text{ for }i=1,\ldots,r,\ b_k(x,t,z)=0\text{ for }k=1,\ldots,\ell\}.\] If \[(x,t)\in\operatorname{graph}(f|_K)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad\exists z\in\mathbb R^s:(x,t,z)\in G,\] then \[\inf_{x\in K}f(x)=\inf\{t:(x,t,z)\in G\}.\] The lifting is exact at the optimization level because its projection is precisely the graph. Moment and localizing matrices in \((x,t,z)\) therefore provide semidefinite relaxations of the lifted polynomial problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An exact finite basic-semialgebraic lift of a function graph converts function optimization into polynomial optimization of the lifted value coordinate without changing the infimum.
assumptions_latex: Let \(K\subset\mathbb R^n\) and let \(f:K\to\mathbb R\).

assumptions_latex: For every instance \(I\), let \(v^*(I)>0\) be the optimal value of a maximization problem.
Let an algorithm return a feasible value \(v_A(I)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The algorithm has multiplicative factor \(\alpha\) precisely when its value ratio is uniformly at least \(\alpha\).

notation.meaning: optimal objective value on instance I

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Maximization convention with strictly positive optimum; minimization uses the reciprocal inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A deterministic algorithm has multiplicative approximation factor \(\alpha\in[0,1]\) on an instance class \(\mathcal I\) if \[v_A(I)\ge\alpha v^*(I)\qquad\text{for every }I\in\mathcal I.\] If \(U(I)\ge v^*(I)\) is a relaxation upper bound and rounding produces \(v_A(I)\ge\alpha U(I)\), then the same factor follows because \(v_A(I)\ge\alpha U(I)\ge\alpha v^*(I)\). The ratio convention is unsuitable when the optimum can vanish or change sign unless an explicit normalization is supplied.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For positive-valued maximization, a multiplicative guarantee requires every rounded feasible value to be at least a fixed fraction of the true optimum.
knowledge_statements.title: Multiplicative Approximation Guarantees

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The positive-valued maximization convention is mathematically coherent, but no inspectable source supports the selected convention. Because the statement defines when an algorithm has a multiplicative guarantee, definition is more accurate than condition.

assumptions_latex: For every instance \(I\), let \(v^*(I)\) be the optimal value of a maximization problem.
Let an algorithm return a feasible value \(v_A(I)\), and let \(\varepsilon(I)\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The additive loss is at most \(\varepsilon(I)\) exactly when \(v^*(I)-v_A(I)\le\varepsilon(I)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Absolute additive error for maximization; the error may depend on instance scale.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An algorithm has additive guarantee \(\varepsilon(I)\) on an instance class \(\mathcal I\) if \[0\le v^*(I)-v_A(I)\le\varepsilon(I)\qquad\text{for every }I\in\mathcal I.\] If a relaxation supplies \(U(I)\ge v^*(I)\) and the returned solution satisfies \(U(I)-v_A(I)\le\varepsilon(I)\), then \(v^*(I)-v_A(I)\le\varepsilon(I)\). A scale-normalized version replaces \(\varepsilon(I)\) by \(\varepsilon S(I)\) for an explicitly specified positive scale \(S(I)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An additive guarantee bounds the absolute gap between the true optimum and a returned feasible value, possibly relative to a stated instance scale.
knowledge_statements.title: Additive Approximation Guarantees

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The additive-gap convention is coherent for feasible maximization values, but it has no cited source. The record is phrased as a definition of an additive guarantee, so definition is preferable to condition.

assumptions_latex: Let \(I\) be a fixed optimization instance with optimum \(v^*(I)\).
Let computable statistics \(s(I)\) determine a nonnegative bound \(B(s(I))\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A computable inequality involving \(s(I)\) certifies performance specifically for instance \(I\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A posteriori performance certificate parameterized by computable features of one instance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a maximization instance \(I\), an instance-dependent additive certificate is a verifiable inequality \[0\le v^*(I)-v_A(I)\le B(s(I)),\] where \(s(I)\) is computable from the instance, relaxation solution, or rounded solution without knowing \(v^*(I)\). In particular, if a valid relaxation bound \(U(I)\ge v^*(I)\) is available, then \[v^*(I)-v_A(I)\le U(I)-v_A(I),\] so the observable relaxation gap is an instance-dependent certificate. Unlike a worst-case guarantee, its numerical strength may vary across instances.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An instance-dependent certificate bounds the unknown optimality gap using computable features of the particular instance, such as its relaxation gap.
knowledge_statements.title: Instance-Dependent Guarantees

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Certificate is an appropriate content kind, and the observable relaxation gap gives a valid instance-dependent upper bound. An authoritative source with a specific locator is required before accepting this formulation.

children.title: High-Probability Guarantees
children.top_down_role: Performance guarantees holding with specified probability over randomized data or procedures.

assumptions_latex: Let \(I\sim\mathbb P\) be a random instance and let the algorithmic randomness be included in the probability space.
Let \(L(I,A)\ge0\) be a measurable performance loss.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The loss threshold \(\varepsilon\) holds with confidence \(1-\delta\) when its exceedance probability is at most \(\delta\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Joint probability over the instance model and any randomized rounding.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A high-probability performance guarantee at tolerance \(\varepsilon\ge0\) and confidence \(1-\delta\) is \[\mathbb P\{L(I,A)\le\varepsilon\}\ge1-\delta,\] equivalently \(\mathbb P\{L(I,A)>\varepsilon\}\le\delta\). For maximization one may take \(L(I,A)=v^*(I)-v_A(I)\); for a multiplicative guarantee with \(v^*(I)>0\), one may instead require \(v_A(I)\ge\alpha v^*(I)\) on an event of probability at least \(1-\delta\). The governing probability space must state whether it averages over instances, algorithmic randomness, or both.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A high-probability guarantee says the chosen performance loss stays below a threshold except on an event whose probability is at most delta.
knowledge_statements.title: High-Probability Guarantees

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The probability and exceedance formulations are equivalent, but no source supports the precise joint-randomness convention. Since the statement defines a high-probability guarantee, definition is more appropriate than condition.

children.title: Expected-Performance Guarantees
children.top_down_role: Approximation quality measured through expected objective or recovery performance.

assumptions_latex: Let \(I\sim\mathbb P\) and include any algorithmic randomness in the joint probability space.
Let \(L(I,A)\ge0\) be measurable and integrable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Expected performance is controlled by an upper bound on \(\mathbb E[L(I,A)]\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Expectation over the declared instance and algorithmic probability space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An expected-performance guarantee with loss tolerance \(\varepsilon\ge0\) is \[\mathbb E_{I,A}[L(I,A)]\le\varepsilon.\] For a maximization problem, choosing \(L(I,A)=v^*(I)-v_A(I)\) yields \(\mathbb E[v_A(I)]\ge\mathbb E[v^*(I)]-\varepsilon\). If the guarantee is conditional on the instance, \(\mathbb E_A[L(I,A)\mid I]\le\varepsilon(I)\) must hold for the stated instances; averaging then gives \(\mathbb E_{I,A}[L(I,A)]\le\mathbb E_I[\varepsilon(I)]\), provided the quantities are integrable.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An expected guarantee bounds average performance loss under an explicitly declared distribution over instances, algorithmic randomness, or both.
knowledge_statements.title: Expected-Performance Guarantees

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No source is supplied for the expectation convention, and the displayed comparison of separate expectations additionally requires integrability of the optimal and returned values, not merely their nonnegative difference. The record defines a guarantee and should use definition rather than condition.

children.title: Distributional Instance Models
children.top_down_role: Average-case regimes organized by distributions imposed on problem instances.

assumptions_latex: Let \((\mathcal I,\mathcal F)\) be a measurable space of optimization instances.
Let \(\mathbb P_\theta\) be a specified probability law on that space.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A distributional guarantee is meaningful only relative to the declared family \(\{\mathbb P_\theta\}\) and its quantifiers.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Parametric probability models for random optimization instances.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A distributional instance model is a probability space \((\mathcal I,\mathcal F,\mathbb P_\theta)\), or a family \(\{\mathbb P_\theta:\theta\in\Theta\}\), whose outcomes determine all random data of an optimization instance. The model specification includes the joint law and dependence structure of those data. A pointwise distributional guarantee has the form \(G(\mathbb P_\theta)\) for every \(\theta\in\Theta\); a uniform guarantee requires \(\sup_{\theta\in\Theta}R(\mathbb P_\theta)\le c\). Randomness used by an algorithm is represented by an additional conditional kernel given the instance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A distributional instance model specifies a measurable instance space and a probability law, including dependence, with guarantees quantified pointwise or uniformly over the model family.
knowledge_statements.title: Distributional Instance Models

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Definition is the correct content kind and the model-family quantifiers are coherent, but the record lacks an authoritative source with a specific locator for the distributional-model and conditional-kernel formulation.

children.title: Tail-Risk Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Rare-event regimes where average performance obscures poor approximation outcomes.

knowledge_statements.title: Tail-Risk Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Expectation-to-tail conversion for a nonnegative random relaxation loss.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(L\ge 0\) be a random performance loss satisfying \(\mathbb E[L]\le \varepsilon\). For every \(t>0\), Markov's inequality gives \[\mathbb P\{L\ge t\}\le \min\{1,\varepsilon/t\}.\] Consequently, for \(0<\delta<1\), the upper \((1-\delta)\)-quantile \(\operatorname{VaR}_{1-\delta}(L):=\inf\{q:\mathbb P(L\le q)\ge 1-\delta\}\) is at most \(\varepsilon/\delta\). This order is unimprovable from the mean bound alone: a two-point distribution supported on \(\{0,t\}\) can attain \(\mathbb P(L\ge t)=\varepsilon/t\). Thus exponential or sub-Gaussian tails require additional distributional assumptions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A mean-loss guarantee yields only an inverse-linear tail bound; substantially faster tail decay requires additional concentration assumptions.
assumptions_latex: \(L\) is a nonnegative random variable.
\(\mathbb E[L]\le \varepsilon<\infty\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb P(L\ge t)\le \min\{1,\varepsilon/t\}\) and \(\operatorname{VaR}_{1-\delta}(L)\le \varepsilon/\delta\).

notation.meaning: Upper quantile at confidence level one minus delta

knowledge_statements.title: Nesterov Quadratic Approximation Family
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The real positive-semidefinite quadratic maximization bound over a hypercube.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A\in\mathbb S_+^n\), and define \(v:=\max\{x^{\mathsf T}Ax:x\in[-1,1]^n\}\) and \(v_{\mathrm{sdp}}:=\max\{\langle A,X\rangle:X\succeq0,\ X_{ii}\le1\}\). Then \[\frac{2}{\pi}v_{\mathrm{sdp}}\le v\le v_{\mathrm{sdp}}.\] If \(X^\star\) is SDP-optimal, normalize it to a correlation matrix and sample a centered Gaussian vector with that correlation; componentwise sign rounding produces a feasible vector \(\widehat x\in\{-1,1\}^n\) satisfying \(\mathbb E[\widehat x^{\mathsf T}A\widehat x]\ge(2/\pi)v_{\mathrm{sdp}}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a positive-semidefinite quadratic maximized over a box, Gaussian sign rounding achieves at least two over pi times the SDP value.
assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb S_+^n\).
The SDP optimum is finite and attained.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((2/\pi)v_{\mathrm{sdp}}\le v\le v_{\mathrm{sdp}}\).

knowledge_statements.title: Diagonal-Quadratic Approximation Family
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact diagonal reduction of a homogeneous quadratically constrained quadratic program.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \(Q_0,Q_1,\ldots,Q_m\in\mathbb S^n\) are diagonal. For the finite-valued problem \[v:=\sup\{x^{\mathsf T}Q_0x:x^{\mathsf T}Q_jx\le b_j,\ j=1,\ldots,m\},\] set \(z_i=x_i^2\). Then \[v=\sup\{\operatorname{diag}(Q_0)^{\mathsf T}z:\operatorname{diag}(Q_j)^{\mathsf T}z\le b_j,\ z\ge0\}.\] Every feasible \(z\) is realized by choosing \(x_i=\sqrt{z_i}\), so the lifted SDP has the same value and admits a rank-one optimal solution whenever the displayed linear program attains its optimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Simultaneously diagonal homogeneous quadratics reduce to a nonnegative linear program, making the SDP relaxation value-exact and rank-one recoverable.
assumptions_latex: \(Q_0,\ldots,Q_m\) are real symmetric diagonal matrices.
The quadratic program has finite value.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The quadratic program, its nonnegative linear reduction, and its SDP relaxation have equal optimal values.

knowledge_statements.title: Hidden-Convexity Exactness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Value and solution exactness for the classical trust-region SDP.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Q\in\mathbb S^n\), \(c\in\mathbb R^n\), and \(\Delta>0\). The trust-region problem \[v:=\min\{x^{\mathsf T}Qx+2c^{\mathsf T}x:\|x\|_2^2\le\Delta\}\] has the same value as \[\min\{\langle Q,X\rangle+2c^{\mathsf T}x:\begin{pmatrix}1&x^{\mathsf T}\\x&X\end{pmatrix}\succeq0,\ \operatorname{tr}(X)\le\Delta\}.\] Moreover, an optimal vector for the original problem can be recovered from an optimal relaxed solution. Thus the apparently nonconvex quadratic problem possesses a lossless semidefinite representation despite indefinite \(Q\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The trust-region quadratic problem has a lossless SDP relaxation and permits recovery of an original optimal vector even when its Hessian is indefinite.
assumptions_latex: \(Q\in\mathbb S^n\) and \(c\in\mathbb R^n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The trust-region problem and its lifted SDP have equal values, with an original optimizer recoverable from an SDP optimum.

knowledge_statements.title: Lossless Lagrangian Duality
knowledge_statements.scope_note: S-lemma duality for one real quadratic inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(q_i(x)=x^{\mathsf T}Q_ix+2c_i^{\mathsf T}x+d_i\) for \(i\in\{0,1\}\), where \(Q_i\in\mathbb S^n\). If some \(\bar x\) satisfies \(q_1(\bar x)<0\) and \(v:=\inf\{q_0(x):q_1(x)\le0\}>-\infty\), then \[v=\sup_{\lambda\ge0}\inf_{x\in\mathbb R^n}\bigl(q_0(x)+\lambda q_1(x)\bigr).\] Equivalently, the Lagrangian dual and the standard lifted SDP relaxation have no value gap from the one-constraint quadratic problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A strictly feasible quadratic program with one quadratic inequality has no gap from its Lagrangian dual or standard SDP relaxation.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(m,n\in\mathbb N\), \(Q_0,Q_1,\ldots,Q_m\in\mathbb S^n\), and \(b_1,\ldots,b_m\in\mathbb R\). Define \[v:=\sup\{x^{\mathsf T}Q_0x:x\in\mathbb R^n,\ x^{\mathsf T}Q_jx\le b_j,\ j=1,\ldots,m\}\] and \[v_{\mathrm{sdp}}:=\sup\{\langle Q_0,X\rangle:X\succeq0,\ \langle Q_j,X\rangle\le b_j,\ j=1,\ldots,m\}.\] If an invertible matrix \(T\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) makes every matrix \(T^{\mathsf T}Q_jT\), for \(j=0,1,\ldots,m\), diagonal, then the substitution \(x=Ty\) and variables \(z_i=y_i^2\) give a linear program over \(z\ge0\) with value \(v=v_{\mathrm{sdp}}\). knowledge_statements.title: Rank-Restricted Exactness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Rank-one attainment as a directly checkable solution-exactness certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let an SDP relaxation use the lifted matrix \(Y=\begin{pmatrix}1&x^{\mathsf T}\\x&X\end{pmatrix}\succeq0\), with every original quadratic expression replaced by its corresponding linear functional of \(Y\). If an optimal relaxed solution \(Y^\star\) satisfies \(\operatorname{rank}(Y^\star)=1\), then its normalization \(Y^\star_{00}=1\) implies \(Y^\star=(1,(x^\star)^{\mathsf T})^{\mathsf T}(1,(x^\star)^{\mathsf T})\). The vector \(x^\star\) obeys every original quadratic constraint and has the SDP optimal value; therefore the relaxation is both value-exact and solution-exact.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An optimal normalized rank-one lifted matrix factors into an original feasible vector attaining the SDP value, certifying complete relaxation exactness.
assumptions_latex: The SDP is obtained by the standard quadratic lifting with \(Y_{00}=1\).
An SDP optimum \(Y^\star\) exists and has rank one.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The factor of \(Y^\star\) supplies an original optimizer, and the original and relaxed optimal values coincide.

knowledge_statements.title: Unique-Optimizer Exactness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uniqueness of a rank-one SDP optimizer as a strong solution-exactness condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal R\) be a standard lifted SDP relaxation of a quadratic optimization problem, and suppose \(\mathcal R\) has the unique optimizer \(Y^\star\). If \(Y^\star_{00}=1\) and \(\operatorname{rank}(Y^\star)=1\), then \(Y^\star=(1,(x^\star)^{\mathsf T})^{\mathsf T}(1,(x^\star)^{\mathsf T})\) for a feasible original vector \(x^\star\). This vector is an original optimizer. Moreover, every original optimizer has lift \(Y^\star\); hence, when the normalized lift determines its vector coordinate uniquely, \(x^\star\) is the unique original optimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A unique normalized rank-one SDP optimum recovers an original optimum and, under injective lifting, certifies uniqueness of that original solution.
assumptions_latex: The relaxation is a standard normalized quadratic lift.
Its unique optimizer \(Y^\star\) has rank one.
The normalized lift determines its vector coordinate uniquely.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The recovered \(x^\star\) is the unique original optimizer and the relaxation is solution-exact.

knowledge_statements.title: Face-Exposure Exactness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exactness certified by containment of the exposed optimal SDP face in the lifted feasible hull.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal S\subseteq\mathbb S_+^N\) be the feasible region of an SDP relaxation, let \(\mathcal K:=\operatorname{conv}\{yy^{\mathsf T}:y\text{ is a normalized feasible original lift}\}\), and assume \(\mathcal K\subseteq\mathcal S\). For a minimization objective \(C\), define the exposed optimal face \(F:=\{Y\in\mathcal S:\langle C,Y\rangle=v_{\mathrm{sdp}}\}\). If \(F\subseteq\mathcal K\), then the original and relaxed values coincide, and every relaxed optimizer is a convex combination of lifted original optimizers. If additionally \(F\) is a singleton generated by a rank-one lift, solution exactness follows.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exactness holds when the SDP objective exposes a face contained in the convex hull of feasible rank-one lifts.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal K\subseteq\mathcal S\) and the SDP optimum is attained.
The exposed optimal face satisfies \(F\subseteq\mathcal K\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The relaxation is value-exact; a singleton rank-one face additionally gives solution exactness.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A primal feasible matrix \(X\) is primal nondegenerate when the equality-constraint map covers the entire constraint space along the lineality space of the semidefinite tangent cone: \[\mathcal A\!\left(\operatorname{lin}T_{\mathbb S_+^n}(X)\right)=\mathbb R^m.\] Equivalently, if \(Q=[Q_1\ Q_0]\) is orthogonal with \(\operatorname{range}(Q_1)=\operatorname{range}(X)\), then every vector in \(\mathbb R^m\) is attained by \(\mathcal A(H)\) for some symmetric \(H\) satisfying \(Q_0^{\mathsf T}HQ_0=0\).

Nevertheless, \(\mathcal A(H)=(H_{11},H_{11})\) lies in the proper subspace \(\{(t,t):t\in\mathbb R\}\), even when \(H\) ranges over the tangent lineality space at \(X^*\). knowledge_statements.title: Dual-Corank Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Corank-one dual slack as a rank-one primal certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((X^*,Z^*)\) be a primal-dual optimal pair with \(X^*,Z^*\succeq0\), zero duality gap, and \(X^*\ne0\). If \[\operatorname{corank}(Z^*)=\dim\ker Z^*=1,\] then \[\operatorname{rank}(X^*)=1.\] Thus a corank-one dual slack, matching primal and dual objective values, and a normalization excluding \(X^*=0\) form a rank-one recovery certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonzero complementary primal matrix must be rank one when the optimal dual slack has a one-dimensional nullspace.
assumptions_latex: A primal-dual optimal pair \((X^*,Z^*)\) satisfies \(X^*,Z^*\succeq0\) and zero duality gap.
The primal normalization excludes \(X^*=0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(\operatorname{corank}(Z^*)=1\), then \(\operatorname{rank}(X^*)=1\).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Compute an optimal dual slack \(Z^*\) and a nonzero vector \(v\in\ker Z^*\). Complementarity yields \(\operatorname{range}(X^*)\subseteq\ker Z^*\). If \(\ker Z^*=\operatorname{span}\{v\}\), determine \(\alpha>0\) from the primal affine normalization and set \[X_{\mathrm{rec}}=\alpha vv^{\mathsf T}.\] Verify \(\mathcal A(X_{\mathrm{rec}})=b\) and equality with the certified optimal objective. Output \(X_{\mathrm{rec}}\), together with a compatible vector factor, only when these checks pass; otherwise report that complementarity alone did not identify a rank-one solution.

Complementarity is equivalent to \(\operatorname{range}(X^*)\subseteq\ker Z^*\), and therefore \[X^*=VHV^{\mathsf T}\quad\text{for some}\quad H\in\mathbb S_+^k.\] Conversely, every matrix of this form is positive semidefinite and satisfies \(X^*Z^*=0\). children.title: Corank-Mismatch Boundary
children.top_down_role: Cases where dual corank does not isolate the intended rank-one solution.

assumptions_latex: A nonzero primal optimum \(X^*\succeq0\) is complementary to a dual optimal slack \(Z^*\succeq0\).

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Corank one certifies rank one; corank greater than one gives only \(\operatorname{rank}(X^*)\le\operatorname{corank}(Z^*)\) and is inconclusive.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Complementarity implies \[\operatorname{rank}(X^*)\le\dim\ker Z^*=\operatorname{corank}(Z^*).\] Consequently, \(\operatorname{corank}(Z^*)=1\) certifies rank one for nonzero \(X^*\). If \(\operatorname{corank}(Z^*)=k>1\), the same information permits every rank from \(1\) through \(k\); additional affine constraints or facial information are required. If \(\operatorname{corank}(Z^*)=0\), complementarity forces \(X^*=0\), contradicting any nonzero normalization. Thus mismatch between desired rank and dual corank is the precise boundary of a corank-only certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Complementarity certifies rank one only at dual corank one; larger nullspaces permit higher-rank primal optima.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Factor the current optimum as \(X=VRV^{\mathsf T}\), where \(R\succ0\). Find \(D\in\mathbb S^r\setminus\{0\}\) satisfying \[\mathcal A(VDV^{\mathsf T})=0\quad\text{and}\quad\langle C,VDV^{\mathsf T}\rangle=0.\] Choose a sign and the largest \(t>0\) for which \(R+tD\succeq0\), then update \(X\leftarrow V(R+tD)V^{\mathsf T}\). The update preserves feasibility and objective value and makes the reduced matrix singular. Repeat until no such direction exists; output the resulting lower-rank optimal matrix.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Move within the optimal face along a constraint-preserving direction until an eigenvalue vanishes, then repeat.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Compute a positive rank-one decomposition \[X^*=\sum_{j=1}^q\lambda_jv_jv_j^{\mathsf T},\qquad \lambda_j>0.\] For each component, apply the lift's required normalization to form a candidate \(X_j\) of rank one. Output the first candidate passing all tests. If no component passes, the decomposition alone supplies no exact recovery, even though its weighted sum equals \(X^*\).

knowledge_statements.title: Extreme-Point Recovery
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Barvinok-Pataki rank bound used for extreme-point recovery.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X^*\) be an extreme point of an SDP optimal spectrahedron described by \(m\) linearly independent affine equalities, and let \(r=\operatorname{rank}(X^*)\). Then \[\frac{r(r+1)}{2}\le m.\] Hence an extreme optimal solution has the corresponding certified rank bound. In particular, if \(m\le2\) and \(X^*\ne0\), then \(r=1\), yielding rank-one recovery.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An extreme SDP optimum has rank satisfying the Barvinok-Pataki bound; with at most two independent equalities it is rank one.
assumptions_latex: The optimal set of the SDP contains an extreme point \(X^*\), and \(m\) is the number of linearly independent affine equalities describing the optimal spectrahedron.
The feasible set has no zero matrix when rank-one recovery is sought.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every such extreme point satisfies \(r(r+1)/2\le m\), where \(r=\operatorname{rank}(X^*)\); hence \(m\le2\) forces \(r=1\).

notation.meaning: Number of independent affine equalities describing the optimal spectrahedron.

children.title: Nonunique-Decomposition Boundary
children.top_down_role: Ambiguity arising when decompositions produce multiple incompatible candidates.

knowledge_statements.title: Nonunique-Decomposition Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Characterizes loss of uniqueness for spectral rank-one decompositions of a positive semidefinite matrix.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\in\mathbb S_+^n\) have positive eigenvalues \(\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_r\). Its orthogonal spectral decomposition \(X=\sum_{i=1}^r\lambda_i u_i u_i^{\mathsf T}\) is unique up to permutation and sign changes of the vectors exactly when all positive eigenvalues are simple. If a positive eigenvalue has multiplicity at least two, any orthogonal rotation within its eigenspace produces a different collection of rank-one summands with the same sum; hence decomposition-based recovery does not identify unique factors.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repeated positive eigenvalues permit rotations within an eigenspace, so the PSD matrix no longer determines unique spectral rank-one factors.
assumptions_latex: \(X\in\mathbb S_+^n\).
Only orthogonal spectral rank-one decompositions are compared.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A repeated positive eigenvalue is precisely the boundary for uniqueness up to signs and permutation.

notation.meaning: Cone of real symmetric positive semidefinite matrices.

knowledge_statements.title: Spectral Rank Diagnostics
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact and tolerance-based spectral diagnostics for rank-one positive semidefinite SDP solutions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(n\geq2\) and let \(X\in\mathbb S_+^n\setminus\{0\}\) have ordered eigenvalues \(\lambda_1\geq\cdots\geq\lambda_n\geq0\). Exact rank-one recovery is certified by \(\lambda_2=0\), in which case \(\lambda_1>0\) and \(X=xx^{\mathsf T}\) for \(x=\sqrt{\lambda_1}u_1\). For a numerical tolerance \(\tau\geq0\), the effective-rank diagnostic declares rank one when \(\lambda_2\leq\tau\lambda_1\). This approximate declaration is not an exact rank certificate unless \(\tau=0\); it only gives \(\lVert X-\lambda_1u_1u_1^{\mathsf T}\rVert_2=\lambda_2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a nonzero PSD matrix of dimension at least two, the second eigenvalue certifies exact rank one when zero and quantifies the spectral error of the leading rank-one approximation otherwise.
assumptions_latex: \(X\in\mathbb S_+^n\setminus\{0\}\).
Eigenvalues are ordered nonincreasingly.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{rank}(X)=1\iff\lambda_2=0\), and \(\lVert X-\lambda_1u_1u_1^{\mathsf T}\rVert_2=\lambda_2\).

children.title: Spectral Rounding
children.top_down_role: Candidate recovery using dominant spectral structure of a near-rank-one solution.

knowledge_statements.title: Spectral Rounding
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic leading-eigenvector rounding template for a lifted semidefinite solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a nonzero matrix \(X\in\mathbb S_+^n\), an original feasible set \(F\subseteq\mathbb R^n\), a deterministic rounding map \(\Pi_F:\mathbb R^n\to F\), an objective \(f:F\to\mathbb R\), and whether \(f\) is minimized or maximized. Compute a largest eigenpair \((\lambda_1,u_1)\) with \(\lVert u_1\rVert_2=1\), form \(y=\sqrt{\lambda_1}u_1\), and set \(x_+=\Pi_F(y)\) and \(x_-=\Pi_F(-y)\). Return the candidate with the smaller value of \(f\) for minimization or the larger value of \(f\) for maximization.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Round both signs of the leading rank-one factor into the original feasible set and retain the candidate with the better original objective value.
assumptions_latex: \(X\in\mathbb S_+^n\setminus\{0\}\).
\(F\subseteq\mathbb R^n\).
\(\Pi_F(z)\in F\) for every \(z\in\mathbb R^n\).
\(f:F\to\mathbb R\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The returned point belongs to \(F\) and is at least as good under \(f\) as the other sign candidate.

children.title: Randomized Rounding
children.top_down_role: Candidate recovery using randomized sampling informed by the relaxed matrix.

knowledge_statements.title: Randomized Rounding
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Gaussian covariance rounding template for a positive semidefinite relaxation solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input \(X\in\mathbb S_+^n\), a feasible rounding map \(\Pi_F:\mathbb R^n\to F\), an objective \(f:F\to\mathbb R\), and a sample count \(N\in\mathbb N\) with \(N\geq1\). Choose \(r\in\mathbb N\) and \(V\in\mathbb R^{n\times r}\) such that \(X=VV^{\mathsf T}\). Independently draw \(g_k\sim\mathcal N(0,I_r)\), set \(y_k=Vg_k\), and form \(x_k=\Pi_F(y_k)\) for \(k=1,\ldots,N\). For minimization, output an element of \(\operatorname*{argmin}_{1\leq k\leq N}f(x_k)\); for maximization, output an element of \(\operatorname*{argmax}_{1\leq k\leq N}f(x_k)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Draw Gaussian vectors whose covariance is the SDP matrix, round each one feasibly, and retain the sampled candidate with the best original objective value.
assumptions_latex: \(X\in\mathbb S_+^n\).
\(F\subseteq\mathbb R^n\).
\(\Pi_F(y)\in F\) for every \(y\in\mathbb R^n\).
\(f:F\to\mathbb R\).
\(N\in\mathbb N\) and \(N\geq1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The selected output belongs to \(F\), and its objective is no worse than that of any sampled candidate.

notation.meaning: A matrix factor in R^{n by r} satisfying X equals V times its transpose.

children.title: Local Recovery Refinement
children.top_down_role: Post-rounding improvement of recovered candidates within the original feasible geometry.

knowledge_statements.title: Local Recovery Refinement
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Monotone local improvement applied after feasible SDP rounding.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For minimization, input a rounded point \(x_0\in F\), objective \(f:F\to\mathbb R\), neighborhood oracle \(\mathcal N:F\to2^F\), tolerance \(\varepsilon\geq0\), and iteration limit \(T\). At iteration \(t<T\), choose \(y_t\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{y\in\mathcal N(x_t)}f(y)\). If \(f(y_t)\leq f(x_t)-\varepsilon\), set \(x_{t+1}=y_t\); otherwise stop and output \(x_t\). If no earlier stop occurs, output \(x_T\). For maximization, reverse the inequalities and optimize over the neighborhood by maximization.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Starting from a feasible rounded point, repeatedly accept a sufficiently improving feasible neighbor and return the final feasible iterate.
assumptions_latex: Each \(\mathcal N(x)\) is nonempty, contained in \(F\), and admits an optimizer.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every iterate is feasible and the accepted objective sequence is monotone.

notation.meaning: Set of feasible local candidates around x.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The generic monotone local-search algorithm is coherent, but no source supports its placement or formulation as an SDP recovery-refinement method.

children.title: Rounding-Stability Boundary
children.top_down_role: Sensitivity of recovered candidates to spectral noise, tolerances, or perturbations.

knowledge_statements.title: Rounding-Stability Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Identifies the eigengap boundary governing stability of leading-eigenvector rounding.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\in\mathbb S_+^n\) have \(\lambda_1(X)>\lambda_2(X)\), and let \(\widetilde X=X+E\) be symmetric. If \(\lVert E\rVert_2<\bigl(\lambda_1(X)-\lambda_2(X)\bigr)/2\), the leading eigenspaces remain one-dimensional and their angular displacement is controlled by the perturbation-to-gap ratio. At the boundary \(\lambda_1(X)=\lambda_2(X)\), no uniform continuity bound for a selected leading eigenvector exists: arbitrarily small symmetric perturbations can select orthogonal directions inside the repeated top eigenspace, producing discontinuous rounded outputs.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Leading-eigenvector rounding is stable only relative to a positive top eigengap; at a repeated top eigenvalue, tiny perturbations can change direction drastically.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) and \(E\) are real symmetric.
Rounding depends nontrivially on a selected leading eigenvector.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A positive top eigengap enables perturbation control, whereas a zero eigengap destroys uniform directional stability.

notation.meaning: Symmetric perturbation of the SDP solution.

children.title: Higher-Rank Optima
children.top_down_role: Optimal SDP solutions whose intrinsic rank exceeds one.

knowledge_statements.title: Higher-Rank Optima
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separates existence of an SDP optimum from existence of a rank-one optimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider an SDP with nonempty optimal set \(\mathcal X^\star\subseteq\mathbb S_+^n\). If \(\min_{X\in\mathcal X^\star}\operatorname{rank}(X)>1\), then the relaxation has no rank-one optimal matrix and direct factor recovery \(X=xx^{\mathsf T}\) is impossible at the relaxation optimum. The existence of one computed higher-rank optimum alone is insufficient for this conclusion, because the same optimal face may also contain an uncomputed rank-one matrix.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Rank-one optimal recovery fails only when every SDP optimum has rank above one, not merely when a solver returns one higher-rank optimum.
assumptions_latex: The SDP optimal set \(\mathcal X^\star\) is nonempty.
Original recovery requires an optimal matrix of the form \(xx^{\mathsf T}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\min_{X\in\mathcal X^\star}\operatorname{rank}(X)>1\) excludes rank-one recovery at optimality.

children.title: Multiple Optimizers
children.top_down_role: Problem instances admitting several distinct original optimizers.

knowledge_statements.title: Multiple Optimizers
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nonuniqueness boundary for identifying a single recovered solution from an SDP optimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal X^\star\) be the optimal set of an SDP relaxation. If it contains distinct rank-one matrices \(x_1x_1^{\mathsf T}\neq x_2x_2^{\mathsf T}\), then optimality and the SDP data alone do not identify a unique lifted solution. Convexity implies that every matrix \(X_\theta=\theta x_1x_1^{\mathsf T}+(1-\theta)x_2x_2^{\mathsf T}\), with \(0<\theta<1\), is also optimal. Such a mixture has rank at most two, and it has rank two exactly when \(x_1\) and \(x_2\) are linearly independent. Thus, when linearly independent rank-one optima exist, a solver may return a higher-rank optimum even though rank-one optima also exist.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Distinct rank-one optima prevent unique identification; when their generating vectors are linearly independent, the optimal set also contains rank-two mixtures.
assumptions_latex: The SDP feasible region is convex and its objective is linear.
\(x_1x_1^{\mathsf T}\) and \(x_2x_2^{\mathsf T}\) are distinct rank-one optimal matrices.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Optimality does not ensure unique recovery, and \(\operatorname{rank}(X_\theta)=2\) precisely when \(x_1\) and \(x_2\) are linearly independent.

notation.meaning: Convex-combination weight in the open unit interval.
Convex mixture of the two rank-one optimal matrices.

children.title: Convex-Hull Ambiguity
children.top_down_role: Relaxed optima representing mixtures of multiple recoverable solutions.

knowledge_statements.title: Convex-Hull Ambiguity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Explains ambiguity introduced when an SDP relaxation represents convex mixtures of lifted feasible points.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S=\{xx^{\mathsf T}:x\in F\}\subseteq\mathbb S_+^n\), and suppose a relaxation contains \(\operatorname{conv}(S)\). If \(X=\sum_{i=1}^k\alpha_i x_ix_i^{\mathsf T}\) with \(k\geq2\), \(\alpha_i>0\), \(\sum_i\alpha_i=1\), and at least two distinct lifted matrices, then \(X\) encodes only their convex mixture. Unless the decomposition and a component-selection rule are uniquely determined, \(X\) does not specify which original feasible point should be recovered; if \(X\) has rank greater than one, it is itself not a lifted point in \(S\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A convex mixture of distinct lifted feasible points need not identify any unique original point and is not rank one when its span is multidimensional.
assumptions_latex: \(F\subseteq\mathbb R^n\).
The relaxation admits convex combinations of lifted feasible points.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A nontrivial mixture generally provides no unique inverse under the lifting map \(x\mapsto xx^{\mathsf T}\).

notation.meaning: Set of rank-one lifts of original feasible points.

children.title: Rank-One Recovery Failure
children.top_down_role: Conditions under which no unique rank-one candidate can be extracted.

knowledge_statements.title: Rank-One Recovery Failure
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Formal failure criterion for exact recovery from an optimal semidefinite relaxation matrix.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be the original feasible set and let \(\mathcal X^\star\) be the SDP optimal set. Exact rank-one recovery fails when \(\mathcal X^\star\cap\{xx^{\mathsf T}:x\in F\}=\varnothing\). This condition means that no optimal relaxation matrix is the lift of an original feasible point. It is stronger than failure of a particular eigendecomposition or rounding method and remains valid even when approximate or suboptimal feasible recovery is possible.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact recovery fails precisely when the SDP optimal set contains no rank-one lift of an original feasible point.
assumptions_latex: Original solutions are lifted by \(x\mapsto xx^{\mathsf T}\).
The SDP optimal set \(\mathcal X^\star\) is nonempty.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Exact optimal recovery is impossible if and only if \(\mathcal X^\star\cap\{xx^{\mathsf T}:x\in F\}=\varnothing\).

notation.meaning: Optimal set of the SDP relaxation.

knowledge_statements.title: Explicit Gap Instances
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic instance families certifying an additive integrality gap for an SDP relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a minimization problem, let \(p(I)\) be the original optimum and \(s(I)\) the SDP-relaxation optimum on instance \(I\), so \(s(I)\leq p(I)\). An explicit gap family is a deterministically specified sequence \((I_n)_{n\geq1}\) together with a stated function \(\Delta(n)>0\) and verifiable bounds \(p(I_n)\geq L_n\) and \(s(I_n)\leq U_n\) satisfying \(L_n-U_n\geq\Delta(n)\). These two bounds certify \(p(I_n)-s(I_n)\geq\Delta(n)\). For maximization, reverse the relaxation inequality and corresponding bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An explicit family certifies an SDP gap by deterministic original-value and relaxation-value bounds separated by a stated amount.
assumptions_latex: Every instance \(I_n\) and its SDP relaxation are finitely and deterministically specified.
The original and relaxed objectives use the same normalization.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed bounds certify an additive integrality gap of at least \(\Delta(n)\).

notation.meaning: Original problem optimum on instance I.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The record gives only a generic gap-certification template. It supplies no explicit problem, deterministic instance family, or instance-specific gap bounds, so it is neither an explicit gap instance nor a certificate appropriate to this exact terminal container.

knowledge_statements.title: Probabilistic Gap Constructions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: High-probability construction scheme for proving SDP integrality gaps on random instances.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(I_n\sim\mathcal D_n\) be a random minimization instance, with original optimum \(p(I_n)\) and SDP optimum \(s(I_n)\). If there are deterministic sequences \(L_n,U_n\) and \(\delta_n\in[0,1]\) such that \(L_n-U_n\geq\Delta_n>0\) and \(\Pr\{p(I_n)\geq L_n\text{ and }s(I_n)\leq U_n\}\geq1-\delta_n\), then \(\Pr\{p(I_n)-s(I_n)\geq\Delta_n\}\geq1-\delta_n\). Consequently, whenever \(\delta_n<1\), at least one deterministic instance in the support of \(\mathcal D_n\) has that gap.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Separated high-probability bounds on the original and SDP optima yield a high-probability gap and imply existence of a deterministic gap instance.
assumptions_latex: \(I_n\) is sampled from a specified distribution \(\mathcal D_n\).
Both optima use the same objective normalization.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The gap is at least \(\Delta_n\) with probability at least \(1-\delta_n\), and a deterministic witness exists if \(\delta_n<1\).

notation.meaning: Distribution over instances of size n.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The probabilistic implication is mathematically valid and principle is a plausible content kind, but no actual random construction, problem class, distribution, or supporting source is supplied.

assumptions_latex: \(G\) is a finite group acting linearly on a lifted matrix space.
The minimization SDP feasible region \(\mathcal R\) is convex and \(G\)-invariant, and its objective \(c\) satisfies \(c(gY)=c(Y)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{gap}=\beta-\alpha>0\) is an integrality-gap certificate whenever \(\alpha<\beta\).

notation.meaning: relaxation value attained by an invariant feasible point

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: convex averaging over a finite symmetry group preserves invariant SDP constraints and objectives

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-group averaging principle for constructing symmetric SDP gap witnesses.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every \(Y\in\mathcal R\), the Reynolds average \(P_G(Y)=|G|^{-1}\sum_{g\in G}gY\) belongs to \(\mathcal R\), is fixed by every \(g\in G\), and satisfies \(c(P_G(Y))=c(Y)\). Consequently the SDP optimum may be sought in the fixed-point subspace. If an invariant feasible point \(\bar Y\) has value \(\alpha=c(\bar Y)\), while every feasible solution of the original minimization problem has value at least \(\beta>\alpha\), then the instance has additive integrality gap at least \(\beta-\alpha\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Averaging any SDP solution over its finite symmetry group preserves feasibility and value. An invariant relaxation value below the exact optimum therefore certifies an integrality gap.
knowledge_statements.title: Symmetry-Based Gap Constructions

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The finite-group averaging argument and resulting additive-gap certificate are mathematically coherent and fit the symmetry-based construction container, but no inspectable source is cited for the symmetry-reduction and gap-construction claim.

assumptions_latex: \(n,a,b,r\in\mathbb N\), \(f,h_1,\ldots,h_a,g_1,\ldots,g_b\in\mathbb R[x]\), and \(x\in\mathbb R^n\).
The polynomial problem is \(f^*=\min\{f(x):h_i(x)=0\ (i=1,\ldots,a),\ g_j(x)\ge0\ (j=1,\ldots,b)\}\), and \(f^*\) is finite.
The objective satisfies \(\deg(f)\le 2r\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(\widetilde{\mathbb E}[f]=\alpha<f^*=\beta\), then the level-\(r\) relaxation has additive integrality gap at least \(\beta-\alpha\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Degree-bounded pseudoexpectation certificate for a polynomial-optimization SDP gap.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A degree-\(2r\) pseudoexpectation is a linear functional \(\widetilde{\mathbb E}:\mathbb R[x]_{\le 2r}\to\mathbb R\) satisfying \(\widetilde{\mathbb E}[1]=1\), \(\widetilde{\mathbb E}[q^2]\ge0\) whenever \(\deg(q^2)\le2r\), \(\widetilde{\mathbb E}[h_i p]=0\) for every \(i\in\{1,\ldots,a\}\) whenever \(\deg(h_i p)\le2r\), and \(\widetilde{\mathbb E}[g_jq^2]\ge0\) for every \(j\in\{1,\ldots,b\}\) whenever \(\deg(g_jq^2)\le2r\). These conditions are represented by moment-matrix and localizing-matrix positive semidefiniteness together with the equality moment equations. If \(\widetilde{\mathbb E}[f]=\alpha\) and the true minimum is \(f^*=\beta>\alpha\), then \(\widetilde{\mathbb E}\) certifies a level-\(r\) additive gap of at least \(\beta-\alpha\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A normalized pseudoexpectation satisfying base square positivity, all degree-bounded equality equations, and all degree-bounded localizing positivity tests is feasible for the moment SDP. If its objective is below the true minimum, it certifies a relaxation gap.
knowledge_statements.title: Pseudoexpectation Gap Witnesses

For every \(s\le R\), its restriction to \(\mathbb R[x]_{\le2s}\) preserves normalization, all applicable equality constraints, and every positivity test of degree at most \(2s\); hence it is feasible for level \(s\). If \(\deg f\le2r\) and the true minimum satisfies \(f^*\ge\beta>\alpha\), then every level \(s\) with \(r\le s\le R\) has relaxation value at most \(\alpha\) and additive gap at least \(\beta-\alpha\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Adaptive schedule for selecting successive orders in a nested minimization hierarchy.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input an initial order \(r_0\), tolerance \(\varepsilon\), limit \(r_{\max}\), update map \(U\), and optionally a certified feasible value \(U^*\). Set \(k=0\). Solve relaxation \(r_k\) to obtain \(L_{r_k}\). Stop with status tolerance-reached if \(U^*-L_{r_k}\le\varepsilon\); stop with status budget-exhausted if \(r_k=r_{\max}\). Otherwise set \(r_{k+1}=\min\{U(r_k),r_{\max}\}\), increment \(k\), and repeat. When no \(U^*\) is available, replace the tolerance test by a declared bound-stagnation or resource criterion.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Solve increasingly strong relaxation orders until the certified optimality gap meets tolerance or the order budget is exhausted; otherwise advance using the prescribed update rule.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \(L_r=\inf\{c(Y):Y\in\mathcal R_r\}\). Since \(\mathcal R_{r+1}\subseteq\mathcal R_r\), minimizing over level \(r+1\) cannot produce a smaller value, so \(L_r\le L_{r+1}\). If every exact feasible solution admits a feasible lift in every \(\mathcal R_r\) with unchanged objective, then \(L_{r+1}\le f^*\). Therefore \((L_r)\) is a nondecreasing sequence of valid lower bounds on the exact minimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nested minimization relaxations produce nondecreasing lower bounds, and every bound remains no larger than the exact optimum.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Additive decomposition of cumulative hierarchy improvement into one-level gains.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For consecutive relaxation values define the marginal tightening gain by \(\Delta_r=L_{r+1}-L_r\). Monotonicity gives \(\Delta_r\ge0\). For any integers \(t>r\), cancellation of intermediate bounds yields \[L_t-L_r=\sum_{s=r}^{t-1}(L_{s+1}-L_s)=\sum_{s=r}^{t-1}\Delta_s.\] Thus \(\Delta_r=0\) records no one-level improvement, while the cumulative strengthening over an order interval is exactly the sum of its marginal gains.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The gain from one hierarchy level is the difference of consecutive bounds. These gains are nonnegative and telescope to the total improvement over any order interval.
knowledge_statements.title: Marginal Tightening Gains
