children.top_down_role: Hierarchy ranges where higher order produces negligible bound improvement.

assumptions_latex: The nested feasible sets \(\mathcal R_{r+1}\subseteq\mathcal R_r\) are nonempty.
Both level optima are attained for the common objective \(c\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L_{r+1}=L_r\) if and only if \(\operatorname*{argmin}_{\mathcal R_r}c\cap\mathcal R_{r+1}\ne\varnothing\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: the equivalence follows directly from nested feasible sets and attainment
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact criterion for one-step bound stagnation under attainment.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(L_s=\min\{c(Y):Y\in\mathcal R_s\}\) for \(s\in\{r,r+1\}\). The bound stagnates from level \(r\) to level \(r+1\), meaning \(L_{r+1}=L_r\), exactly when some level-\(r\) minimizer remains feasible at level \(r+1\): \[\operatorname*{argmin}_{Y\in\mathcal R_r}c(Y)\cap\mathcal R_{r+1}\ne\varnothing.\] This condition concerns equality of consecutive values only; it does not imply that either value equals the exact optimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Two consecutive attained bounds are equal exactly when at least one optimizer of the weaker relaxation remains feasible for the stronger relaxation.
knowledge_statements.title: Bound-Stagnation Regimes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The equivalence is correct for nested nonempty feasible sets when both minima are attained, and it appropriately avoids claiming global optimality. The condition fits the bound-stagnation container, but no inspectable source is supplied.

children.title: Moment-Matrix Dimension Growth
children.top_down_role: Growth of moment-matrix dimensions with variable count and relaxation order.

assumptions_latex: The variables are \(x\in\mathbb R^n\).
The order-\(r\) moment matrix is indexed by monomials of total degree at most \(r\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Its dimension is \(N(n,r)=\binom{n+r}{r}\), with \(N(n,r)(N(n,r)+1)/2\) upper-triangular scalar positions.

notation.meaning: number of monomials in n variables of degree at most r

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dense total-degree moment-matrix size in the commutative hierarchy.

source_refs.locator: 3.2.1 Moment and localizing matrix p. 58
source_refs.source_title: Moments, Positive Polynomials and Their Applications

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The monomial vector \(v_r(x)=(x^\alpha)_{|\alpha|\le r}\) has length \[N(n,r)=\#\{\alpha\in\mathbb N^n:|\alpha|\le r\}=\binom{n+r}{r}.\] Hence the dense moment matrix \(M_r(y)=(y_{\alpha+\beta})_{|\alpha|,|\beta|\le r}\) is an \(N(n,r)\times N(n,r)\) positive semidefinite block. Its symmetric upper triangle contains \(N(n,r)(N(n,r)+1)/2\) scalar positions. For fixed \(r\), \(N(n,r)=\Theta(n^r)\); for fixed \(n\), \(N(n,r)=\Theta(r^n)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An order-r dense moment matrix has one row per monomial of degree at most r, namely binomial(n+r,r) rows, with corresponding polynomial growth in fixed dimension or order.
knowledge_statements.title: Moment-Matrix Dimension Growth

source_witnesses.locator: 3.2.1 Moment and localizing matrix p. 58

children.title: Localizing-Matrix Dimension Growth
children.top_down_role: Growth of localizing-matrix blocks induced by polynomial constraints.

assumptions_latex: The inequality polynomial \(g\in\mathbb R[x]\) has degree \(d\).
The relaxation order satisfies \(r\ge\lceil d/2\rceil\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The localizing matrix has dimension \(N(n,r-\lceil d/2\rceil)=\binom{n+r-\lceil d/2\rceil}{r-\lceil d/2\rceil}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dense localizing-matrix size determined by relaxation order and constraint degree.

source_refs.locator: 3.2.1 Moment and localizing matrix p. 58
source_refs.source_title: Moments, Positive Polynomials and Their Applications

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Set \(d_g=\lceil\deg(g)/2\rceil\). At relaxation order \(r\ge d_g\), positivity of \(g\) is imposed through \(M_{r-d_g}(gy)\succeq0\), indexed by monomials \(x^\alpha\) with \(|\alpha|\le r-d_g\). Therefore its row and column dimension is \[N(n,r-d_g)=\binom{n+r-d_g}{r-d_g}.\] Its symmetric upper triangle has \(N(n,r-d_g)(N(n,r-d_g)+1)/2\) scalar positions, so higher-degree constraints produce smaller localizing blocks at a fixed relaxation order.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A degree-d inequality at order r uses monomials only through degree r-ceil(d/2), giving a localizing block of the corresponding binomial dimension.
knowledge_statements.title: Localizing-Matrix Dimension Growth

children.title: Constraint-Count Growth
children.top_down_role: Expansion in equality, consistency, or semidefinite constraints across hierarchy levels.

assumptions_latex: A dense order-\(r\) relaxation has \(m\) polynomial inequalities \(g_j(x)\ge0\).
For each inequality, \(d_j=\lceil\deg(g_j)/2\rceil\le r\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: There are \(m+1\) PSD blocks and \(S_r=\frac{N_r(N_r+1)}2+\sum_{j=1}^m\frac{N_j(N_j+1)}2\) symmetric scalar positions.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: PSD-block and scalar-position counts for a dense inequality-only moment relaxation.

source_refs.locator: 3.2.1 Moment and localizing matrix p. 58
source_refs.source_title: Moments, Positive Polynomials and Their Applications

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The dense order-\(r\) relaxation contains one PSD constraint \(M_r(y)\succeq0\) and one PSD constraint \(M_{r-d_j}(g_jy)\succeq0\) for each \(j=1,\ldots,m\), hence \(m+1\) PSD blocks. Writing \(N_r=\binom{n+r}{r}\) and \(N_j=\binom{n+r-d_j}{r-d_j}\), their symmetric scalar positions total \[S_r=\frac{N_r(N_r+1)}2+\sum_{j=1}^m\frac{N_j(N_j+1)}2.\] Additional polynomial equalities generate separate linear moment equations and are not included in this count.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With m inequalities, the dense relaxation has one moment block and m localizing blocks. Their scalar position count is the sum of the blocks' triangular sizes.
knowledge_statements.title: Constraint-Count Growth

children.title: Memory-Limiting Regimes
children.top_down_role: Problem regimes where representation size becomes the principal computational limit.

assumptions_latex: All moment and localizing PSD blocks are stored densely.
The available memory holds at most \(B\) scalar words.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Dense assembly is memory-infeasible whenever \(N_r^2+\sum_{j=1}^mN_j^2>B\), up to fixed implementation constants.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: dense storage of a matrix block requires a quadratic number of scalar words
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Memory failure boundary for dense storage of hierarchy PSD blocks.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the moment block have dimension \(N_r\) and the localizing blocks dimensions \(N_1,\ldots,N_m\). Dense storage requires \[\Theta\!\left(N_r^2+\sum_{j=1}^mN_j^2\right)\] scalar words, even before solver workspaces and linear-system factors are included. Thus a machine budget of \(B\) scalar words cannot hold the assembled dense PSD blocks once \(N_r^2+\sum_jN_j^2>B\), up to fixed storage constants. Because \(N_r=\binom{n+r}{r}\), this boundary can be reached rapidly as either dimension or relaxation order increases.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dense hierarchy storage grows as the sum of squared PSD-block dimensions. Once that sum exceeds available scalar-word memory, the relaxation cannot be assembled densely.
knowledge_statements.title: Memory-Limiting Regimes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Quadratic dense-storage growth fits the memory-limiting regime container, but the precise threshold written with coefficient one depends on full versus packed storage and implementation constants. No source is supplied to fix the storage model or support the stated failure boundary.

assumptions_latex: The compact feasible set satisfies conditions under which the chosen Positivstellensatz is complete.
For every \(\varepsilon>0\), the polynomial \(f-(f^*-\varepsilon)\) has a valid certificate of total degree at most \(D(\varepsilon)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every level \(r\ge\lceil D(\varepsilon)/2\rceil\) satisfies \(0\le f^*-L_r\le\varepsilon\).

notation.meaning: degree bound for an epsilon-valid positivity certificate

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditional conversion of positivity-certificate degree bounds into hierarchy convergence rates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \(f-(f^*-\varepsilon)\) admits, for each \(\varepsilon>0\), a positivity certificate accepted by the hierarchy whose products and squares have degree at most \(D(\varepsilon)\). Any relaxation order \(r\) with \(2r\ge D(\varepsilon)\) contains that certificate in its dual cone. Weak duality then gives \(L_r\ge f^*-\varepsilon\), while validity of the relaxation gives \(L_r\le f^*\). Consequently \[0\le f^*-L_r\le\varepsilon\qquad\text{for all }r\ge\left\lceil D(\varepsilon)/2\right\rceil.\] Thus quantitative certificate-degree bounds induce convergence-order bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If an epsilon-accurate positivity certificate has degree D(epsilon), then hierarchy order ceil(D(epsilon)/2) suffices to achieve an epsilon-accurate lower bound.
knowledge_statements.title: Degree-Driven Rates

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The conditional transfer from an accepted degree-D(epsilon) positivity certificate to hierarchy order ceil(D(epsilon)/2) is coherent and the complexity-bound role fits degree-driven rates. Its validity depends on the precise hierarchy and certificate-degree convention, for which no inspectable source is supplied.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A clique family \((I_k)_{k=1}^m\) satisfies the running-intersection property if its members can be ordered so that for every \(k=2,\ldots,m\) there exists \(p(k)<k\) with \[I_k\cap\bigcup_{j<k}I_j\subseteq I_{p(k)}.\] Equivalently, the cliques admit a clique tree in which, for each variable index \(i\), the cliques containing \(i\) form a connected subtree.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Cliques satisfy running intersection when each new clique’s overlap with all earlier cliques lies inside one earlier parent clique.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider minimization of a polynomial over a basic closed semialgebraic set. Suppose its data decompose over cliques \((I_k)_{k=1}^m\), the cliques have running intersection, and the clique-wise quadratic modules satisfy a sparse Archimedean condition. knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize \(S_0\) from the polynomial supports and mandatory diagonal exponents. At iteration \(k\), form \(G(B,S_k)\), choose its prescribed chordal extension \(\widehat G_k\), and update \[S_{k+1}=S_k\cup\{\beta+\gamma:\{\beta,\gamma\}\in E(\widehat G_k)\}.\] Stop when \(S_{k+1}=S_k\), and output the maximal cliques of \(\widehat G_k\) as PSD-block index sets. Because \(S_k\subseteq B+B\) grows monotonically and \(B\) is finite, termination occurs in finitely many iterations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repeatedly chordalize the monomial support graph and add clique-generated exponent sums until the finite support stops changing.
knowledge_statements.title: Iterative Term-Sparsity Refinement

eq X_2,\qquad X_2
eq X_3,\qquad X_1
eq X_3\quad	ext{almost surely}.\] The first two relations force \(X_1=X_3\), contradicting the third. Thus overlap consistency alone does not guarantee a global representing measure.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Three pairwise binary laws can have matching one-variable marginals yet be globally incompatible when every pair is required to disagree.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an elimination ordering, when a vertex \(v\) is eliminated, all of its later neighbors are joined pairwise. The elimination clique at \(v\) is \[C_v=\{v\}\cup N_+(v),\] where \(N_+(v)\) denotes its later neighbors after fill. Hence fill-in can increase maximal-clique cardinalities and therefore the dimensions of clique-indexed PSD blocks.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Elimination adds edges among later neighbors; these fill edges create larger chordal cliques and can increase PSD block dimensions.

children.title: PSD Block Growth
children.top_down_role: Expansion of semidefinite blocks caused by enlarged maximal cliques.

assumptions_latex: \(G=(V,E)\) is replaced by a chordal extension whose largest maximal clique has cardinality \(q\).
The order-\(d\) local moment block uses all monomials of degree at most \(d\) in the clique variables.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(s(q,d)=\binom{q+d}{d}\), so growth of \(q\) directly enlarges the PSD blocks and can erase the computational advantage of sparsity.

notation.meaning: largest maximal-clique cardinality after chordal extension
dimension of a clique moment block

review_flags: Exact sparse moment-SOS source locator is missing.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quantifies loss of sparse-SDP savings through clique moment-block dimensions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let the largest maximal clique of a chordal extension contain \(q\) variables. At relaxation order \(d\), the associated moment matrix indexed by monomials of degree at most \(d\) has dimension
\[
s(q,d)=\binom{q+d}{d}.
\]
Its unrestricted symmetric PSD variable therefore has \(s(q,d)(s(q,d)+1)/2\) scalar entries. Consequently, fill-in that increases \(q\) increases both the PSD block dimension and its storage superlinearly; when \(q=n\), the largest sparse block has exactly the dimension of the corresponding dense order-\(d\) moment block.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A clique of size q produces an order-d PSD moment block of size binomial(q+d,d); if q reaches n, the sparse block becomes dense-sized.
knowledge_statements.title: PSD Block Growth

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The block-dimension formula and dense-size boundary fit the failure-boundary container, but no inspectable sparse moment–SOS source is supplied. The domains of q and d, and the qualification d>=1 for superlinear storage growth, should also be stated.

knowledge_statements.title: Elimination-Ordering Sensitivity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uses a star graph to exhibit sharp ordering-dependent fill-in.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(n\ge 2\) and consider the star graph \(K_{1,n}\), with one center and \(n\) leaves. Leaf-first elimination adds no fill and yields maximal clique cardinality \(2\). Center-first elimination connects every pair of leaves; together with the original center–leaf edges, the resulting chordal extension is \(K_{n+1}\) and has maximal clique cardinality \(n+1\). Thus elimination ordering can radically change fill and the largest PSD block size.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a star with n leaves, leaf-first elimination gives maximal cliques of size 2, whereas center-first elimination produces the complete graph on n+1 vertices.
assumptions_latex: \(n\ge 2\) is an integer.
A chordal extension is generated by eliminating vertices and connecting every pair of their remaining neighbors.

children.title: Sparsity-Loss Boundary
children.top_down_role: Regimes where chordal conversion no longer yields a useful size reduction.

assumptions_latex: The order-\(d\) sparse hierarchy uses clique moment matrices from a chordal extension with largest clique cardinality \(q_n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(q_n=\Theta(n)\), the largest sparse PSD block is asymptotically dense-scale, so structural sparsity alone gives no block-size separation.

notation.meaning: largest clique cardinality after chordal extension

review_flags: Exact sparse-hierarchy boundary source is missing.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Identifies linear clique growth as the dense-scale boundary for fixed-order blocks.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
At relaxation order \(d\), the largest clique moment block has dimension \(\binom{q_n+d}{d}\), whereas the dense moment block has dimension \(\binom{n+d}{d}\). If \(q_n=\Theta(n)\), then for fixed \(d\),
\[
\binom{q_n+d}{d}=\Theta\!\left(\binom{n+d}{d}\right).
\]
Hence the sparse formulation has no asymptotic separation in its largest PSD block dimension. In particular, a chordal extension containing an \(n\)-vertex clique reproduces the dense PSD constraint exactly.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When the largest chordal clique grows linearly with n, fixed-order sparse moment blocks have the same asymptotic size as dense blocks.
knowledge_statements.title: Sparsity-Loss Boundary

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The fixed-order asymptotic comparison is mathematically sound and correctly classified as a failure boundary, but the record supplies no inspectable source for the sparse-hierarchy interpretation.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Chordal PSD matrix completion applied to the specified entries of a partial moment matrix, without asserting completion of its full moment structure.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(M_G(y)\) be a partial real symmetric matrix formed from specified entries of a moment matrix. Suppose its specified-entry graph \(G\) is chordal and all repeated moment labels among the specified entries have consistent values. children.title: Clique-Based Conversion
children.top_down_role: Conversion of a global semidefinite representation into clique-indexed blocks.

knowledge_statements.title: Clique-Based Conversion
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conversion of a chordal PSD-completion constraint into coupled clique PSD constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C_1,\ldots,C_m\) be the maximal cliques of a chordal specified-entry graph. Replace the requirement that a global partial matrix admit a PSD completion by variables \(X_k\in\mathbb S_+^{|C_k|}\). For every nonempty overlap \(S=C_i\cap C_j\), impose \[ X_i[S,S]=X_j[S,S]. \] These equalities define one consistent value for every specified entry. Impose each original affine constraint on those induced specified-entry values. The resulting clique formulation has exactly the same feasible specified entries as the original PSD-completion formulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A chordal PSD-completion constraint is represented by PSD matrices on maximal cliques, equality of all shared entries, and the original affine constraints evaluated on the resulting global specified-entry values.
assumptions_latex: The specified-entry graph is chordal with maximal cliques \(C_1,\ldots,C_m\).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For clique-indexed symmetric matrices \(X_i\in\mathbb S^{|C_i|}\) and \(X_j\in\mathbb S^{|C_j|}\), define \(S_{ij}=C_i\cap C_j\). They are overlap-consistent when
\[
X_i[S_{ij},S_{ij}]=X_j[S_{ij},S_{ij}],
\]
with rows and columns identified by their global indices. Equivalently, every entry whose two global indices lie in both cliques has the same value in both local matrices. If the cliques form a clique tree, it suffices to impose this equality on the overlaps of adjacent cliques.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Clique matrices are overlap-consistent when all entries indexed by their intersection agree; on a clique tree, adjacent-overlap equalities suffice.

knowledge_statements.title: Global Completion Compatibility
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local-to-global compatibility under the chordal running-intersection property.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C_1,\ldots,C_m\) be the maximal cliques of a chordal graph, and let a clique tree satisfy the running-intersection property. Suppose \(X_k\in\mathbb S^{|C_k|}\) and, for every clique-tree edge \((i,j)\), the matrices agree on \(C_i\cap C_j\). Then there exists a unique global partial symmetric matrix whose principal submatrix on each \(C_k\) equals \(X_k\). If additionally \(X_k\succeq0\) for every \(k\), this partial matrix admits a global positive-semidefinite completion.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Running-intersection and adjacent-overlap consistency glue clique matrices into one global partial matrix; PSD clique blocks then guarantee a global PSD completion.
assumptions_latex: The maximal cliques \(C_1,\ldots,C_m\) admit a clique tree satisfying the running-intersection property.
The local matrices agree on the overlap associated with every clique-tree edge.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: There is a unique global partial symmetric matrix inducing all local clique matrices; if every local matrix is PSD, that partial matrix has a PSD completion.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(S=C_i\cap C_j\neq\varnothing\) and choose \(X_i\succeq0\) and \(X_j\succeq0\) such that
\[
X_i[S,S]\neq X_j[S,S].

If a global symmetric matrix \(X\) induced both local matrices, then its unique principal submatrix \(X[S,S]\) would have to equal both conflicting overlap blocks, which is impossible. Therefore clique-wise PSD constraints without overlap consistency are insufficient for global completion compatibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Two individually PSD clique matrices with conflicting values on their overlap cannot arise from any single global matrix.

assumptions_latex: \(\Gamma\) is a finite group with a unitary representation \(\rho\) on a finite-dimensional complex space.
The Hermitian matrix \(X\) satisfies \(\rho(g)^*X\rho(g)=X\) for every \(g\in\Gamma\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A symmetry-adapted unitary basis block-diagonalizes \(X\), and \(X\succeq0\) is equivalent to PSD constraints on the multiplicity blocks.
review_flags: A representation-theoretic source with the commutant decomposition is required.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-group commutant decomposition over complex Hermitian matrices.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Decompose the unitary representation as \(U^*\rho(g)U=\bigoplus_\alpha(\rho_\alpha(g)\otimes I_{m_\alpha})\), where \(\rho_\alpha\) are pairwise inequivalent irreducible representations of dimensions \(d_\alpha\). Every invariant Hermitian matrix has the form
\[
U^*XU=\bigoplus_\alpha(I_{d_\alpha}\otimes Y_\alpha),
\qquad Y_\alpha\in\mathbb H^{m_\alpha}.
\]
Moreover, \(X\succeq0\) if and only if \(Y_\alpha\succeq0\) for every \(\alpha\). Thus one invariant PSD constraint reduces to independent PSD constraints on multiplicity spaces.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite-group-invariant Hermitian matrix splits into repeated multiplicity blocks, and positivity is equivalent to positivity of those smaller blocks.
knowledge_statements.title: Group-Invariant Block Diagonalization

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The complex finite-group commutant decomposition is mathematically standard and correctly classified as a representation, but no representation-theoretic source or locator is supplied.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Entry-orbit parameterization of invariant matrix variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\Gamma\) act on \(I\), and let \(\mathcal O\) be the orbit partition of \(I\times I\) under \(g\cdot(i,j)=(gi,gj)\). A matrix \(X\) is \(\Gamma\)-invariant exactly when it is constant on every \(O\in\mathcal O\), equivalently
\[
X=\sum_{O\in\mathcal O}z_OB_O,
\]
where \((B_O)_{ij}=1\) precisely when \((i,j)\in O\). For a real symmetric variable, coefficients for transposed orbits are identified. This replaces entry variables by orbit coefficients while retaining the PSD constraint on the assembled matrix.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A group-invariant matrix is constant on pair orbits, so it can be parameterized by one coefficient per orbit, with transpose identifications for symmetry.

assumptions_latex: \(\Gamma\) is finite and acts unitarily on a finite-dimensional complex space.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reduction through irreducible types and their multiplicity spaces.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Write the representation space as the orthogonal sum of isotypic components
\[
V=\bigoplus_\alpha V_\alpha,
\qquad V_\alpha\cong W_\alpha\otimes M_\alpha,
\]
where the \(W_\alpha\) carry pairwise inequivalent irreducible representations. Any invariant Hermitian matrix preserves every \(V_\alpha\) and restricts there as \(I_{W_\alpha}\otimes Y_\alpha\) for a Hermitian operator \(Y_\alpha\) on \(M_\alpha\). Consequently, global positive semidefiniteness is equivalent to \(Y_\alpha\succeq0\) for all \(\alpha\), with no coupling between distinct isotypic components.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Decomposing into isotypic components turns an invariant PSD constraint into independent PSD constraints on irreducible multiplicity spaces.

knowledge_statements.title: Stabilizer-Aware Blocks
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Block diagonalization using the subgroup stabilizing the relaxation data.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H\) be a finite group with unitary representation \(\rho:H\to U(V)\), and let a Hermitian Gram matrix \(Q\) satisfy \(Q\rho(h)=\rho(h)Q\) for every \(h\in H\). knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A Gram matrix commuting with a finite stabilizer group decomposes into smaller multiplicity-space blocks, and it is positive semidefinite exactly when every reduced block is positive semidefinite.

knowledge_statements.title: Symmetry-Reduction Limits
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact invariant-variable restriction fails when the full optimization problem is not group invariant.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Exact averaging over a group requires invariance of the objective and every feasibility condition. For a concrete failure, let \(P\) swap the two coordinates and consider \[\min\{X_{22}:X\succeq0,\ X_{11}=1\}.\] The feasible matrix \(X=\operatorname{diag}(1,0)\) has value \(0\). Restricting to matrices invariant under \(X\mapsto PXP^{\mathsf T}\) imposes \(X_{11}=X_{22}\), so every invariant feasible matrix has objective value \(1\). Thus a noninvariant objective or constraint can make symmetry restriction change the optimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Restricting to invariant matrices is exact only for fully invariant problems; a two-coordinate example shows that missing invariance can increase the optimum from zero to one.

children.title: Quotient-Ring Reduction

knowledge_statements.title: Quotient-Ring Reduction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Polynomial SOS certificates represented modulo equality constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(I=\langle h_1,\ldots,h_s\rangle\subset\mathbb R[x]\) encode polynomial equalities and let \(A=\mathbb R[x]/I\). A polynomial \(f\) has a sum-of-squares certificate in the quotient ring precisely when there exist \(q_1,\ldots,q_r\in\mathbb R[x]\) such that \[[f]=\sum_{j=1}^r[q_j]^2\quad\text{in }A,\] equivalently \(f-\sum_jq_j^2\in I\). This certificate implies \(f(x)\ge0\) for every real point \(x\) satisfying \(h_i(x)=0\) for all \(i\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Equality constraints permit computations modulo their ideal; an SOS identity in the quotient is an ordinary SOS identity up to an ideal element and certifies nonnegativity on the equality variety.

\(f,q_1,\ldots,q_r\in\mathbb R[x]\).

knowledge_statements.title: Equality-Ideal Reduction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Truncated moment constraints induced by polynomial equalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix order \(d\) and a linear functional \(L:\mathbb R[x]_{\le2d}\to\mathbb R\). For equality generators \(h_i\), impose \(L(h_iq)=0\) for every polynomial \(q\) with \(\deg(h_iq)\le2d\). Then \(L(p)=L(r)\) whenever \(p-r\in I\) and both sides admit an equality-ideal representation within the truncation. Hence the moment and localizing equations depend only on the corresponding truncated residue classes, allowing redundant ideal directions to be removed from the semidefinite relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Vanishing moment equations for all admissible equality multiples make the truncated functional depend only on polynomial residue classes, permitting removal of equality-ideal directions.

children.title: Normal-Form Basis Compression
children.top_down_role: Reduced polynomial bases selected through normal forms modulo equations.

knowledge_statements.title: Normal-Form Basis Compression
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Gröbner normal forms compress quotient moment and Gram representations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input an equality ideal \(I\subseteq\mathbb R[x]\), a degree-compatible term order, a Gröbner basis \(G\) of \(I\), and a relaxation order \(d\in\mathbb N\). Form the standard-monomial list \(B_d\) consisting of monomials of degree at most \(d\) that are not divisible by any leading monomial of \(G\). For every product \(uv\) with \(u,v\in B_d\), compute the remainder \(\operatorname{NF}_G(uv)\). Assemble the moment or Gram coefficient maps using these remainders, solve the resulting compressed conic problem, and output its solution in the basis \(B_d\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Using a degree-compatible Gröbner basis, retain standard monomials through the relaxation degree, reduce their products to normal form, and build the moment or Gram relaxation in this compressed quotient basis.
assumptions_latex: \(I\subseteq\mathbb R[x]\) is an equality ideal.
\(G\) is a Gröbner basis of \(I\) for a degree-compatible term order.
\(d\in\mathbb N\), and all required product normal forms lie within the represented truncation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(B_d\) spans the quotient classes represented through degree \(d\), and their products are encoded by \(\operatorname{NF}_G(uv)\).

knowledge_statements.title: Nonradical-Ideal Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quotient reduction by a nonradical ideal retains nilpotent algebraic directions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(I=\langle x^2\rangle\subset\mathbb R[x]\), the real variety is \(V_{\mathbb R}(I)=\{0\}\), but the quotient \(\mathbb R[x]/I\) contains the nonzero nilpotent class \([x]\), with \([x]^2=0\). Its vanishing ideal is \(I(V_{\mathbb R}(I))=\langle x\rangle\), strictly larger than \(I\). Therefore quotienting by the supplied equality ideal preserves valid polynomial identities but need not produce the reduced coordinate ring of feasible points; dimension counts or point-extraction arguments that silently replace \(I\) by its real radical are not justified.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonradical equality ideal can retain nilpotent quotient directions absent from the real feasible set, so reduced-coordinate or point-extraction conclusions require a real-radical condition.
assumptions_latex: \(I=\langle x^2\rangle\subset\mathbb R[x]\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(I\subsetneq I(V_{\mathbb R}(I))\) and \([x]\ne0\) while \([x]^2=0\) in \(\mathbb R[x]/I\).

notation.meaning: ideal of polynomials vanishing on the real zero set
residue class of x modulo the equality ideal

knowledge_statements.title: Fixed-Basis DSOS
knowledge_statements.scope_note: DSOS polynomials defined through a diagonally dominant Gram matrix in a prescribed basis.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix a polynomial basis vector \(z(x)\). A polynomial \(p\) is diagonally-dominant-sum-of-squares in this basis if there exists a symmetric matrix \(Q\) such that \[p(x)=z(x)^{\mathsf T}Qz(x),\qquad Q_{ii}\ge\sum_{j\ne i}|Q_{ij}|\quad\text{for every }i.\] Introducing nonnegative variables that majorize \(|Q_{ij}|\) gives linear constraints, so membership in the fixed-basis DSOS cone is representable by a linear program. Diagonal dominance also implies \(Q\succeq0\), hence every fixed-basis DSOS polynomial is SOS.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A fixed-basis DSOS polynomial has a diagonally dominant Gram matrix. Its membership is LP-representable, and diagonal dominance ensures the polynomial is SOS.
assumptions_latex: \(z(x)\) is a fixed finite polynomial basis vector.
\(Q\) is real and symmetric.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Q\text{ diagonally dominant}\Rightarrow Q\succeq0\Rightarrow p\text{ is SOS}\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The fixed-basis DSOS definition, LP representability, and SOS implication are standard and correctly assigned to a definition container, but no primary source with a locator is supplied.

knowledge_statements.title: Basis-Updated DSOS
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Iterative DSOS inner approximations generated by congruence updates of the Gram basis.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize an invertible matrix \(U_0\). At iteration \(k\), solve the relaxation with every relevant Gram matrix constrained to \(P=U_k^{\mathsf T}Q U_k\), where \(Q\) is symmetric and diagonally dominant. Let \(P_k\) be an obtained positive-definite Gram matrix and choose an invertible factor \(U_{k+1}\) satisfying \(P_k=U_{k+1}^{\mathsf T}U_{k+1}\). Repeat until the objective improvement is below a prescribed tolerance, and output the last relaxation solution. Since the identity matrix is diagonally dominant, \(P_k\) remains feasible for the next Gram cone.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Solve successive DSOS relaxations, refactor the current Gram matrix as the next basis, and stop when improvement is small; the preceding Gram point remains feasible after each update.
assumptions_latex: \(U_0\) is invertible.
Each selected \(P_k\) is positive definite and admits an invertible factor.
Each subproblem is solved to the chosen optimization tolerance.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P_k=U_{k+1}^{\mathsf T}I U_{k+1}\) is feasible at iteration \(k+1\), so a minimization bound cannot worsen.

notation.meaning: diagonally dominant matrix in the transformed basis
Gram matrix selected at iteration k

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithmic role fits the leaf and the displayed feasibility-preserving update is coherent under the stated positive-definiteness assumptions. A primary source is required to establish that this is the intended basis-update variant and to support the monotonic-bound claim.

knowledge_statements.title: Fixed-Basis SDSOS
knowledge_statements.scope_note: SDSOS polynomials defined through a scaled diagonally dominant Gram matrix.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix a polynomial basis vector \(z(x)\). A polynomial \(p\) is scaled-diagonally-dominant-sum-of-squares in this basis if \[p(x)=z(x)^{\mathsf T}Qz(x)\] for some symmetric matrix \(Q\) admitting a positive diagonal matrix \(D\) such that \(DQD\) is diagonally dominant. Equivalently, \(Q\) is a sum of positive-semidefinite matrices supported on principal index sets of size at most two. Consequently, fixed-basis SDSOS membership has a second-order-cone representation and implies that \(p\) is SOS.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A fixed-basis SDSOS polynomial has a Gram matrix made diagonally dominant by positive diagonal scaling, equivalently a sum of two-index PSD blocks; membership is SOCP-representable.
assumptions_latex: \(z(x)\) is a fixed finite polynomial basis vector.
\(Q\) is real and symmetric.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Q\text{ scaled diagonally dominant}\Rightarrow Q\succeq0\Rightarrow p\text{ is SOS}\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard SDSOS and scaled-diagonal-dominance characterization

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The scaled-diagonal-dominance definition and two-index PSD-block characterization are mathematically appropriate, but the record lacks a primary SDSOS citation with a specific locator.

knowledge_statements.title: Basis-Updated SDSOS

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize an invertible matrix \(U_0\). At iteration \(k\), solve the relaxation with each relevant Gram matrix constrained to \(P=U_k^{\mathsf T}Q U_k\), where \(Q\) is scaled diagonally dominant. For an obtained positive-definite Gram matrix \(P_k\), choose an invertible factor \(U_{k+1}\) satisfying \(P_k=U_{k+1}^{\mathsf T}U_{k+1}\). Iterate until the objective improvement is below a prescribed tolerance, then output the last solution. Because the identity is scaled diagonally dominant, the preceding Gram point is feasible in the updated cone.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Successive SDSOS relaxations use a factor of the current Gram matrix as the next basis; this preserves the preceding point and yields nonworsening minimization bounds.
assumptions_latex: \(U_0\) is invertible.
Each selected \(P_k\) is positive definite and admits an invertible factor.
Each subproblem is solved to the chosen optimization tolerance.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P_k=U_{k+1}^{\mathsf T}I U_{k+1}\) is feasible at iteration \(k+1\), so a minimization bound cannot worsen.

knowledge_statements.title: Bounded-Degree SOS Surrogates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-order quadratic-module certificates for polynomial lower bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(m,s,d\in\mathbb N\), let \(g_1,\ldots,g_m,h_1,\ldots,h_s,f\in\mathbb R[x]\), let \(\gamma\in\mathbb R\), define \(K=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:g_j(x)\ge0\text{ for }j=1,\ldots,m,\ h_i(x)=0\text{ for }i=1,\ldots,s\}\), and let \(I=\langle h_1,\ldots,h_s\rangle\). A bounded-degree SOS certificate for \(f\ge\gamma\) on \(K\) consists of SOS polynomials \(\sigma_0,ldots,\sigma_m\) satisfying \[f-\gamma\equiv\sigma_0+\sum_{j=1}^m\sigma_jg_j\pmod I,\qquad \deg(\sigma_0)\le2d,\quad \deg(\sigma_jg_j)\le2d\text{ for }j=1,\ldots,m.\] Evaluating this identity on \(K\) gives \(f(x)\ge\gamma\) for every \(x\in K\), while fixed \(d\) yields a finite-dimensional semidefinite formulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At a fixed nonnegative integer order, an SOS-weighted combination of the indexed inequalities, modulo the indexed equality constraints, certifies the real lower bound gamma and gives a finite semidefinite relaxation.
assumptions_latex: \(m,s,d\in\mathbb N\).
\(g_1,\ldots,g_m,h_1,\ldots,h_s,f\in\mathbb R[x]\) and \(\gamma\in\mathbb R\).
Each \(\sigma_j\) is a sum of squares, and the displayed degree bounds hold.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f(x)\ge\gamma\text{ for every }x\in K\).

children.title: Block Factor-Width Surrogates
children.top_down_role: Cone approximations structured by blockwise factor-width restrictions.

knowledge_statements.title: Block Factor-Width Surrogates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: PSD inner approximations assembled from bounded-size principal blocks.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(n\in\mathbb N\) and \(1\le k\le n\), define the factor-width-\(k\) cone by \[\operatorname{FW}_k^n=\left\{Q\in\mathbb S^n:Q=\sum_{\substack{C\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}\\1\le |C|\le k}}E_C^{\mathsf T}Q_CE_C,\quad Q_C\succeq0\right\},\] where \(E_C\in\mathbb R^{|C|\times n}\) extracts the coordinates indexed by \(C\), and \(Q_C\in\mathbb S^{|C|}\). Every such \(Q\) is positive semidefinite, and \[\operatorname{FW}_1^n\subseteq\operatorname{FW}_2^n\subseteq\cdots\subseteq\operatorname{FW}_n^n=\mathbb S_+^n.\] Thus replacing a Gram constraint by membership in \(\operatorname{FW}_k^n\) gives an inner surrogate using positive-semidefinite blocks of size at most \(k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A factor-width surrogate writes a Gram matrix as a sum of positive-semidefinite matrices supported on coordinate blocks of bounded size; increasing the block size enlarges the cone up to the full positive-semidefinite cone.
assumptions_latex: \(n\in\mathbb N\) and \(1\le k\le n\).
For each nonempty \(C\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}\), \(E_C\in\mathbb R^{|C|\times n}\) is its coordinate-extraction matrix.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{FW}_k^n\subseteq\mathbb S_+^n\) and, for \(k<n\), \(\operatorname{FW}_k^n\subseteq\operatorname{FW}_{k+1}^n\).

notation.meaning: factor-width-k cone in the symmetric n-by-n matrices
coordinate-extraction matrix for index set C

knowledge_statements.title: Surrogate-Strength Ordering
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Ordering of valid lower bounds produced by nested inner SOS-cone surrogates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:g_j(x)\geq0,\ j=1,\ldots,s\}\). For \(r=1,\ldots,m\), define \(\gamma_r=\sup\{\gamma\in\mathbb R:f-\gamma=\sigma_0+\sum_{j=1}^s\sigma_jg_j,\ \sigma_j\in K_r\}\), and define \(\gamma_{\mathrm{SOS}}\) by replacing \(K_r\) with \(\Sigma_{n,2d}\). Then \(\gamma_1\leq\cdots\leq\gamma_m\leq\gamma_{\mathrm{SOS}}\leq f^*\), where \(f^*=\inf_{x\in S}f(x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nested inner SOS surrogates produce monotonically stronger valid lower bounds, none exceeding the full SOS bound or the true infimum.
assumptions_latex: \(K_1\subseteq\cdots\subseteq K_m\subseteq\Sigma_{n,2d}\), and every polynomial in each \(K_r\) is globally nonnegative.
\(f,g_1,\ldots,g_s\in\mathbb R[x]\), all certificate products are degree-compatible, \(S\neq\varnothing\), and the displayed suprema are finite and have nonempty feasible sets.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\gamma_1\leq\cdots\leq\gamma_m\leq\gamma_{\mathrm{SOS}}\leq f^*\).

knowledge_statements.title: Scalability–Accuracy Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Factor-width hierarchy and the explicit block dimensions of its direct extended formulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \(\mathrm{FW}_k^N=\{Q\in\mathbb S^N:Q=\sum_{|I|=k}E_I^{\mathsf T}X_IE_I,\ X_I\in\mathbb S_+^k\}\). Then \(\mathrm{FW}_2^N\subseteq\cdots\subseteq\mathrm{FW}_N^N=\mathbb S_+^N\). The direct formulation at level \(k\) uses \(\binom Nk\) positive-semidefinite blocks of order \(k\), with \(\binom Nk k(k+1)/2\) scalar block entries before coupling equations. Thus strength is monotone in \(k\), whereas this raw lifted-size count is governed by \(\binom Nk\) and need not be monotone.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Larger factor width gives a stronger cone and full width recovers the PSD cone; the direct formulation has binomial(N,k) PSD blocks of order k, so its raw lifted size is not monotone in k.
assumptions_latex: \(N\geq k\geq2\), and \(E_I\in\mathbb R^{k\times N}\) selects the coordinates indexed by \(I\subseteq\{1,\ldots,N\}\), where \(|I|=k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathrm{FW}_2^N\subseteq\cdots\subseteq\mathrm{FW}_N^N=\mathbb S_+^N\), and the direct level-\(k\) formulation uses \(\binom Nk\) PSD blocks of order \(k\).

knowledge_statements.title: Basis Dependence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Concrete basis dependence of a diagonally-dominant Gram surrogate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(p(x)=(x_1+2x_2)^2\). knowledge_statements.title: Strict Inner-Approximation Gaps
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Explicit witnesses for strict gaps among standard Gram-matrix inner approximations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(n\geq3\), let \(A_n=\operatorname{diag}(A,I_{n-2})\), where \(A=\begin{pmatrix}1&2\\2&4\end{pmatrix}\), and let \(B_n=\operatorname{diag}(J_3,I_{n-3})\), where \(J_3=\mathbf1\mathbf1^{\mathsf T}\). Then \(A_n\in\mathrm{SDD}_n\setminus\mathrm{DD}_n\) and \(B_n\in\mathbb S_+^n\setminus\mathrm{SDD}_n\). Consequently, \(\mathrm{DD}_n\subsetneq\mathrm{SDD}_n\subsetneq\mathbb S_+^n\) for every \(n\geq3\).

knowledge_statements.title: Scaling Sensitivity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sensitivity of Gram-cone surrogates to positive diagonal basis scaling.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Q=\begin{pmatrix}1&1/2\\1/2&1\end{pmatrix}\) and \(D=\operatorname{diag}(1,3)\). Then \(Q\in\mathrm{DD}_2\) but \(DQD\notin\mathrm{DD}_2\), so diagonal dominance is not invariant under positive diagonal congruence. By contrast, for every symmetric \(Q\) and invertible positive diagonal \(D\), \(Q\in\mathrm{SDD}_n\) if and only if \(DQD\in\mathrm{SDD}_n\). Hence diagonal rescaling of basis elements can change DSOS membership, while SDSOS membership is preserved.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Positive diagonal basis scaling can change diagonal-dominance membership but preserves scaled-diagonal-dominance membership.
assumptions_latex: DSOS and SDSOS Gram surrogates use diagonal dominance and scaled diagonal dominance, respectively.
\(D\) is an invertible positive diagonal matrix, and the corresponding basis change transforms the Gram matrix by positive diagonal congruence or its inverse.

knowledge_statements.title: Monomial Basis Selection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Total-degree monomial Gram representation and the effect of restricting the selected monomial span.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(z_d(x)=(x^\alpha)_{|\alpha|\leq d}\in\mathbb R^N\), where \(N=\binom{n+d}{d}\). A polynomial \(p\in\mathbb R[x_1,\ldots,x_n]\) of degree at most \(2d\) is a sum of squares of polynomials of degree at most \(d\) if and only if there exists \(Q\in\mathbb S_+^N\) such that \(p(x)=z_d(x)^{\mathsf T}Qz_d(x)\) identically. For a selected monomial subvector \(w\), the restricted representation \(p=w^{\mathsf T}Q_ww\), \(Q_w\succeq0\), is exact precisely for polynomials admitting an SOS decomposition whose squared summands lie in \(\operatorname{span}(w)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A polynomial of degree at most 2d is SOS exactly when it has a PSD Gram representation over all monomials of degree at most d; restricting the monomials restricts the allowed squared summands.
assumptions_latex: \(p\in\mathbb R[x_1,\ldots,x_n]\) has degree at most \(2d\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(p\) is SOS if and only if \(p=z_d^{\mathsf T}Qz_d\) for some \(Q\succeq0\).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \(\phi_d=Tz_d\) with \(T\) invertible. Every Gram representation \(p=z_d^{\mathsf T}Qz_d\) induces \(p=\phi_d^{\mathsf T}\widetilde Q\phi_d\), where \(\widetilde Q=T^{-\mathsf T}QT^{-1}\). Congruence gives \(Q\succeq0\) if and only if \(\widetilde Q\succeq0\), so the exact SOS cone is basis invariant. If \(\phi_d\) is orthonormal for an inner product \(\langle u,v\rangle_\mu=\int u(x)v(x)\,d\mu(x)\), then its basis moment matrix satisfies \(\int\phi_d\phi_d^{\mathsf T}\,d\mu=I\), which can improve coefficient scaling without changing exact SOS feasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An invertible orthogonal-basis change transforms Gram matrices by congruence, preserving exact SOS membership while potentially improving numerical scaling.

knowledge_statements.title: Variable Scaling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Affine variable normalization before constructing and solving a polynomial relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Choose an invertible diagonal \(D\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) and \(c\in\mathbb R^n\), set \(x=Dy+c\), and define \(\widehat f(y)=f(Dy+c)\) and \(\widehat g_j(y)=g_j(Dy+c)\). Construct and solve the relaxation in the \(y\)-coordinates. Given a certificate \(\widehat f-\gamma=\widehat\sigma_0+\sum_{j=1}^s\widehat\sigma_j\widehat g_j\), return \(\sigma_j(x)=\widehat\sigma_j(D^{-1}(x-c))\). This substitution bijectively preserves polynomial identities, SOS membership, and the feasible sets defined by the transformed inequalities.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a finite family \(a_i(x)\leq b_i\) indexed by \(I\), an initial subset \(I_0\subseteq I\), and tolerance \(\varepsilon\geq0\). At iteration \(t\), solve the conic master problem containing constraints in \(I_t\), obtaining \(x_t\). Compute \(i_t\in\arg\max_{i\in I\setminus I_t}v_i(x_t)\), where \(v_i(x)=a_i(x)-b_i\). If no omitted constraint exists or \(v_{i_t}(x_t)\leq\varepsilon\), return \(x_t\); otherwise set \(I_{t+1}=I_t\cup\{i_t\}\). The method terminates after at most \(|I\setminus I_0|+1\) master solves and returns a point satisfying every indexed inequality within \(\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repeatedly solve the current relaxation and add a most-violated omitted constraint; finite termination yields feasibility within the chosen tolerance.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: To test \(c^{\mathsf T}x\leq\delta\), consider \(\sup\{c^{\mathsf T}x-\delta:x\in K,\ Ax=b,\ Cx\leq d\}\). A verifiable redundancy certificate is a pair \((y,\lambda)\) satisfying \(\lambda\geq0\), \(A^{\mathsf T}y+C^{\mathsf T}\lambda-c\in K^*\), and \(b^{\mathsf T}y+d^{\mathsf T}\lambda-\delta\leq0\). Indeed, weak conic duality then bounds the supremum by a nonpositive number, so every \(x\in F\) satisfies the candidate inequality. Strict negativity certifies slack redundancy. Failure to find such a pair does not establish nonredundancy without an appropriate strong-duality or exact primal maximization condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nonnegative inequality multipliers and a dual-cone slack can certify that an added inequality is implied by the existing conic system.

knowledge_statements.title: Constraint Screening
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Safe screening rule for affine constraints in a semidefinite relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a relaxation region \(R\), candidate inequalities \(a_i(X)\le b_i\), and certified bounds \(U_i\ge \sup_{X\in R}(a_i(X)-b_i)\), initialize the retained set as \(I=\varnothing\). For each \(i\), discard the constraint when \(U_i\le 0\), and otherwise add \(i\) to \(I\). Output the formulation containing precisely the constraints indexed by \(I\). Every discarded inequality is valid throughout \(R\), so its removal leaves the feasible set unchanged. An uncertified numerical estimate of \(U_i\) is insufficient for safe screening.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Discard a constraint only when a certified bound proves that its violation is nonpositive throughout the current relaxation region.
assumptions_latex: \(R\) is the feasible region before the candidate inequalities are imposed.
Each \(U_i\) is a rigorous upper bound.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(R\cap\bigcap_i\{X:a_i(X)\le b_i\}=R\cap\bigcap_{i\in I}\{X:a_i(X)\le b_i\}\).

knowledge_statements.title: Active-Constraint Retention
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Tolerance-based retention predicate for previously generated affine constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X_k\) be the current relaxation solution and let \(s_i(X)=b_i-a_i(X)\) be the slack of a generated inequality \(a_i(X)\le b_i\). For a prescribed activity tolerance \(\tau_k\ge 0\), define the retained active set by \[I_k^{\mathrm{act}}=\{i:s_i(X_k)\le \tau_k\}.\] Constraints in \(I_k^{\mathrm{act}}\) are retained at the next iteration. knowledge_statements.title: Formulation-Growth Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dense size boundary for order-d polynomial moment relaxations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For polynomials in \(n\) variables and relaxation order \(d\), the monomial vector of degree at most \(d\) has size \(s(n,d)=\binom{n+d}{d}\). Consequently, a dense moment relaxation contains a positive-semidefinite moment matrix of order \(s(n,d)\), with \(s(n,d)(s(n,d)+1)/2\) distinct scalar entries. Thus fixed \(d\) gives \(s(n,d)=O(n^d)\), whereas fixed \(n\) gives \(s(n,d)=O(d^n)\). Any additional localizing matrices and generated constraints increase this baseline formulation size.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A dense order-d moment matrix has binomial dimension, producing quadratic growth in its distinct scalar matrix entries.
assumptions_latex: The relaxation uses the full monomial basis through degree \(d\).
No sparsity or symmetry reduction is applied.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(s(n,d)=\binom{n+d}{d}\) and the principal PSD block has \(s(n,d)(s(n,d)+1)/2\) distinct entries.

knowledge_statements.title: Adaptive Relaxation-Order Selection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sequential order selection for a nested polynomial moment-SOS hierarchy.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Choose an initial admissible order \(d_0\), a maximum order \(d_{\max}\), and certification tolerances. For \(d=d_0,d_0+1,\ldots,d_{\max}\), construct and solve the order-\(d\) relaxation, obtaining bound \(L_d\) and moment data \(y^{(d)}\). Stop and output \(d\) when either a rigorously validated primal value \(U_d\) satisfies \(U_d-L_d\le\varepsilon\), or an applicable exactness certificate, such as a verified flat-extension condition, holds. Otherwise increase \(d\). If no test succeeds by \(d_{\max}\), output an uncertified boundary status rather than claiming exactness.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Increase relaxation order until a verified objective gap or exactness certificate meets the stopping rule; otherwise report the imposed order limit.
assumptions_latex: The relaxations are nested and each selected order is well defined.
Reported stopping certificates are independently verified.

knowledge_statements.title: Exact Certificate Reconstruction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Rational reconstruction of an approximate Gram-matrix SOS certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given approximate symmetric Gram matrices \(Q_j\), rational polynomial data, and coefficient maps \(\mathcal A_j\), choose rational approximants \(\widehat Q_j\), then project them onto the rational affine space satisfying \[\sum_j\mathcal A_j(\widehat Q_j)=b.\] Verify this identity by exact rational arithmetic and verify \(\widehat Q_j\succeq0\) using an exact rational factorization or exact principal-minor test. Output the reconstructed matrices only if both checks pass; otherwise refine the approximants or return reconstruction failure. A passing output is an exact, finitely checkable polynomial certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Rationalize approximate Gram matrices, enforce coefficient identities exactly, and accept only after exact positive-semidefiniteness verification.
assumptions_latex: All target polynomial coefficients are rational.
The Gram coefficient maps \(\mathcal A_j\) are rational linear maps.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Acceptance implies \(\sum_j\mathcal A_j(\widehat Q_j)=b\) and \(\widehat Q_j\succeq0\) for every \(j\).

children.title: Polynomial-Identity Residuals
children.top_down_role: Residual assessment for reconstructed polynomial certificate identities.

knowledge_statements.title: Polynomial-Identity Residuals
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coefficientwise residual for a proposed polynomial certificate identity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(p,q_1,\ldots,q_m\in\mathbb R[x]_{\le D}\), where \(q_j\) are the polynomial terms reconstructed from a proposed certificate. The polynomial-identity residual is \[r(x)=p(x)-\sum_{j=1}^m q_j(x)=\sum_{|\alpha|\le D}r_\alpha x^\alpha.\] Its coefficientwise diagnostic is \(\rho_{\infty}=\max_{|\alpha|\le D}|r_\alpha|\). The identity is exact precisely when every \(r_\alpha=0\); under tolerance \(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{id}}\), it is numerically accepted when \(\rho_{\infty}\le\varepsilon_{\mathrm{id}}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Subtract the proposed certificate polynomial from the target and measure the largest absolute coefficient discrepancy.
assumptions_latex: The target and reconstructed terms use a common monomial basis through degree \(D\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(p=\sum_jq_j\iff\rho_\infty=0\).

knowledge_statements.title: Semidefinite Feasibility Checks
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Spectral acceptance condition for symmetric matrix blocks.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each symmetric certificate block \(Q_j\in\mathbb S^{n_j}\), define its semidefinite violation by \(v_j^{\mathrm{psd}}=\max\{0,-\lambda_{\min}(Q_j)\}\). Given tolerance \(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{psd}}\ge0\), the proposed certificate passes the numerical semidefinite-feasibility check exactly when \[\max_j v_j^{\mathrm{psd}}\le\varepsilon_{\mathrm{psd}}.\] At zero tolerance this is equivalent to \(Q_j\succeq0\) for all \(j\). With positive tolerance, passing certifies only membership in an enlarged spectral neighborhood unless rounding error is enclosed rigorously.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Measure each matrix block's negative minimum eigenvalue and accept only when the worst violation is within tolerance.
assumptions_latex: Every checked block is represented by a real symmetric matrix.
Eigenvalue error is controlled when a rigorous conclusion is required.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{psd}}=0\) implies passage exactly when \(Q_j\succeq0\) for every \(j\).

knowledge_statements.title: Constraint-Feasibility Checks
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Residual-based feasibility test for affine equalities and inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a candidate matrix tuple \(X\), affine equalities \(A_i(X)=b_i\), and affine inequalities \(C_k(X)\le d_k\), define \[v_{\mathrm{eq}}(X)=\max_i|A_i(X)-b_i|,\qquad v_{\mathrm{ineq}}(X)=\max_k\max\{0,C_k(X)-d_k\}.\] Given nonnegative tolerances \(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{eq}}\) and \(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{ineq}}\), the tuple passes the constraint-feasibility check exactly when both corresponding violations do not exceed their tolerances. Zero tolerances recover exact affine feasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Compute worst equality and inequality residuals and compare each with its declared feasibility tolerance.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(X\) passes iff \(v_{\mathrm{eq}}(X)\le\varepsilon_{\mathrm{eq}}\) and \(v_{\mathrm{ineq}}(X)\le\varepsilon_{\mathrm{ineq}}\).

children.title: Tolerance-Sensitivity Regimes

knowledge_statements.title: Tolerance-Sensitivity Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Three-way stability boundary for residual and eigenvalue feasibility decisions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let a scalar diagnostic \(z\) be accepted when \(z\le\tau\), and suppose the computed value \(\widehat z\) has certified error \(|z-\widehat z|\le\delta\). If \(\widehat z+\delta\le\tau\), acceptance is certified; if \(\widehat z-\delta>\tau\), rejection is certified; and if \([\widehat z-\delta,\widehat z+\delta]\) intersects \(\tau\), the decision is tolerance-sensitive and must be reported as ambiguous. The same rule applies to residual norms and to \(z=-\lambda_{\min}(Q)\) for semidefinite feasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasibility decision is stable only when the diagnostic's certified error interval lies wholly on one side of the tolerance.
assumptions_latex: \(\delta\ge0\) is a rigorous absolute error bound.
Acceptance is defined by \(z\le\tau\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Intersection of \([\widehat z-\delta,\widehat z+\delta]\) with \(\tau\) is the ambiguity boundary.

knowledge_statements.title: Numerical-Rank Estimation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Spectral numerical rank of a symmetric positive-semidefinite matrix.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(M\in\mathbb S_+^n\) have eigenvalues \(\lambda_1(M)\ge\cdots\ge\lambda_n(M)\ge0\). For absolute threshold \(\tau\ge0\), define \[\operatorname{rank}_{\tau}(M)=\#\{i:\lambda_i(M)>\tau\}.\] For a relative threshold \(\eta\ge0\) and \(\lambda_1(M)>0\), use \(\tau=\eta\lambda_1(M)\). The selected threshold and scaling convention are part of the estimate; numerical rank is not an intrinsic rank certificate unless spectral errors and eigenvalue separation are controlled.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Numerical rank counts eigenvalues exceeding a declared absolute or relative threshold.
assumptions_latex: \(M\) is real symmetric and positive semidefinite.
The eigenvalues are ordered nonincreasingly.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{rank}_{\tau}(M)=\#\{i:\lambda_i(M)>\tau\}\).

knowledge_statements.title: Near-Flatness Detection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Tolerance-based approximate flat-extension diagnostic for moment matrices.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(M_d(y)\) be an order-\(d\) moment matrix and let \(M_{d-r}(y)\) be the principal truncation required by the relevant flat-extension theorem, where \(r\) is determined by the constraint degrees. For threshold \(\tau\), declare numerical near-flatness when \[\operatorname{rank}_{\tau}M_d(y)=\operatorname{rank}_{\tau}M_{d-r}(y).\] This is a diagnostic rather than an exact certificate: extraction or exactness may be asserted only after verifying the theorem's positivity, localizing, and exact-rank hypotheses, or after exact reconstruction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Near-flatness means the thresholded ranks of a moment matrix and its required truncation agree, but this alone is not exactness.

\(d\ge r\) and both ranks use the same threshold convention.

children.title: Threshold Sensitivity

knowledge_statements.title: Threshold Sensitivity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Piecewise-constant dependence of numerical rank on its eigenvalue threshold.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(M\in\mathbb S_+^n\), the function \(r(\tau)=\operatorname{rank}_{\tau}(M)\) is nonincreasing and piecewise constant for \(\tau\ge0\). It can change only when \(\tau\) crosses an eigenvalue of \(M\). More precisely, for \(0\le\tau_1<\tau_2\), \[r(\tau_1)-r(\tau_2)=\#\{i:\tau_1<\lambda_i(M)\le\tau_2\}.\] Hence a rank or near-flatness decision is threshold-stable on an interval containing no relevant eigenvalue and is sensitive when the interval crosses one.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Thresholded rank decreases only when the threshold crosses eigenvalues; rank decisions are stable between successive eigenvalues.
assumptions_latex: \(M\) is real symmetric and positive semidefinite.
Numerical rank counts eigenvalues strictly greater than the threshold.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(r(\tau_1)-r(\tau_2)=\#\{i:\tau_1<\lambda_i(M)\le\tau_2\}\).

children.title: Ambiguous-Rank Boundary
children.top_down_role: Spectral regimes where numerical rank cannot be assigned reliably.

assumptions_latex: \(X\in\mathbb S_+^n\) is the computed semidefinite matrix.
The unknown exact matrix \(X_\star\in\mathbb S_+^n\) satisfies \(\|X-X_\star\|_2\leq\varepsilon\).
The numerical-rank threshold satisfies \(\tau>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{rank}_\tau(X_\star)\) is not robustly determined by \(X\) whenever \(\sigma(X)\cap[\tau-\varepsilon,\tau+\varepsilon]\neq\varnothing\).

notation.meaning: Thresholded numerical rank of a positive semidefinite matrix.
Spectral-norm uncertainty radius for the computed matrix.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Spectral-norm uncertainty boundary for threshold-based numerical-rank diagnostics of positive semidefinite relaxation solutions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define the ambiguous-rank boundary by \[\mathcal A_{\tau,\varepsilon}:=\{X\in\mathbb S_+^n:\min_i|\lambda_i(X)-\tau|\leq\varepsilon\}.\] If \(X\in\mathcal A_{\tau,\varepsilon}\), then some admissible perturbation \(E\in\mathbb S^n\) with \(\|E\|_2\leq\varepsilon\) can move an eigenvalue of \(X\) across the threshold \(\tau\); consequently, the value of \(\operatorname{rank}_\tau(X+E)\) is not invariant over the uncertainty set. If \(X\notin\mathcal A_{\tau,\varepsilon}\), every such perturbation that preserves positive semidefiniteness leaves \(\operatorname{rank}_\tau(X+E)=\operatorname{rank}_\tau(X)\). Thus membership in \(\mathcal A_{\tau,\varepsilon}\) marks the failure boundary for a threshold-based rank certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Rank is diagnostically ambiguous when an eigenvalue lies within the perturbation radius of the chosen threshold; outside this band, every admissible perturbation preserves the thresholded rank.
knowledge_statements.title: Ambiguous-Rank Boundary

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure_boundary kind fits the leaf, but no cited source supports the perturbation formulation. With rank defined using λ>τ, the closed symmetric band is not exact: an eigenvalue at τ−ε cannot be moved above τ by a perturbation of norm at most ε, whereas one at τ+ε can be moved to τ. The statement also alternates between unrestricted symmetric perturbations and PSD-preserving perturbations, and the conclusion about rankτ(X⋆) does not precisely express nonuniqueness over all compatible exact matrices. A sourced formulation must fix the endpoint convention, require ε>0, and use one consistent uncertainty set.
